Golden and Diamond Jubilees . . .

Compiled by Vonnie Stotz

BOWDLE GOLDEN JUBILEE

It was hot, hot, hot, but nothing dampened the spirit of the Bowdle Booster
trips scheduled a week before the Golden (50th) Jubilee held in Bowdle June
24 and 25, 1936. A caravan of Sunbonnet girls, the German and City bands
and other fun loving citizens took over Bowdle to inform them of the
celebration.

They visited the towns of Hosmer, Hillsview, Eureka, Herreid, Mound City,
Mobridge, Selby and Java. Selby entertained them to a Free Day on June 17.
The next day the "Belles of the Nineties" and "The Whisker Club" went to
Aberdeen to be part of the American Legion Downtown Frolic Parade.

When the boosters arrived about a mile from Ipswich they stopped and donned
their hoops and skirts and the men dressed in their odd clothing to make
themselves stand out in the crowd. A passerby noticed the "dressing up",
contacted the sheriff and reported a band of Gypsies were coming to town.
The so-called "Gypsies" told the sheriff their story and convinced him of
their good intentions and journeyed on their way.

The first day events began with 6,000 people braving the 100 degree heat.
The highlight was the arrival of the special train from Aberdeen with the
American Drum and Bugle Corps., mounted patrol, Hub City Band and 200
boosters. The morning parade was postponed to the afternoon so this group
could take part. Mayor Kruger welcomed everyone.

Winners for the floats were R. de Malignon, the Bowdle Implement and Mike
Hoerner. (Those donkey leading whisker clad pioneers.) Also in the parade
were Bowdle's famous babies, the Wagner Triplets. In the juvenile section
each entrant shared a money prize. Sharing honors with the Bowdle Band were
the Hub City Band, Hoven, Hosmer and Dutch Bands.

Thursday Bowdle, Hosmer, Eureka and the Dutch Bands kept the air filled
with music and toe tapping as they presented their favorite pieces. Sports
events held in the afternoon were a baseball game between two neighboring
towns and a Donkey Ball Game. Novelty races such as potato foot races, pop
drinking and pillow fights were held. Horseshoe games were played
throughout the day. The evening events featured an Oldtimers Band and a
popular Orchestra for the big Bowery Dance.

The second day greeted the 8,000 people with 110 degree temperatures. The
main event of the day was the 19 rounds of boxing. The main boxing event
was a 6-round bout between Ervin Kunz of Minneapolis and Blackie Zerr of
Aberdeen. Others were semifinals with Gust Kundert of Java and George
Mastell of Trail City; Percy Schlepp and Harold Pfitzer, both of Java;
Albert Gese of Bowdle and Emil Wolff of Java and Lawrence Gese of Bowdle
and Howard Kunz of Java.

More sports events including baseball games and donkey ball games, novelty
races and cigar smoking contests were held during the day and evening.

A Kiddies Parade started the day off with dressed up doll buggies, bicycles
and party dresses. The evening concluded again with Bowery Dances and
Oldtime Dances.

Main speaker for the day was Judge J.W. McCarter. Parts of his speech
follow: "The plat of Bowdle was dated June 25, 1886 and filed July 14,
1886 by Joseph C. Lawler. The surveyor was J.C. Turk. The right-of-way of
the Chicago, Milwaukee and St. Paul Railroad Company at Bowdle was filed by
Joseph C. Lawler June 25, 1887. J.W. Parmley was Register of Deeds.

"South Dakota was then a Territory and became a State Nov. 2, 1889. From
June 25, 1886 for the next 10 years Bowdle and vicinity rapidly became
settled. Pioneers were local captains of industry who took a chance in a
new country. By 1900 the townships tributary to Bowdle were well settled.
Those early settlers were an honorable and religious people. They worked
hard. They earned what they got. They were not worshippers of dollars or
searchers for luxury."

BOWDLE DIAMOND JUBILEE

Running the Bowdle Diamond (75th) Jubilee celebration with military
precision was Gardner Gross, retired regular army colonel. He was assisted
by co-chairmen Hekner Leno and Ray Kurle. This two-day event started June
21, on a cool, cloudy day.

Prior to the big days, booster trips were planned and carried out to the
surrounding towns under the chairmanship of Milford Hartzell. Letters of
congratulations and greetings came from the President of the United States
(John F. Kennedy) plus state dignitaries and former Bowdle citizens who
could not attend.

The first day began with registration, followed by the Kiddies Parade.
Sweepstake winners at this event were Mark and Candice Bieber with a pony
cart. First place winners in categories were: Humorous, Jane Dewald; S.D.
Centennial Theme, Kathy Thurn; Original, Ernestine and Eileen Hoffman; 75th
Jubilee Theme, Candice and Mark Bieber; Bike, Kendall Aldinger.

A free Stage Show was held in the afternoon and evening of the first day.
Street sports, under the direction of Edmund Dewald, including tug-of-war,
races, etc., followed by a baseball game with the American Legion Jr. team,
coached by Ozzie Schlepp. The Bowdle High School band presented a concert
under the direction of Mr. Norman Olson. Dances for young and old concluded
the first day events.

Thursday, June 22, began with an Oldtimers Breakfast honoring King Charles
Commet and Queen Magdalena Gross. Master of Ceremonies was Henry Gross.
Approximately 250 attended.

Chairman of the Main Parade was Gardner Gross with Rueben Schumacher,
Gordon Stotz and Dwight Commet keeping the parade running smoothly to avoid
bottlenecks. The parade consisted of 50 floats with 50-60 vehicles (old and
new) and 80 men and women on horseback. Six bands from the Bowdle area
marched in the parade.

Thousands of people watched as St. Augustine's Catholic Church captured the
overall float sweepstakes. Category first place winners were Commercial,
Bowdle State Bank; Civic, Bowdle Mothers' Club; Individual, James (Mickey)
Brown and Albert Perman; Religious, Seventh-day Adventist Church; 4-H and
Extension, ABC Extension Club; Historical, Joe Herman in a covered wagon;
Bands, Gettysburg High School. Others honored during the parade were
Bowdle's first baby, Carl Haupt and Bowdle's oldest area farmer, Joseph
Stangl Sr.

Chairman Mike Mitzel, along with his co-workers, fed about 4,000 people at a
free barbecue in Meakins Park. Featured speaker for this event was former
Bowdle native, W.J. Klein. A Horse Show followed, hosted by Circle S Saddle
Club of Selby. Ribbons were awarded in all events.

Entertainment for the evening was the judging of whiskers and costumes. Top
honors in the beard contest went to Mike Hoerner, who also won it for the
50th. Mike was hospitalized at the time due to an automobile accident. Mrs.
Leo Reede of California copped first prize in the traditional costume
category. In the ladies and children's division were Mrs. Helmuth
Eisenbeisz and daughters taking sweepstakes honors. Dave Dedrick of KELO-TV
in Sioux Falls was Master of Ceremonies.

        Queen Magdalena Gross and King Charles Commet

The highlight for most of the people attending was the Class Reunion held
at the Bowdle School. Co-chairmen were Lorraine Kurle and Alma Leno. Over
400 classmates met to reminisce about their school days, favorite teachers
and mischief they got into and away with. Little did any of them know that
this would be the last class reunion held in good old Bowdle High. The next
reunion was held in the new school and gym in 1977 when the Bowdle
All-School Reunion was held. In 1976 the old Bowdle High was condemned,
torn down and replaced.

The Diamond Jubilee Historical Book chairperson was Mrs. Vincent Hoven,
assisted by Mrs. Theo Grosz. This 80-page book consisted of the history of
Bowdle, its churches, business places, pioneers and settlers.

Along with all the other events were a Murphy's Northern State Carnival,
booths, stands and many eating places for the crowd to gather. Reunions of
relatives in back yards, on lawns and in homes dominated the two-day event.

Family Histories . . .

GLENN WAYNE and LYNNE [JONES] ABBOTT

"My mother, Mary Welborg Jensen, was a secretary in Superior, WI when she
won a South Dakota homestead near Watauga in Corson County with a lottery
ticket in 1908. Only 18, but adventuresome, mother was one of the first
women homesteaders--living in a tent at first. This dwelling was replaced
by a house for winter, one of the best around, built by friends. My father,
Irwin Leon Abbott, owned the adjoining homestead, which was combined with
my mother's, when they married in 1912. My father raised and trained
horses, as well as farmed.

Our family returned to Wisconsin in 1921 to farm near Webster where I
attended rural school. My brother Billy, age 5, died at Kilkare where my
parents managed a resort. Mother wanted to leave so we moved to the Selby
and Glenham area. We then lived on farms in the Bowdle area where I
attended high school.

        Glenn and Lynne Abbott

I always wanted a motorcycle or car. Dad said I could have one when I
earned it. I worked for a neighbor earning 50 cents daily until I could buy
a 1917 Excelsior belt-drive motorcycle. Six months later I hit a lady
driving a Model "T" broadside, smashing it up. She went through a stop
sign. I still have holes in my shin bones. My school friend, Beulah Erbe,
gathered up the pieces of my bike and put them in a shed. After I
recuperated, I rebuilt the cycle trading it plus $5 for a 1925 Model "T"
sports roadster to drive to school--no buses then.

In the middle of my senior year my father died from a heart attack Jan. 9,
1936, leaving us brokenhearted and destitute. After graduation we moved to
Hinckley, MN. Because of asthma I couldn't join the armed forces. During
the war I hauled pipe for the oil fields over the Alcan Highway. I married
Marcella Newcomb in 1942, divorced in 1944 and married Lynne Olson Jones
later that year. We moved to Portland, OR where I was employed as a
mainline mechanic for a large Ford dealership for 29 years. We spent six
months in Hawaii and retired to our home in Portland. Winters are enjoyed
on the desert near Yuma, Arizona.

Lynne's training as a nurse was utilized in caring for our own eight
children, as well as eight foster children. We adopted our children from
previous marriages. We belong to the church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day
Saints (Mormon.) Leon, Herbert and Betty survive in my family. Irvin
(father) Abbott was born Feb. 28, 1884, died Jan. 9 1936 and Mary (mother)
was born July 10, 1889, died Jan. 23, 1974. Children and birthdates are
Jerome Rolf Nov. 20, 1941; Violet Thora April 26, 1942; Glenn Walter Feb.
6, 1943; Anna Oradine Jan. 13, 1944; Thomas Wayne Oct. 5, 1945; Janet
Elayne Dec. 21, 1946; Karen Alberta Nov. 8, 1947 and Linda Mae Jan. 21.
1952."

R.E. [ED] and PAT [CUNNINGHAM] ACKERSON

R.E. (Ed) Ackerson and his wife Sally and four children Tanya, Steve, Mark
and Lori moved to Bowdle in February 1974 to manage the Miller Funeral
Home. All four children graduated from Bowdle High School. Sally died in
April 1981.

Ed married Pat (Cunningham) Afdahl Oct. 1981. Ed and Pat had been brother
and sister-in-law 27 years. Pat's husband died May 1981. Pat also has four
children: Susan, Mike, Lisa and Jeff. Now the family consists of eight
children and 13 grandchildren.

Ed's family is Tanya and David Huffman, Nathan and Sarah of Selby; Steve
and Kristi Ackerson, Ryan and Dustin of Grand Prairie, TX; Mark and Cyndi
Ackerson and Andrew of Orlando FL and Lori and Pat Dewald, Jennifer and
Rachei Ann of Roscoe.

Pat's family is Susan and Ed Crawford, Brian and Emily of Irving, TX; Mike
and Debbie Afdahl Nicole and Alyson of Watauga, TX; Lisa Guest and Ray of
Euless, TX and Jeff and Darlene Afdahl and Aimee of Euless, TX.

Ed's parents both live in Ellendale, ND and Pat's parents live in Redfield.

DR. ALEJANDRO and ROMANA ADAJAR

Dr. Adajar, a native of the Philippines, arrived in Bowdle in 1973 from
Chicago. He saw an ad in a medical journal in Chicago listing the need of a
doctor in Bowdle.

Dr. Adajar had the honor of S.D. Senator George McGovern helping him locate
in this vicinity. After practicing medicine in Bowdle for a year, his
family joined him. They lived in the country for about five years before
moving to town. They decided to purchase the Art Hoffman house, which they
still occupy at the present time.

A few years ago Dr. Adajar and his wife moved to West Virginia, but missing
their small town community they returned after a year. Now Dr. Adajar
continues his medical practice in the clinic north of the hospital. His
wife Romana acts as the receptionist.

        Romana and Dr. Alejandro Adajar

The couple has five children. Beth, an RN, married Carney Haberer. They
have a daughter, Crystal and live in Aberdeen. Adajar Jr. lives and works
in Watertown. Aurora married Harvey Addingast and both work in the medical
field. They live in Abeline, TX. Romano attends USD at Vermillion and is in
premed. Fernando is a senior at Bowdle High School.

FRIEDRECK and ROSINA [STOTZ] AIPPERSPACH

The children of Friedreck and Rosina Aipperspach can trace their family
line back seven generations to the time when their ancestors lived in
Wittenberg, Germany. From there they migrated to Russia where Friedreck was
born June 20, 1868.

He was baptized in the Lutheran faith and attended the Lutheran School.
Nov. 20, 1897 Friedreck was married to Rosina Stotz. Baby Katherine was
born Feb. 22, 1899 but spent only a brief time with them, as she died Dec.
27, 1901. Rosina arrived Dec. 27, 1901 and in 1902 Mr. and Mrs. Aipperspach
brought their daughter to the United States.

They landed in New York and came to Aberdeen by train where Fred Buechler
met them with a buggy and team of horses, taking them to his home where
they spent the winter. Mrs. Aipperspach and Mrs. Buechler were sisters.

In the spring 1903 Friedreck took his family to Venturia, ND where they
homesteaded on 160 acres of land. During their North Dakota years Friedreck
became an American citizen.

Four more children came to bless their home: Eva arrived June 7, 1905; Fred
was born Dec. 15, 1906; Philip was born Jan. 20, 1909 and Lydia arrived
June 29, 1910. Rose, Eva and Fred attended country school until 1912 when
the family moved to South Dakota, spending the first year in the summer
kitchen at the Fred Buechler farm. Martha was born there March 12, 1913.

They established a new home on a farm two miles from the Buechlers were Mr.
Aipperspach bought a quarter section of land. Theodore was born on the farm
July 4, 1918. All the children were baptized and confirmed in the Lutheran
faith. Four children died in infancy.

In 1934 Mr. and Mrs. Aipperspach retired from the farm and moved to Bowdle
where they became members of the American Lutheran Church. Their devotion
to Christ was exemplified by their faithful attendance to services.

Mr. Aipperspach died Dec. 11, 1956 at 88 years of age. His wife survived
him seven years, departing this life Mar. 1, 1963, also at 88 years of age.

Their descendants and spouses are as follows: Rosina became the bride of
Adam Mertz. They had seven children: Allene married Walter Barth; Roland,
whose wife was Mary Lassle; Ella married Vernon Schneider; Elenora is the
spouse of John Gab, Quentin's wife is Lynn, Donald married Margie Rabba and
two children died in infancy.

Eva Aipperspach became the bride of George Naasz. Their children were:
Arlene, who married LeRoy Buhl and Dewyne married Gayland Naasz. Two
children died in infancy.

        The Fred Aipperspach Family

Fred Aipperspach married Tillie Reiner. Two children died. Their son Donald
married Lila Darell Truett, whose only child died.

Phillip married Eleanor Herman. Their daughter Dianne married Richard
Kettering.

Lydia married John Clark. Their son Ka married Dorothy Olsen and another
son Kenneth married Bernadine Ochs. Roger married Judy Pinson. Clarks had
the misfortune to lose their daughter Debora Ann June 14, 1970, when she
succumbed to an illness at age 16 years.

Martha married Adam Reiner. Their son Darryl married Rose Reiner and their
daughter Sheila married Larry Chase.

Theodore married Toppy Smith. They had two daughters: Deedie who married
Richard Brandner and Leslie, who married Benny McCafferty.

At the time of this writing Rose, Eva and Theodore have died. Only four
children survive their parents.

PHILLIP and ELEANOR K. [HERMAN] AIPPERSPACH

Phillip Aipperspach was born in Venturia, ND Jan. 20, 1909 to Mr. and Mrs.
Fred Aipperspach. Fred Aipperspach was born July 20, 1868 in Germany, as
was his wife Nov. 2, 1874. Phillip's father died Dec. 11, 1956. His mother
died March 1, 1963.

Eleanor K. Herman was born July 22, 1915 at Lowry to Mr. and Mrs. Henry
Herman, both of whom were born in South Russia. Eleanor's father was born
Sept. 30, 1876 and died March 24, 1952. Her mother was born March 30, 1878
and died April 11, 1963. Eleanor received her education at the Swan Lake
School near Hoven. She was married to Phillip Aipperspach June 9, 1936 in
Minneapolis, Minnesota.

        Phillip Aipperspach

Phillip is a World War II veteran. He served from Feb. 1943 to Nov. 1945 in
the European Theater. Private Aipperspach was inducted into the 123rd
Ordinance Maintenance Battalion, first Armored Division. After being
trained at Camp Walters, TX and Camp Schingo, PA, Phillip was sent to New
Port News, VA. July 14, he was transported aboard the Mariposa and arrived
in Casablanca, Africa July 21, 1943. He was one of the troops engaged in
battles at Naples, at Foggia, Rome, Arno, Northern Appennines and Po Valley.
He returned to the United States Nov. 18, 1945 from Marseilles, France as
Tech 4 on the J.C. Breckenridge. He arrived in Boston, MA Nov. 26, 1945 and
was discharged from Fort McArther, San Pedro, CA Dec. 8 1945.

Phillip returned to work for the Ford Motor Company in Long Beach, CA where
he was employed 30 years, retiring October 1971. Their current address is
5400 Clark Avenue #131, Lakewood, CA 90712.

Phillip and Eleanor have a daughter, Diane L. married to Richard Kettering
who is employed as a truck driver. Diane and Richard have two children:
Brandi Schwartz (age 14) and Ricky Kettering (age 5.) They live at 3207
Eckleson, Lakewood, CA.

ALEX and ALVINA [KILBER] ALBRECHT

Alex Albrecht was born in Russia Oct. 10, 1900. He died at Bowdle Oct. 27,
1971. He married Alvina Kilber June 21, 1925. Alvina was born Aug. 8, 1903
near Roscoe.

They lived on the farm one mile south of Bowdle. There were good times and
bad. In 1926 a tornado took the roof off the house, the dry 30's and then
the government took the cattle and shot them, burying them in a ditch at
the city dump which was across the road from the farm.

There were sad times when two infant sons died. Jerald 1934 and Leland
1935. Tragedy struck Aug. 5, 1951 when Gilbert drowned in the Mobridge
swimming pool.

They moved to town for a short time and Helmuth Eisenbeisz moved his family
to the farm. Helmuth was asked to work at Farmers Union and Alex and Alvina
moved back to the farm . . . the life they liked best.

The kerosene light was put away then they installed a 6 volt light system.
This was followed by a 32 volt and a windcharger for power. You could buy
refrigerators for 32 volt, which was an improvement over the ice box. You
cut ice all winter and stored it under hay so it would last all summer.
There were no ice machines to get the ice like they do now. When REA was
brought to the area it was like living in town. You could use all the
appliances and if the wind didn't blow you did not have to worry about dim
lights.

Alex served offices -- member of the township, St. John's Lutheran Church
and Sportsmen's Club. He like fishing and carpenter work. He built a
kitchen and bath onto the present house in 1946. He also built toys for his
children, which they still cherish.

Alvina was kept busy with the garden, canning, raising poultry and helping
in the fields during the summer. Winter months were spent sewing clothes
for her family, quilting and crocheting, which she still likes to do.

They retired from farming in 1963 and moved to Bowdle to 1088 Second Avenue.

        Alex and Alvina Albrecht

Children: Lucylle born May 11, 1926, married Helmuth Eisenbeisz Sept. 8,
1946; Gilbert born June 28, 1929, died Aug. 5, 1951; Darlene born March 21,
1931, married Norwin Walz June 2, 1953; Jerald born Dec. 6, 1933, died Jan.
13, 1934; and Leland born Jan. 6, 1935, died Jan. 11, 1935. After the death
of Alex, Alvina remained in her home. She married Jacob Diedtrich Oct. 21,
1973. They are living at 1088 Second Avenue at the present time.

ALFRED and WILHELMINA [MILLER] ALBRECHT

Alfred Albrecht was born Feb. 8, 1868 in Russia. Wilhelmina Miller was also
born in Russia in 1872. They were joined in marriage Nov. 21, 1899.

In 1903 they immigrated to the United States and settled on a farm in
Walworth County. Bowdle was their home from 1915 to 1916. Then they moved
to a farm one mile south of Bowdle where they lived until they retired to
Bowdle in a home formerly located west of St. John's Evangelical Lutheran
Cemetery.

Wilhelmina died Feb. 24, 1934. Alfred remained in Bowdle another three
years and then moved to Roscoe to be near his daughter Ella Weidenmeyer. In
1952 he entered the Lutheran Home in Eureka and died March 29, 1953 after
suffering a stroke.

        Alfred Albrecht

They had four children. Alex, born Oct. 10, 1900, married Alvina Kilber
June 21, 1925 and died Oct. 27, 1971; Edward, born Feb. 8, 1903, lives in
Broderick, CA; Emma, born Feb. 15, 1905, married Robert H. Kilber of Roscoe
and died Jan. 27, 1952 and Ella, born June 13, 1909, married Fred
Weidenmeyer of Roscoe and lives in Sioux Falls.

Wilhelmina Albrecht will be remembered for the big gardens she had and the
vegetables she sold. Alex and his family lived on the home place until he
retired and moved into town.

REV. PAUL and MARIE [HOFFMAN] ALBRECHT

Rev. Paul Albrecht and his wife, Marie, made their home in Bowdle 39 of his
47 years in ministry. His parents, Jacob and Christina Albrecht, were born
in Germany. Paul was born Sept. 17, 1898 in Renville, MN and received his
education at Dr. Martin Luther College in New Ulm, Northwestern College in
Watertown, WI and Wisconsin Synod Seminary.

The Rev. Paul Albrecht and Marie Hoffman were married in Minneapolis. She
was born Oct. 27, 1905 to Pastor and Mrs. Theodore Hoffman at Mayville, WI.

The Albrechts came to Bowdle in July 1927 where he pastored St. John's
Lutheran Church of the Wisconsin Synod. Their family included eight
children.

Marcus, born July 18, 1924 and his wife, Margaret live at Mindora, WI,
where he pastors a church They have three sons. Jerome, born Sept. 23, 192a
is pastor of a church in Milwaukee, WI. He and his wife, Delores have five
children. Quentin was born Oct. 26, 1926. He and his wife, Ardell are
teachers. They have six children and live in Watertown, WI. Lois, born Jan.
28, 1928, her husband, Eddie Krieper and their three children live in
Fairfax, MN. Homer, born May 25, 1929 and wife Christina live in Espanola,
NM. They have one child. Dr. Paul Jr. was born Sept. 24, 1930. He and his
wife Carol have four sons and live in Sparta, WI. Elaine, born Dec. 5, 1933
and husband, Richard Ogren, live in St. Paul with their three sons. Martin
(nicknarned Doc) was born Aug. 25, 1942. He and his wife, Annette have six
children and live in Eau Claire, WI.

In 1959 Pastor Albrecht and some of St. John's church members splintered
from the Wisconsin Synod to form the Synod of Lutheran Confession and
founded Holy Redeemer Church in Bowdle. They built a new church edifice and
parsonage in the western part of Bowdle. Rev. Albrecht served for nine
years as the first president of the Synod of Lutheran Confession. He
pastored this church until 1966 when he retired.

The couple moved to Madison, WI to live and he taught and preached to a
large group of handicapped people and some other adults more than two
years. On his second retirement they made their home in Auburndale, FL, but
found the climate not to their liking and after two years returned to
Wisconsin to make their home in Eau Claire.

Rev. Albrecht died in March 1976. Marie Albrecht continues to make her home
in Eau Claire.

CHRISTIAN and ROSINA [SCHOCK] ALDINGER

Christian Aldinger was born in December 1861 to Friederick and Margaret
Aldinger m Russia. He grew up in Russia and married Rosina Schock there in
1887. They had three children born to them in Russia: Rudolph, Robert and
Mathilda. The family came to the United States in 1894 and arrived in the
Bowdle area in 1900. Two children were born in South Dakota: Pauline and
Reinhold.

        Back: Robert, Pauline, Rudolph, Mathilda. Front: Friederick,
        Reinhold, Christian, Rosina.

Christian purchased land from Mr. & Mrs. H.B. Lennan Sept. 18, 1900. It was
located five miles east and five miles south of Bowdle. He continued to live
on the farm until 1920 when he moved to Greenway.

His first wife died July 4, 1914 and is buried south of Bowdle in a rural
cemetery. Christian lived in Greenway with his second wife Fredericka until
his death April 8, 1922. He is buried south of Bowdle. His children
continued to live on the farm until the late 1920's.

FRIEDERICK and MARGARET [BERRETH] ALDINGER

Friederick Aldinger was born in July 1833 in Russia. He was married to
Margaret Berreth and raised three sons: Christian, Leonhardt and Gottlieb.
He arrived in America at New York City in April 1898, following his son
Christian to South Dakota and Edmunds County.

He homesteaded 160 acres of land north of Bowdle in June 1898, on what is
now the Tim Spiry farm.

His first year on the homestead was a busy one. He built his house, which
was 16' by 16' in size, costing $75. He dug a well, which he valued at $50
and plowed 40 acres of land for planting, in which he invested $120. The
first of these projects was the house in June 1898.

He lived and worked the land from June 1898 until December 1904, when he
sold it to Emanuel Weron. He had received his Homestead Patent for the land
Sept. 16, 1904 from the U.S. Government.

After the sale of the land he bought 160 acres next to his son Christian's
farm. He lived with his son and family until his death Jan. 29, 1910. He is
buried in a rural cemetery south of Bowdle.

JOSEPH and MATHILDA [WAGNER] BACHMAN

Joseph Bachman and his wife Mathilda came to America from Odessa, Russia in
1905. Joseph's first work in the new country was for the Milwaukee
Railroad. Later he worked on a farm near Hoven.

Sometime later Joseph and two of his brothers, Matt and Theo, rented a farm
five miles east of Bowdle. Two years later Mr. Bachman bought land four
miles east of Bowdle and built a home and other farm buildings. It was here
that Joseph and Mathilda raised their family of 12 children, three of whom
died in infancy.

        Joseph and Mathilda Bachman

Mr. Bachman was well known throughout the county, having served as County
Commissioner eight years. Mathilda died in 1940 and Joseph died in 1955.

Their family included Mathew, Bernard and Pius, who live in Bowdle; Mary of
Aberdeen; Sister Assumpta of Mankato, MN; Vincent of Wilmington, DE; Joe of
Alexandria, MN; Tony of Milwaukee, WI and Father Paul Bachman of Highmore.

MATHEW and FRANCES [VAN WELL] BACHMAN

Mathew, son of Joseph and Mathilda Bachman, was born in Bowdle -- one of 12
children. He attended school in Cottonwood Lake Township, five miles east
of Bowdle.

Mathew married Mathilda Gerber in 1935 in St. Anthony's Church at Hoven.
They farmed four miles east of Bowdle. Their family consisted of five
children:

Virginia married Bert Leidholt and lives in Minot, ND; Delbert married
Delores Mardian and resides in Mandan, ND; Betty married Jerry Burke and is
in Corcoran, MN; Paul married Patty Winkler and lives in Pierre; Jerome
lost his life in the Armed Forces in a jet plane off the coast of Japan.

Matt farmed, was on the township board of supervision, ASC Board and State
ASC Advisory Board. He was an original incorporator of FEM Electric
Association and served as a director for 34 years and vice-president of the
FEM Board 1977-1979. He was presented the Pioneer Award by the association
June 1985 for his longtime service to the rural electrification program.
The award signified Matt's lasting and valuable contribution in the early
development and advancement of rural electrification.

Matt worked for Basin Electric as right-of-way agent on the Antelope Valley
Project for 31/2 years. He also worked for Federal Crop Insurance for nine
years. He is active in church work and a member of the Knights of Columbus.

His wife Mathilda died March 4, 1979. He retired in 1981 and moved to
Bowdle. He married Frances Van Well Dec. 26, 1981 at St. Anthony's Church
in Hoven.

RAYMOND and LILA [DUMDIE] BACHMAN

        Back: Ray, Lila, Paul. Front: Victoria, Debra, Teresa

Raymond was born Oct. 3, 1927 in Bowdle to Theodosius and Cecelia Bachman.
He married Lila Dumdie July 17, 1950. Lila was born March 19, 1932 in
Emerado, ND to Gust and Kate Dumdie.

Raymond and Lila were raised in the Bowdle area and graduated from Bowdle
High School. Their family roots go back to before the turn of the century
as their grandparents were some of the first settlers in this area.

Ray entered the U.S. Navy after graduation in 1945, made the Navy his
career and retired 20 years later. In 1950 Lila joined the Navy as his wife
and companion and they spent the first 15 years of their life together
traveling about the country and overseas at various duty stations.

Enroute they managed to bring into this world four children of whom they
are most proud. One highlight was the tour of duty in Japan. It was Lila's
first encounter with life outside the United States. It was an interesting
experience for the entire family. After retirement they returned to South
Dakota. The selection of South Dakota was simply because they had found no
other area in the United States that was a better, nor cleaner, nor safer
place to raise a family.

After stops in Aberdeen, Williston, ND and Mobridge they landed in Bowdle
and purchased the Bowdle Theatre. In 1971 they built the first fastfood
service drive inn at the intersection of Highway 12 and 4th Avenue. The
Corner Cottage is still there.

In 1972 Ray became active in public service by serving one term as a city
councilman. In 1975 he was elected county commissioner of the 5th District
and served 12 years in the capacity. In 1982 Ray returned to the profession
he always enjoyed--the sales and service of insurance. He accepted the
National Farmers Union Insurance in Bowdle and is currently engaged in this
business.

Lila became head cook for the Bowdle School Lunch Program in 1972. She
worked at school over the winter months and together Ray and Lila managed
the Comer Cottage Drive Inn during the summer until 1983, when Lila retired
from cooking and went to work as Ray's secretary and girl Friday with
National Farmers Union Insurance.

Ray and Lila's children are as follows:

Teresa Marie was born April 23, 1951 in Corpus Christi, TX. She and her
husband Darrel Daniels live in Aberdeen with their sons Steven Ray, age 15
and Anthony, age 9.

Paul Alan was born June 13, 1952 in Corpus Christi, TX. He currently
resides with his wife Diane in Huron. Paul is a graduate of South Dakota
School of Mines & Technology, a licensed electrical engineer and is
employed by Northwestern Public Service. Their sons are Nicholas, age 7 and
Nathan, age 3.

Victoria Lynn was born Nov. 17, 1955 in Minneapolis, MN. Vicki and her
husband Duane Knecht reside in Bowdle and own D & D Oil Co. Vicki is also a
full-time student at Northern State College. Duane & Vicki have four
daughters: Melanie Simon, age 13; Carrie Simon, age 12; Sandi is age 5 and
Erin is age 4.

Debra Jean was born July 19, 1958 in Minneapolis, MN. Debi is a graduate of
Dakota Wesleyan College with a degree in radiology technology. She and her
husband C. Scott Parkhurst have two sons: Jeremiah, age 4 and Jordon, age 2.

THEODOSIUS and CECELIA [KRUMM] BACHMAN

Theodosius Bachman was born Nov. 5, 1900 in Russia. His parents had

Seven children were born to Theo and Cecelia Bachman, all of whom were

1925; Raymond, born Oct. 3, 1927; Josephine Bachman Torkelson, born Feb. 2,
1930 and Dorothy Bachman Rhinehart, born June 4, 1933.

Mrs. Cecelia Bachman still resides in Bowdle after almost 84 years. She has
six living children. Four of her children served in the Armed Forces during
World War II. The other children are scattered from the East Coast to the
West Coast.

Edward and Raymond live in South Dakota, Dorothy and George live on the
East Coast, while Jo and Marion are on the West Coast. Mrs. Bachman has 24

BERHHARDT B. JR. and KATHERINE [MILLER] BAER

Barney, or as more affectionately remembered, B.B. Baer, a pioneer farmer
from the southwest of Bowdle, was born Sept. 9, 1888 in Crimea, South
Russia. He was the son of John and Barbara Baer (nee Miller.) In 1889 his
parents brought him to the United States making their first home in the new
land in Freeman. Later they homesteaded in Theodore Township located in
Walworth County. Nov. 18, 1908 he married Katherine (Katie) Miller, the
daughter of Johannas and Marie Miller. Katie Miller Baer, born May 13,
1888, also came to the United States in 1889 from Crimea South Russia. She
and her parents also first settled in Freeman and then homesteaded in
Theodore Township in Walworth County.

        Bernhardt B. and Katherine Baer

Barney (B.B.) and Katie Baer farmed southwest of Bowdle in the community
that their parents had settled and on the original homesteads. In 1927
Barney lost his right arm in a corn shredder accident. He and his sons
continued the farming operation. Even though Barney experienced the loss of
an arm he rose to the occasion by continuing to operate farming equipment
and by becoming active in church and community affairs in the Bowdle area.

He was active as a member of the Board of Directors of the local Bowdle
Farmers Union Elevator. and as an elder in his local church called the
Theodore Lutheran Church. His disability did not limit his activity or his
participation in all areas of family and community living.

Barney (B.B.) died Dec. 14, 1950 and is buried at the Theodore Cemetery.
His wife was a resident at the Colonial Manor in Ipswich until she died Dec.
6, 1984. She is also buried at Theodore Cemetery.

Barney and Katie were original members of the Theodore Lutheran Church and
when this landmark in the Theodore community was moved, they became
members of St. John's Ev. Lutheran Church in Bowdle.

Barney and Katie were blessed with five sons and a daughter. Reinholdt was
born Feb. 8, 1911. He farmed with his brothers and parents. He died Feb.
24, 1952 and is buried at Theodore Cemetery.

Johnny, the second son, was born Feb. 12, 1915. He served his country in
the Army during World War II, married Mary Schumacher of Lake City, MN and
made his home there, where he died on Aug. 9, 1976.

Harold, the third son, was born June 29, 1918. He also served his country
in the Army during World War II and Korean Conflict. He married Annie Jung
of Bowdle and presently resides in Billings, MT. He is retired and active
in the American Legion and Veterans of Foreign Wars. They are the parents
of three children: Peggy, Mark and Michael.

Alma, the only daughter, was born Feb. 7, 1921. She was in business as a
beautician in Selby. She married Herbert Wolff of Java and for many years
they operated a service station in Selby and Mobridge. They have one son
Terry, and have retired to live in Apache Junction, AZ.

Erwin, the fourth son, was born May 17, 1924. He married Lorraine Gorne,
and for many years farmed the original farm of Barney (B.B. Baer) until a
fire took the home and they moved to the Roscoe area to continue with their
farming occupation.

Edmund, the youngest and fifth son, was born Nov. 3, 1926. He served in the
Navy during World War II. He is married to Rhoda L. Sauer of New Ulm, MN.
They have one daughter Larissa. Edmund, a former missionary to Africa and
teacher, is presently employed as director of parole services for the
state of South Dakota. Their home is in Pierre.

        Ed, Harold, Johnny, Reinhold, Erwin Baer

Barney (B.B. Baer) was always interested in education and progress and
encouraged his family to meet life with confidence of hope, stabilized in a
strong Christian heritage. His wife Katie, after Barney's death, moved to
Bowdle where she demonstrated her courage of life and creating beauty. Her
flower garden in Bowdle caught the eye of many of the residents and for
many years her garden cheered many on their way.

WILMER and MARGUERITE [HOFER] BAER

Wilmer W. Baer was born Aug. 21, 1912 at Bowdle, the son of Herman and Anna
Baer. His father was a Bowdle businessman and operator of the Gretna Grain
Elevator in partnership with Henry Bauder for many years before retiring.
Herman C. Baer was born Jan. 4, 1874 in Crimea, Russia and died in 1964.
Anna Baer was born at Oberwart, Austria Jan. 6, 1876 and died in 1965.

Wilmer graduated from Bowdle High School, received his bachelor of arts
degree from South Dakota State University and his master's from the
university at Denver, CO. He married Marguerite E. Hofer May 31, 1939. That
year they moved to Fairview, MT where Wilmer was the high school principal
and in 1944 moved to La Grande, OR where he was the business manager of
Eastern Oregon College. In 1946 he took a teaching position at Washington
State University in Pullman. After 31 years on the faculty, he retired in
1977 as Professor Emeritus of Business Administration.

Highlights of his 31 years in education include a Ford Foundation Seminar
at Williams College, Williamstown, MA, a trip to Europe and a trip on a
Norwegian freighter from Vancouver, B. C. to Philadelphia via the Panama
Canal, which stopped at a number of U.S. west cost ports and other ports in
South America and the Caribbean. Since retirement they have traveled
extensively to the Mediterranean countries of Greece, Turkey and Israel,
also the Caribbean, Mexico and Hawaii.

Wilmer and his wife have two children. Wilma Ann, born April 25, 1944,
married Lynn Ertsgaard in 1966 and has three sons Bryan, Joel and Leif.
They live in Seattle, WA. She teaches part-time and has her own business,
Liturgical Arts.

Norman W. Baer was born May 19, 1947 and lives at Brookings. He married
Linda Larson in 1969 and has a son Benjamin and a daughter Elizabeth.
Norman is on the faculty at South Dakota State University doing teaching
and research.

GUSTAVE and MARIE [KRISCHENOWSKI] BARTH

Gustave Barth was born Aug. 31, 1898 at Hoffenstahl, Neudorf, South Russia
to Wilhelm and Barbara Barth. When he was six months old his parents
brought their family, consisting of the children: Barbara, John, Louise and
the baby, to Bremen, Germany, where they boarded a ship to come to the
United States. The small baby became very ill on the voyage and though the
doctors on shipboard treated the baby, the family did not have funds to pay
for his care and they were quarantined at Ellis Island for a short time due
to the baby's illness.

Two brothers of Gustave's mother, who had preceded them to the U.S. and
settled in the Eureka area, came to the aid of the stranded family and
helped them to get settled in a sod house on a farm north of Eureka.

Two more children came to join the family: Katie, now Mrs. Lehr and Helen,
now Mrs. Schuler were born in Eureka. Gust's parents became caretakers of
the Eureka Lutheran College and Gust attended the college. His mother did
the cooking, baking and washing and his father did the janitorial work. The
family had living quarters there.

Gust's parents were born in Neudorf, South Russia. Wilhelm was born Sept.
2, 1860 and died Oct. 4, 1925. Barbara was born July 25, 1863 and died Dec.
21, 1952.

Gust Barth married Marie Krischenowski Feb. 4, 1926 at Bison and they made
their home on a farm northeast of Hosmer. Esther and Lenora were born
during these farming years. In 1933 the family moved to a farm northeast of
Bowdle. Due to the difficult drought times of the thirties and Mr. Barth's
failing eyesight, the family moved into Bowdle in 1938.

Ernest was born in 1938 and Neil joined the family in 1942. Esther Barth,
who was born in 1927, lives in Mobridge and is the wife of Gerald N.
Ekholm. Lenora was born in 1928 and is married to Norman L. Gross. They
live in Bowdle and have three children: Dean, Shelly and Sheri. Ernest and
Neil live in Pierre, where they have married and each has four children.

        Back: Lenora, Neil, Ernest, Esther. Front: Gustave and Marie Barth.

All of the Barth children graduated from the Bowdle High School and were
confirmed in the Congregational Church in Bowdle.

Gust Barth died Sept. 3, 1979 at the Mobridge Care Center at the age of 81.
Marie Barth still resides in Bowdle.

        GUSTAVE BARTH Born: Aug. 31, 1898--Died: Sept. 3, 1979 IN LOVING
        MEMORY

Gust Barth was a farmer at Heart; loved to talk about those farming days
with his family and old neighbor friends. And even though the family faced
many disappointments, hardships, blizzards, droughts, grasshopper plagues
and then being forced to give up farming due to blindness, Gust still
enjoyed talking about the good old farming days. We all revere the memory
of this brave and courageous man who also had the ability to play a number
of instruments and never missed a German Sing-A-Long at church and his last
home, the Mobridge Care Center.

HENRY and ELIZABETH [KRAMER] BAUDER

In the early days Bowdle had three elevators: Gretna Grain Co., Farmers
Equity and John Geib Elevator and in 1893 a roller mill grinding out flour.

Henry Bauder and Herman Baer, who came to Bowdle in 1898, became owners of
two elevators in 1914 known as Gretna Grain Co. One was in Bowdle and the
other was six miles east on the railroad at the Gretna spur.

Henry and Elizabeth Bauder had three children: Johanna (Askegaard now of
Pasco, WA), Eloise (Holsing now of Salem, OR) and Arnold. Arnold left Bowdle
after graduating from high school to work for Sherwin Williams Paint Co. in
Florida. He and his wife adopted two little boys and later, in appreciation
of the great intelligence of these lads and the happiness they had brought,
decided to adopt another child, but this time one who needed them greatly.
Their little daughter was mentally handicapped, but responded to their
loving care with a greatly increased learning ability. Arnold had moved his
family to Ashland, OR where he owned a hardware store. When he learned he
had a fatal disease he moved his family to Portland where he felt they
would have better opportunities and he died there in 1962.

Henry and his partner sold their Gretna Grain Co. to Joseph Stappler in
1945 and both families moved to the West Coast. Mrs. Bauder died soon
thereafter and Henry made his home with his daughter, Eloise Holsing and
family in Salem until his death.

Johanna Bauder and her husband George Askegaard were teachers in the Bowdle
schools and she sent this information:

"My childhood years were spent in Bowdle until graduation from high school.
I became a teacher and later married, but my parents continued to live in
Bowdle and we often returned to visit on holidays or vacations.

"As youngsters I suppose we were typical of the times. We didn't have our
recreation furnished us, but made our own good times. We played many group
games, one of which was Cricket, which I have never heard of in any other
location. We used the handles of worn out brooms or mops and cut them into
two lengths, 10 inches and 25 inches. We chose up sides and each player got
a chance to pitch, bat or cricket until one of the opponents caught the
little stick and then he was out. The game ended when all the players on
one side were out. Points were assigned for each part of the game and we
kept score. Does anyone in Bowdle still play Cricket?"

EDWIN R. and CLARA [KUNDERT] BAUER

Edwin R. Bauer is the son of the late Andrew J. Bauer and Lena (nee Baer)
Bauer. He grew up in the Bowdle area and graduated from Bowdle High School.
After serving in the United States Marines he came back to Bowdle and
farmed with his father and brother Alvin.

In 1950 he married Clara Kundert, daughter of Albert and Katherine Kundert,
also a Bowdle resident and graduate of Bowdle High School.

Ed worked for the Bowdle Hardware and Clara worked for National Farm Loan
Association, managed by A.C. Merkel. In 1954 they moved to Groton where Ed
worked for the Gullickson Hardware. In October 1955 they moved to Lodi, CA,
where Ed went into partnership with Kundert's appliance.

In 1976 Mr. Kundert retired and Ed and Clara are now sole owners of Kundert
& Bauer appliance in downtown Lodi.

They have two daughters: Bonnie, a registered nurse in the Intensive Care
Unit at Sacramento Mercy Hospital, who married a local rancher, John Rocha,
and Betty, an assistant and receptionist at Sovinskys' Health Center, is
married to Joel Wilson, a welder at Stockton Steel.

The Bauers have many fond memories of their life in Bowdle and hope
everything you plan will be a success.

MARTIN F. and VERNA [LICKFELT] BAUMAN

GEORGE L. and EMILY BAUMGARTEN

In 1884 George Louis Baumgarten filed on government land in southeastern
Walworth County. He brought his wife, Emily, with him and a small frame
house graced the prairie as their home. Neighbors soon followed and were
neighbors indeed, all their lives. These included Charles & Mary Dorwin,
Sam & Mary Boyd, Bill Boyd & wife, sister Meg & husband Morris Baker,
Suppree Commet & wife Jennie, Charles O'Neil & wife.

Fire, hail and drought were dark shadows on the prairie. The state became
the 47th in our nation. Counties were surveyed and Bangor in Walworth
County was the focus of Mr. Baumgarten's service. He was alternately
auditor and treasurer a good share of his time.

Bowdle was the trade town of the settlers. Bowdle was the end of the
railroad until 1909. At the time of the Indian uprising it loomed as a
rescue means to points east. Five children were born to George and Emily
Baumgarten.

They were Matilda Lydia, Edith Emma, Fern Frances, Elsie Emily and George
Arthur. Elsie married Roy Hoefs and is the last leaf on the Baumgarten
tree. Surviving descendants are Lyle Christianson of Witchita, KS and
Lorraine Ward of Madison, WI.

Mr. Baumgarten managed the Bowdle Flour Mill eight years. Of all the
Walworth County Pioneer Club members listed in this story, only the
children of the Commets remain in the Bowdle area.

ROBERT and JUDITH [NOWATZKI] BEADLE

Robert Beadle was born June 27, 1944 to Richard and Phyllis Beadle of
Onaka. He has one sister, Virginia. He graduated from Cresbard High School
in 1962 and attended Northern State College and Aberdeen School of
Commerce. He was employed at Spaulding Auto Co. 1965-1975 as a salesman.

Robert married Judith Nowatzki in 1966 at Aberdeen. She was the daughter of
Ted and Betty Nowatzki of Langdon, ND and has three sisters and two
brothers. After graduating from St. Alphonsus High School in 1963 she
attended Presentation School of Nursing at Aberdeen, graduating in 1966.
She was employed at St. Luke's and Dakota Midland hospitals prior to
moving to Bowdle.

        Back: Rachelle, Sharon, Joseph. Front: Gerald, Judith, Robert
        Beadle.

In 1975 Robert purchased Berg Ford Agency and brought his family to Bowdle.
They have four children. Sharon was born Feb. 25, 1967; Rachelle, April 23,
1968; Joseph, April 27, 1970 and Gerald, April 17, 1974. Sharon had the
honor of being selected 1985 South Dakota State Snow Queen.

Robert Beadle was elected mayor of Bowdle in 1984.

ERWIN O. and ARLENE [JORDAL] BEITELSPACHER

Erwin O. Beitelspacher was born Aug. 30, 1912 to John and Christina
(Schumacher) Beitelspacher near Java. Other children were Ella, who died at
age 22; Melinda, a twin to Erwin; Cleo; Erhard; Ruben; Arnold, whose life
ended at age four due to diptheria; Clarence and Eugene.

Erwin completed eight grades in the District School and in 1938 rented the
Pat Hagen farm southeast of Hoven. In 1942 he purchased the Schuler farm
north of Tolstoy (which he still owns) and in December 1942 he married
Arlene Jordal.

Arlene Inez Jordal Beitelspacher was born April 22, 1917 at Mount Vernon.
She was the daughter of Alfred and Ida Luglan Jordal. Alfred was born Nov.
30, 1882 at Alfred Lee, IL and died Feb. 13, 1947. Ida Jordal was born Oct.
1, 1888 at Fort Dodge, IA and died March 25, 1955.

Erwin and Arlene Beitelspacher's children are Sharon, born Oct. 6, 1943.
She is now the wife of Dennis Freed and a teacher at Paullina, IA. They
have two children: Traci and Susan. Richard Beitelspacher was born Sept. 3,
1944. He married Sharon Beyers and they ranch at Bowdle. Their children are
Krecia, Kindra, Mark and Lance. Shirley Beitelspacher was born Feb. 10,
1946 and is a real estate agent. She married Gary Meddaugh and they live at
Rockville, MD with their children Mark and Wendy. David Beitelspacher was
born Dec. 24, 1954. He and his wife Kathy (Hunstad) have two children
Justin and Joshua. They live at Wessington Springs where David is manager
of the ASCS Office.

Erwin Beitelspacher purchased the George Blando farm two miles east of
Bowdle in 1955 and moved to the Bowdle community where he raised black
Angus cattle for 20 years. In 1969 two new exotic breeds of cattle were
introduced into the "all black herd"--the Simmental from Switzerland and
the Limousin from France, through artificial insemination.

By 1970 Richard was the technician and also operating the "Blando" farm.
The Simmentals were found to be the most favorable stock and soon became
the main herd on the ranch.

        Back: Richard, Erwin, David. Front: Shirley and Sharon
        Beitelspacher.

Arlene Beitelspacher died of cancer in 1967 and Erwin married Willa Knie of
Ipswich in 1970. They lived on her farm southeast of Ipswich until 1975
when they rented out the farm land and retired in Ipswich.

Erwin now enjoys summer fishing on the Missouri and they spend the winter
months in Mission, TX.

CHARLES and ORPHA [BRENNEISE-ZUMBAUM] BENSON

Orpha, a 1951 graduate of Bowdle High School, was born Dec. 20, 1931 to
Henry and Katie (Losing) Brenneise at the farm 2-1/2 miles south of
Greenway, Spring Creek Township, McPherson County. She is the youngest of
eight children. The others are Jonathan, Sam, Sarah, Ruth, Kenas, Nathan and
Adah.

Orpha was united in marriage to Gilbert Zumbaum June 5, 1951 in the Bowdle
Seventh-day Adventist Church with Elder Adam Rudy officiating.

Gilbert, the youngest of three children, was born Dec. 28, 1929 to
Christian H. and Martha (Dollinger) Zumbaum at the farm home in Moscow
Township, McPherson County. He attended country school and grew up to be a
third generation farmer on the Binder Zumbaum homestead. His older brother
is Alvin and is now in the Lutheran Home in Eureka and his sister Lillian
McDonald lives in California. Gilbert was in the Army Oct. 1951 to Oct.
1953. He spent 14 months in Korea. While Gilbert was in Korea, Orpha taught
school in Campbell County.

When Gilbert returned they again were full-time farmers. Adopting two
children, Glenn Aug. 18, 1959 and Arlene April 17, 1962, they were actively
engaged in farming until Feb. 7, 1980 when Gilbert was killed in a farm
accident.

Orpha remained on the farm and a few years later met Charles R. Bensen, a
state highway patrolman about 5-1/2 miles west of Leola. To make a long
story short Charles was baptized into the Seventh-day Adventist Church May
14, 1983 in Bowdle and retired June 17. Charles and Orpha were married July
3, 1983.

        Charles and Orpha Benson

Charles Ronald Bensen was born Dec. 30, 1928 to Charles August and Mary
(Underbrinh) Bensen at Ann Arbor, MI. At age five they moved to St. Paul,
MN where he grew up with his sister Ruth. It was May 1946 when he graduated
from the John A. Johnson High School. He enlisted in the U.S. Army Sept. 2,
1946 and received an honorable discharge March 2, 1948.

Charles married Marion Anderson May 20, 1949 and lived in St. Paul working
in the carpenter trade for two years, farmed at Clarks Grove, MN a few
years and then moved to Rapid City in 1960 where he worked on the Titan
Missile sites.

Six children were born to this union: John R. and Charles A. now of
Aberdeen; Barbara and Patricia of California and Julie of Faulkton.
Elizabeth died in infancy.

April 29, 1963 Charles joined the South Dakota Highway Patrol and July 22,
1963 they moved to Faulkton where he was stationed for 18 years. Late in
1963 Marion was diagnosed as having multiple sclerosis. She died Feb. 21,
1978. Charles was transferred July 1, 1981 to Eureka where he served until
retirement.

Charles and Orpha are now living on the Binder Zumbaum homestead. In 13
months after their marriage they have helped build four churches with the
Maranatha group. They do extensive traveling.

ALBERT and LENORA [EISENBEISZ] BERG

Albert, the son of Jacob Jr. and Christina (Dietterle) Berg, was born on a
farm in the Hoven area May 11, 1919. At the age of 16 Albert entered the
Civilian Conservation Corp, serving two years as an assistant leader. He
later returned to farming. In 1942 he was drafted into the service and
served 42 months in the Air Force during World War II. After his discharge
Albert settled in Bowdle and worked as assistant manager of Gretna Grain
Company.

At this time he met Lenora Eisenbeisz, daughter of Fred M. and Anna
(Scherbenski) Eisenbeisz, who was born in Bowdle Jan. 29, 1924. Lenora
graduated from the Bowdle High School and then attended Northern State
College, receiving her B.S. and M.S. degrees in education and school
administration.

        Lenora and Albert Berg

Albert and Lenora were married in 1947. For the next four years Albert
owned and operated a small construction company and confectionary in Bowdle.
Lenora continued teaching in Bowdle. In 1951 Albert sold his business and
became the Standard Oil bulk dealer and built the Standard Oil Station. In
1957 he sold the Standard Oil Agency and purchased the Ford dealership,
which he continued to manage until his retirement in 1976. At this time
Lenora became superintendent of schools at Roscoe and a year later
superintendent of Bowdle Public Schools. After Albert's retirement he
became mayor of Bowdle, a position he held six years.

Albert and Lenora took time to raise, love and enjoy their twin daughters:
Bonna and Donna. Bonna married Larry Eisenbeisz of Bowdle. They have one
daughter Tara. Bonna is a supervisor for the Social Security
Administration. Larry works for the Internal Revenue Service as an appeals
officer in the St. Paul, MN area.

Donna married John Carlson of Bowdle. They have one son Jeffrey. Donna is a
building manager for General Service Administration. John is vice-president
of finance for Webb Publishing Company in the St. Paul, MN area.

        John and Donna          Larry and Bonna,
        Jeffrey Carlson         Tara Eisenbeisz

JACOB J. and ALVINA [BAER] BERG

Jacob J. Berg was born in rural Hoven to Jacob and Christina (Dieterle)
Berg April 27, 1914. He lived here during his boyhood years until he joined
the Armed Forces of World War II.

Alvina Baer was born to Theodore and Lydia (Riede) Baer near Hoven Oct. 29,
1921. She is a family member of 13 children and 12 are still living.

Jacob and Alvina were married Dec. 2, 1943 in Tampa, FL while Jake was
stationed at the Air Force Base. They were blessed with a son Ronald Jan.
12, 1945 in Tampa.

Following his service duty Jake became a truck driver in Bowdle for several
years and their daughter Connie was born Aug. 9, 1948. The family then
moved to Claremont where Jacob worked for the elevator company for two
years. The family moved back to Bowdle and Jake operated the Standard Oil
Station for 22 years, retiring in 1975.

Jake died Oct. 19, 1982. Alvina continues to live in Bowdle.

Their son Ronald married Gwen Wagenaar of Arlington. They live with their
sons Michael and Jonathan in Albuquerque, NM. Ronald is an offset cameraman.

Connie Berg was married to Matthew Gundlach and has two sons Matthew Jr.
(Fritz) and Nathan. Connie and her sons live in Bloomington, MN where she
works as a direct marketing copywriter.

        Ronald and Connie, Jacob and Alvina Berg

JACOB JR. and CHRISTINA [DIETTERLE] BERG

Jacob Berg Jr. was born to Mr. and Mrs. Jacob Berg Sr. June 29, 1891 in
South Russia and came with them when a young man to America. His parents
settled on a farm between Bowdle and Java. Dec. 15, 1910 he married
Christina Dietterle. She was born to Jacob and Elizabeth (Seickloch)
Dietterle at Klositz, Russia Sept. 10, 1889. When she was 18 she came to
America with her family and settled with them on a farm in the Lowry area.

Jacob took his bride to a farm near Hoven, where they lived until March
1943, when they bought a farm west of Bowdle. Jacob died in 1946 at the age
of 54. His wife then moved to Bowdle. In 1954 she married Albert Dietz of
Lodi, CA and they made their home in Lodi for 20 years. Mr. Dietz died in
1973. Christina then returned to South Dakota and made her home with her
daughter, Mrs. Lydia Schmidtgall until her death in 1974 at the age of 84.

Six children were born to Jacob Jr. and Christina Berg: Lydia (Mrs. Edward
Schmidtgall) who farmed near Bowdle; Jacob J. Berg (married Alvina Baer),
farmed near Bowdle and then later was manager of the Bowdle Standard Oil
Station until his death; Albert (married Lenora Eisenbeisz) and ran a Ford
dealership in Bowdle; Erwin (married Allegra Maish of Roscoe) lives in
Watkins, MN managing a retirement home; Esther (married Dale Murray) and
lives in Pueblo, CO, retired from Civil Service career and Melvin lives in
Denver, CO.

ARTHUR and EMILIE [BUXCEL] BIEBER

Arthur Bieber was born June 3, 1910 on the family farm in Walworth County,
south of Java. His parents Johann and Elisabeth Bieber had come to this
country with their parents when small children from Glueckstahl, Russia and
lived in the Eureka area. After they were married they homesteaded south of
Java where they reared their 11 children. They retired to live in Bowdle in
1919. Arthur's mother Elisabeth was born Dec. 30, 1872 and died in 1930. His
father was born Nov. 14, 1869 and died in 1932.

Arthur received a high school education and married Emilie (Millie) Buxcel
Jan. 11, 1931. Her parents were Frederick and Katherine Buxcel. Mr. Buxcel
was born in Hillsboro, KS Oct. 27, 1886 and died Dec. 5, 1913. Emilie's
mother was born in Mannsburg, South Russia Feb. 12, 1888 and departed this
life Jan. 12, 1979. Emilie was born in Hutchinson County Nov. 4, 1919 and
received an elementary education.

After their marriage Arthur and Emilie farmed on his father's homestead
where their eight children were born. One died at an early age.

Allene Lillian was born Sept. 3, 1931, is the wife of Morris Eisenbeisz and
the mother of four children: Hope, Blake, Miles and Heidi.

Willis Arthur was born Nov. 14, 1932. He married Joanne Masteller. They have
two sons Scott and Gregg and are ranchers in the Bowdle area.

LeRoy William, born Jan. 23, 1934, married Jo Ann Dosch and is a rancher
in the Leola area. They have three children: Theresa, Melissa and Amy.

Ronald Alfred, born Aug. 24, 1935, married Lois Menzel and is a rancher in
the Leola area. They have four children: Craig, Sandra, Kristi and Stewart.

Dale Roger, born Aug. 30, 1940, is a Bowdle farmer and married the former
Mardella Buechler. Their children are Beth, Dawn and Joshua.

Dennis John, born Nov. 12, 1942, farms in the Bowdle area. He married the
former Jeanne Geditz. Their children are Penny, Colette, Tammy, Justin and
Katrina.

Mary Ann Margaret was born Oct. 5, 1945 and is the wife of Charles Mertes of
Hoven, where he deals in refrigeration and farms. Mary Ann is a nurse.
Their children are Barry, Monte and Marty.

        Back: Ron, Dale, Willis, Dennis. Front: Maryann, Millie, Art,
        Allene, LeRoy Bieber.

After living on the farm 41 years, their son Dennis took over the farm and
Art and Millie retired to live in Bowdle.

Mrs. Bieber recalls that her parents homesteaded in Hutchinson County in
1907. Her father was ill of dropsy and could not work, so her mother, with
the help of her father, built a sod house in the summer of 1913. Frederick
Buxcel died the following December, leaving her mother with four small
children. She found work seven miles from home, doing housework for a
family that owned a store and had the post office. In 1915 Katherine Buxcel
remarried to Paul Haeder of the Java area, where she lived until 1977. She
spent the last 21 months of her life in the Bowdle Nursing Home.

Of their life, Arthur recalls, "We started farming in 1931 right after the
depression years. The first 10 years were very hard. He became ill in the
spring 1933. There were many hospital and doctor bills and 1934 brought no
rain, but during that dry time, we managed to build a new house on the
homestead. The old house was no longer livable. Our six children were born
during these hard times. It was another two or three years before the rains
came again and we had a good harvest."

"We struggled through until 1943 when the crops improved and prices were
better due to World War II. Then life became much easier and the children
were old enough to be of some help. Also modern machinery made life on the
farm much better."

DALE and MARDELLA [BUECHLER] BIEBER

Dale Rodger Bieber, son of Art and Millie Bieber, grew up on a farm
southwest of Bowdle. As a young man he attended Northern College in
Aberdeen and Augustana College at Sioux Falls and served in the National
Guard. He then returned to farm with his dad and brothers.

Aug. 22, 1965 he married Mardella Edna Buechler, daughter of Arthur and
Edna Buechler. Mardella was a graduate of Concordia College in Moorhead, MN
and had worked for the state of South Dakota as a social worker.

        Dale, Mardella, Beth, Joshua, Dawn Bieber.

Together they began farming on the old Jake Perman place north of Hoven.
Since the house on that farm had fallen into disrepair and did not have
running water or central heat, their first big project was to build a
house. They did much of the work themselves with lots of help from
relatives, especially Dale's mother, his brother Dennis and Mardella's
mother. By Thanksgiving they were able to live in part of the basement.

Long before the house was completed they started on their second
project--raising a family. Their eldest daughter, Beth Ann, was born Sept.
9, 1966. The three of them lived in one room in the basement for six
months. By the time Dawn Renee joined the family April 5, 1968, the first
floor of the house was pretty well complete. When Joshua Dale came along
Nov. 25, 1972, they finally finished the basement and utility room. Now the
house and family were complete.

Some of the other big projects they've worked on together have been the
removal or renewal of old buildings, the addition of a few new buildings,
the construction of many yards of corral, and the planting and cleaning of
miles of shelterbelt trees. The land has also seen some improvement. One
quarter that was sod is now under irrigation and many, many days have been
spent removing rocks from all the fields.

Like all the farmers in the area, they have weathered some bad years. There
have been the winter of 1977-1978 and the droughts of the late 1970's and
early 1980's plus the ever recurrent sieges of bad prices. Their worst year
has probably been 1974 when not only did the bottom fall out of the cattle
prices, but their 20-month-old son Joshua suffered a brain tumor and was
hospitalized for six weeks at the University Hospital in Minneapolis.
Joshua made a full recovery, but the cattle prices still suffer occasional
fits of depression.

Dale and Mardella have many things in common. They are both lifetime
members of St. Paul American Lutheran Church and have served and continue
to serve in various positions on the council, Sunday school and ALCW. They
also have a common interest in music. Mardella started playing organ in
church when she was 13. Dale began singing solos in high school. They
started dating when Dale was asked to sing at a wedding for which Mardella
was to play. Mardella still plays for church and Dale still sings an
occasional solo. Through the years the children have joined them in various
types of ensemble music.

DENNIS and JEANNE [GEDITZ] BIEBER

Dennis Bieber was born to Art and Emilie (Buxcel) Bieber Nov. 12, 1942 at
Mobridge. He grew up on the farm and completed the eighth grade education
offered in the township school. After graduating from Bowdle High School, he
served six months in the Armed Forces National Guard and then enrolled in
South Dakota State University at Brookings. He continued to farm with his
father and brothers on land his grandfather homesteaded.

Dennis married Jeanne Geditz Aug. 10, 1968, daughter of Peter Jr. and
Josephine Sindelar Geditz. Dennis and Jeanne have five children. Penny was
born Sept. 16, 1969; Colette, Aug. 31, 1970, Tammy, July 15, 1972; Justin,
Dec. 5, 1975 and Katrina, Feb. 4, 1979.

        Back: Penny, Jeanne, Dennis, Colette. Front: Tammy, Justin,
        Katrina Bieber.

The children all attend Bowdle Schools and are active in swing choir,
basketball, cheerleading, drill team, band and chorus. In 1984 Penny was
chosen Junior Miss Bowdle and Tammy and her cousin Josh Bieber won the
State Junior Talent Contest held in conjunction with the South Dakota Snow
Queen Contest. Colette was named Junior Miss Bowdle in 1985. All the
children are active in the Country Cousins 4-H Club. Penny was chosen the
first 4-H Queen of Walworth County and is a State 4-H Ambassador.

The Dennis Bieber family continues to live on the family homestead raising
and feeding cattle.

EDWIN E. and MARGARET [JOHLFS] BIEBER

Edwin E. Bieber, son of John and Cecelia Bieber, was born on the farm

the business college at Chillicothe, MO.

When the Farmers Union Oil Co. was organized in Bowdle Eddie was one of the

Edwin married Margaret Johlfs, daughter of B.R. and Marie (Harms) Johlfs,
Feb. 7, 1948. She was a graduate of Augustana College in Sioux Falls.

        Back: Mike, Mark, John. Front: Margaret, Jean Ann, Mathew, David,
        Edwin

Edwin and Margaret Bieber have retired and live in Brainard, MN and spend
