DAVID H. and CHRISTINA [STOECKER] EISENBEISZ

Born Aug. 9, 1894 near Neuglueckstahl in the south of Russia, David H.
Eisenbeisz was brought to the U.S. in 1899 by his parents (John Eisenbeisz
Sr.) when the family immigrated to South Dakota and settled on a farm about
seven miles north of Bowdle.

He was one of six children. His three brothers were John Jr., who with his
wife and children immigrated to a farm near Abby, Sask., Canada; Jacob, who
lived on the family farm homestead; Christian, who lived in Mobridge many
years where he was employed by the railroad and in later years moved to
California; and his two sisters were Katherine Bieber, who moved to
California and Mary Schneider, who with her family moved to California many
years ago.

About two years after coming to this country John Eisenbeisz Sr. died in
1901. This left a widow with six children to raise and they all worked
together to survive on the family farm north of Bowdle.

        John Eisenbeisz Sr. Family Back: John Jr., David H., Jacob. Front:
        Christian, Mr. & Mrs. John Sr. and Mary

In 1915 David married Christina Stoecker, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Fred
Stoecker Sr. of Hosmer.

After working for others a few years, David became the owner of the Farmers
Cream Station in 1920 and remained with it until about 1980. In January
1983 he broke a hip in a bad fall and has been immobilized since then and
for some time now, has been a patient in a rest home in Faulkton.

        David and Christina Eisenbeisz

David and Christina had six children: Arthur, Albert (stillborn,) Martha,
Reinhold, Albert and Hilda (died as a small child.)

The oldest Arthur managed a Red Owl store in the Midwest for a time. He and
his wife moved to Seattle, WA where he was stationed with the Coast Guard
during World War II. After the War, they remained in West Seattle where he
owned an insurance and accounting business. He is now semi-retired as a
Certified Public Accountant. Their only child Robert gave his life for our
country in the Vietnam War in 1971.

Martha (Sepp) is living in retirement in the home place in Bowdle.

Reinhold had a successful career in the Federal Civil Service and having
retired several years ago as comptroller of the Naval Air Station in
Seattle, he and his wife continue living there where his three daughters
live.

Albert recently retired after 24 years with the U.S. Postal Service, plus
three years with the VA Insurance Division. He and his wife live in
suburban Minneapolis, MN.

FRED M. and ANNA [SCHERBENSKI] EISENBEISZ

Fred, the son of Matheis and Katherina (Kaiser) Eisenbeisz, was born in
Walworth County near Bowdle Oct. 18, 1894. At the age of four his father
died. Four years later Fred and his mother moved to Bowdle. Fred took
farming jobs with his brother. For a time Fred worked as a mechanic in the
Ford garage owned by his brother-in-law J.J. Eisenbeiss. During this time
he met Anna Scherbenski, daughter of Christian and Christina (Limle)
Scherbenski, who was born near Bowdle Nov. 20, 1917.

In spite of looking into a grim future as a possible draftee for the First
World War, Fred and Anna were married Dec. 18, 1917. Anna thought Fred to
be rather wealthy because he owned a car, grass mower and was part owner in
a threshing machine.

        Back: Alice, Lenora, Morris, Anna Mae, Deloris Front: Alvin, Anna,
        Fred, Lucille Eisenbeisz

Fred and Anna moved to a farm southwest of Bowdle. Five years later they
settled on the old Homestake three miles south of Bowdle, where he owned
and operated his farm until he retired. Anna recalls three particular
years. In 1927 corn was the main fuel to burn to keep the family warm. In
1929 the farm house and all their belongings burned to the ground. Fred
died Nov. 10, 1971 at the age of 77.

Fred and Anna took time to raise, love and enjoy their seven children:
Alice (Mrs. Albert Huber) lives in Bowdle and works as a nurse's aide.
Deloris (Mrs. Eugene Vilhauer) taught school and later managed a bakery in
Sioux Falls, where she now lives. Lenora (Mrs. Albert Berg) graduated from
Northern State with a B.A. and M.S. degree in education and school
administration. She lives in Bowdle. Lucille (Mrs. Warren Ham) lives in
Mount Clemens, MI working as a bookkeeper. Morris married Allene Bieber and
farms south of Bowdle. Alvin married Kathleen Dewald and farms south of
Bowdle. Anna Mae (Mrs. Donald Lange) lives in Atlanta, GA working in Civil
Service in the accounting department.

At the present 23 grandchildren and 25 great-grandchildren have completed
this family.

HELMUTH and LUCYLLE [ALBRECHT] EISENBEISZ

Helmuth Eisenbeisz was born Dec. 14, 1924 in Hosmer. His widowed mother

Helmuth attended the District School near his farm home.

Sept. 8, 1946 he married Lucylle Albrecht. She was born May 11, 1926 to

Their children include Luane, born May 8, 1950 and a graduate of Bowdle

Lanet Eisenbeisz was born Aug. 16, 1953 in Bowdle, graduated from Bowdle

Loxie Eisenbeisz was born Dec. 13, 1960 and graduated from Mobridge High

Hadley Eisenbeisz was born Oct. 7, 1965 at Bowdle. A graduate of Mobridge
High School, he is now a student at South Dakota State University in
Brookings majoring in civil engineering.

Helmuth started working at Farmers Union Oil Co. in Bowdle in 1946 and then
moved to the Alex Albrecht farm in March 1947 where they lived four years
before moving back to town Helmuth continued to work for Farmers Union Oil
Co. until August 1969.

Lucylle taught school until 1948. In 1949 she went to work at the Red Owl
Store, continuing for 21 years and part-time at Mobridge Livestock Barn
from 1961 to 1969.

In August 1969 they moved to Rapid City where Helmuth worked for Strut
Sheet Metal and Brenneise Construction Co. In March 1970 he accepted the
position of manager for Farmers Union Oil Co. in Orient. The following year
they moved to Mobridge where Helmuth worked for Holzworth Brothers until
the fall 1977 when he was made head custodian of Mobridge High School, a
position he still holds.

Lucylle worked at Stoicks Super Market Bakery, the Mo Rest Motel and the
school. She says, "We attend most of the school activities as Helmuth
drives the bus for out-of-town games. He does building of furniture for our
children and grandchildren and likes working on cars. He is presently
restoring two Mustangs owned by our son."

        Loxie, Lanet, Luane, Hadley, Lucylle, Helmuth

"Highlights in our lives were when our three daughters were Snow Queens,
Luane and Lanet at Bowdle and Loxie at Mobridge. We live in one of the
oldest homes in Mobridge. It has been shown on the Jaycees Open House Tour
and the Home Economics Class toured it several times. Everything is
original except for the new kitchen cupboards.

We will always remember the blizzard of 1966 as a fun time. The Erv Gross
family, except Erv and Cathy, stayed with us as did Rosina Eisenbeisz and
Katherine Oster. Erv went to his store and brought milk, soup and items
that could be heated on the oil space heater which Helmuth set up in the
hallway. Kerosene lights took the place of the electric lights. It seemed
like a big happy family homecoming."

JACOB H. and EVA [KURLE] EISENBEISZ

One time Bowdle area farmers, pictured above are Mr. and Mrs. Jacob H.
Eisenbeisz. Jacob was born April 12, 1887 in Odessa, Russia, the son of
John and Katherine nee Hottman Eisenbeisz, who brought their family to a
farm 5-1/2 miles north of Bowdle in 1898.

        Jacob H. and Eva Eisenbeisz

In 1908 Jacob married Eva Kurle of the Akaska area. She was born in
Bergdorf, Russia in 1886 and came to the United States with her mother May 5,
1905.

Mr. and Mrs. Eisenbeisz had two daughters. In 1916 they adopted Lydia
Martel, who was orphaned when she was five years old by the death of her
mother at Logan County, North Dakota. Their daughter Edna was born on the
farm and became the bride of Fred Hettick.

In the 1920's Jacob H. brought his family into Bowdle where he worked as a
salesman for the Ford Garage, until in the 30's when they returned to his
mother's farm. In 1942 they moved to Bismarck, ND where they lived with
their daughter until their deaths.

MATHEIS and KATHERINA [KAISER] EISENBEISZ

In 1851 Matheis Eisenbeisz was born in South Russia in the village of
Neuglueckstahl, where he grew to adulthood. He met Katherina Kaiser who was
also born in this area Aug. 31, 1856.

Matheis Eisenbeisz and Katherina Kaiser were united in marriage in the
village of Neuglueckstahl, South Russia. Eight children came to bless this
union: Matheis, Jacob M. Katherine, Christina, John, David, Christ and
Fred. Fred was the only child of this union born in America.

Compulsory military service, religious persecution and economic unrest
forced the couple to sell their belongings and emigrate to the United States
on the ship Kaiser Wilhela in the year 1894.

Matheis and Katherina, with their seven children, acquired a homestead
stake in Walworth County northwest of Bowdle. Oct. 18, 1894 the eighth
child Fred M. was born. His father Matheis died April 23, 1898 and
Katherina, with her eight children, continued to farm in this area and the
children grew to adulthood.

Matheis was born Oct. 11, 1877. He married Rosina Oster. They set up farming
near Hosmer. Seven children were born to this union: Emil, Albert, Elmer,
Gardner, Gerhard, Helmuth and Ardella.

Jacob M. was born May 15, 1879. He married Maggie Ehret and after a short
period of farming, settled in Aberdeen, operating a bar on main street.
Five children were born to this marriage: George, Magdalina, Jacob Jr.,
Barney and Pauline.

Katherine, born Feb. 12, 1882, married J.J. Eisenbeiss. He operated the
Ford dealership until his wife died in 1929, leaving 10 children to be
raised by the father. After his wife died, J.J. moved to California. His
children were Otto, Albert, Herman, Hildegard, John, Henry, David, Herbert,
Harold and Ted.

Christina was born June 10, 1884 and married Jacob Schock. They farmed in
the Bowdle area. Six children came to bless this union: Kate, Jake, Lydia,
Bertha, Martha and Edna.

John M. was born Aug. 31, 1886. He married Rosina Schumacher. They had one
son Kenneth. John also farmed in Walworth County.

        Back: Jacob, Katherine, Matheis Jr. Middle: Matheis Sr., John,
        Christina, Katherina Front: Christ. Dave, Fred Eisenbeisz

David M. Eisenbeisz was born July 23, 1888. He married Julia Rohrback. They
farmed in the Hosmer area. Six children were born to this marriage: David,
Marie, Katy, Christina, Martha and Melvin.

Christ M. was born Jan. 30, 1892. He was six months of age when his parents
left South Russia, bound for America. Christ married Lydia Fischer and nine
children were born to this union: Elsie, Lillian, Edna, Viola, Martha,
Annie, Clarence, Lee and Agnes. Christ and his family spent most of their
life farming in the West River area.

The last and eighth child Fred M. was born in Walworth County northeast of
Bowdle Oct. 18, 1894. He married Anna Scherbenski of Bowdle. They farmed
near Bowdle until their retirement. Fred died Nov. 10, 1971. Seven children
were born to this marriage: Alice, Deloris, Lenora, Lucille, Alvin, Morris
and Anna Mae.

Katherina Eisenbeisz lived to see all her children grow to adulthood. She
died July 24, 1945 at the age of 89. All her children are deceased.

RHEINHOLT and CLARA [HENKE] EISEMANN

Rheinholt Eisemann was born Feb. 23, 1913 at Eureka. His parents were John
and Martha Eisemann, both born in Russia and now deceased. Rheinholt
received an eighth grade education. He married Clara Elsa Henke Jan. 24,
1942 at Portland, Oregon.

Clara's parents were John and Martha Henke, both born in Russia, John in
1883 and Martha in 1892. She died in 1920. Clara received a tenth grade
education.

Rheinholt and Clara had two children. Rheinholt John was born Dec. 5, 1943
and married Joanna Lynn Veazie in 1972. He is employed by IBM Company.
Kathy Ann was born Sept. 1, 1946 and married Edward P. Tisch in 1970. Both
are in the insurance business and Edward is manager with the company.

Rheinholt relates: "I worked for Jake and Katie Keszlers during the Dirty
Thirties, then I hopped a freight train at Mobridge and rode it to
Vancouver, WA. From there I took a bus to Portland, OR and went to work the
next day at a Shell Oil Station. I was really on my way to Malin, OR to see
Philip and Robert Leidholt. I worked at the Shell Station for nine months
and then got my own Shell Station. Pretty soon I got a letter from Uncle
Sam saying: 'Greetings, Eisemann, I want you to join the Armed Forces.' I
went for induction, but was rejected and my business was gone. I went to
work in a joiner plant outfitting ships.

        John, Clara, Rheinholt, Kathy Ann Eisemann

"After the war I chauffeured Mr. and Mrs. George Buckler for about a year
and then went to work for the Carnation Milk Co. I drove retail
(house-to-house delivery) seven years and wholesale milk and ice cream
truck for three years until disabling arthritis got me. It affects my back
and I also have two metal knees. I am totally disabled and have not driven
a car or worked for 15 years. I also have brain damage, but considering
everything, I am in pretty good shape.

"I got married Jan. 24, 1942 to the most beautiful woman in Portland. We
first had a son and then a daughter. My lovely wife is retired. God has been
good to us and I hope He is also good to the Bowdle people and all my
friends."

ALVIN and RUTH [LEE] ERBE

Alvin, son of August and Emma Erbe, was born Aug. 3, 1892 on the family

When Alvin married Ruth Lee June 12, 1918, the old house was moved across

        [Lee] Erbe.

Ruth Erbe Strom was known for her pleasant personality, delightful sense of
humor and interest in people. The Alvin Erbe farm, built with much effort,
hope and pride, has gone the way of many others--a victim of changing times.

ARLYN ERBE [Submitted by Eunice Mueller]

Arlyn Erbe was born March 27, 1915, the third of four children born to Earl
and Tillie Erbe, who homesteaded on land west of Bowdle in Walworth County.

Arlyn never married and now owns and operates the farm which belonged to
his father. He had a gift for working with machinery, which he inherited
from his father. His hobby was to collect antique cars and restore them.
The cars have been used in parades in Bowdle and nearby communities many
times.

Arlyn was his father's righthand man and when only 10 or 12 years old, he
used to haul the grain to town in the fall for his father. He got along
fine with the old Dodge truck, except when another car or truck driver
would come up behind him and honk the horn. He would be so startled he would
drive the truck right smack into the ditch.

Finally to keep Arlyn and the truckload of grain out of the roadside
ditches, his father sent his younger brother Harold along to watch out the
rear window and let Arlyn know when he could expect someone to toot the
horn. Harold saved the day for the whole family.

This calm young chap successfully took up motorcycle riding as well as
hunting from an airplane. The following is taken from an article written by
Max Cooper of the Aberdeen American News staff during the 1940's.

"Arlyn Erbe, farm youth of the Spring Lake District in Walworth County, has
found hunting of fox and other game from the air a profitable venture. He
brought in a truckload of game pelts to County Auditor Spiry's office in
Selby this week to make application for bounty.

"The bag constituted his take from Dec. 6 to Jan. 28, most of which were
taken in the southern part of the county. The load consisted of 99 foxes, 4
coyotes and 1 badger. The total bounty claim was $776.50 for the 104
predatory animals.

"Arlyn is an ardent airplane pilot and hunter and spends most of his spare
time during the winter hunting. He stated he would receive enough from the
skins to pay him for his shells and gasoline, which were his major
expenses."

The Hoven Review wrote of him: "With due respect to all the other fliers,
folks hereabouts are doffing their hats to pilot-farmer Arlyn Erbe, who
lives about 14 miles north of Hoven. He has flown every type of mission,
either in or out of Hoven, for the past few weeks. Pilots have been in the
limelight here since early December--nearly four months. This winter, which
will undoubtedly be recorded as one of the toughest, has been unduly hard
on all types of ground transportation. On several occasions Hoven has been
snowbound for a solid week at a time. Some farmers haven't been able to
drive their cars to town since late in December."

"Erbe, along with other pilots, has flown in the mail, flown out people in
need of a doctor, brought an expectant mother to the hospital, a soldier
home on furlough had to get back to camp, a farmer has run low on
groceries, another has run out of fuel and a farmer had the misfortune to
break his arm. Whatever the need, Arlyn was there to help. These planes,
equipped with skis adaptable for landing and taking off on the snow, have
been messengers of mercy to those stranded by the snow blocked roads."

        Arlyn Erbe with his airplane.

Arlyn is now 70 years old and has a companion farmer who helps operate the
Erbe farm, where those antique cars are stored for safekeeping and pleasure.

MR. and MRS. AUGUST ERBE

August Erbe left Black Earth, WI with three of his brothers John, Henry and
George in 1881. Their father gave each of them a pair of oxen and $100 cash
when they left home and with this meager start they went west to seek their
fortunes.

August Erbe first took up a quarter of land near Ipswich, but decided to
move to the Spring Lake District where his brothers settled, because the
land there was much better for farming.

He built a small house out of sod and lived in it several years before he
could afford to build another made of lumber. August batched it for seven
years and June 12, 1888 he was married at Bowdle. His wife was amazed to
find he had a pet fox tied up in the cellar. She felt it her duty to clean
things up at once and worked hard at her task. She picked cow chips for
fuel and they were burned in an old-fashioned straw burning stove which was
used for cooking and heating.

The couple had five children. Earl was the oldest, born June 29, 1889. He
required much care for many months thereafter and it was feared he would
not survive. Alvin was born Aug. 3, 1892; Lucy Erbe McElroy was born July
11, 1898; Delbert was born in 1901 and died at age 4 of a rare disease and
Alice was born June 25, 1907.

EARL and TILLIE [LEE] ERBE

The Arlyn Erbe farm, seven miles west of Bowdle on Highway 12, has the
possibility of become a century farm as his grandfather, August Erbe, along
with his brothers John, Henry and George came to Dakota Territory in 1888
to live on that land. Earl Erbe, father of Arlyn, was born on the farm June
29 1889 and in 1918 purchased it from the other heirs. He had two brothers
and two sisters. Alice (Mrs. John Knecht) of Colfax, CA is the only family
survivor.

Earl received his education in the little schoolhouse on the hill near the
farm, as did his children, but they were able to enjoy a secondary and
college education. His daughters became school teachers helping other
children. Earl also learned to play the piano, which he greatly enjoyed.

His mind was always going full-tilt, and one of his childhood experiences
was to dynamite some cottonwood trees and shrubs that grew about a mile
from the house, which he managed to do safely, though he was still a
student at the little schoolhouse. He knew he had better have a reason for
his action to satisfy his father, so he told him the front yard needed some
cottonwoods. His father said the root section from the trees would not grow
again, but young Earl planted them at home and 50 years later rejoiced in
the towering transplanted cottonwoods that had "growed a plenty."

Earl loved to tinker with machinery and sometimes spent nights out in the
shed fixing up things. He said he did not know if he liked tinkering with
tractors better than planting seeds in the ground.

As a youngster he had to help care for three five-horse teams during the
growing season, so when only big tractors were available, he built his own
small tractor before such vehicles were on the market and had the
reputation of being the first all-tractor farmer in the area. He figured out
ways to do the work quicker, such as hitching two 10-foot drills together,
thus eliminating all of the side draft. All farm machinery and implements
were kept in mint condition and his old Studebaker wagon belied its age
because of the care and repair given it.

In June 1911 Earl and his bride, the former Tillie Lee, were married. She
was the daughter of Atley Lee who lived in the Spring Lake area, having
moved there from southeast of Aberdeen. They had four children: Audrey
(Mrs. Herman Rabenberg) and Eunice (Mrs. (Carl Mueller) both of Britton;
Harold, who was killed on Saipan during World War II and Arlyn, who resides
on the farm.

A portion of his creative imagination was caught on the possibilities of
photography. He was rated a "front row" amateur photographer and would have
done okay as a professional. He figured out a way to make enlargements at
his own place by setting the camera in the attic, using the sky for light
and developing the negatives into some of the neatest big pictures seen
that day. He photographed the social life of the farm of his day and his
shots of night lightning were masterpieces.

This complete farmer also had an orchard of grapes, cherries, apples and
plums to enjoy and share. The Erbe farm had other innovations not usually
found on homesteads. There was the ice well, where ice was stored in winter
to enjoy in the hot summer days and a root cellar, where vegetables and
fruit provided nourishment for the winter.

        Tillie and Earl Erbe

Although Earl was a farmer's farmer with five quarters of land that
produced wheat for the cash crop and pastured a large herd of Herefords, he
enjoyed fishing in season and the Erbe menage was never too busy to pack up
a lunch, lug the motor out of the basement, hitch on the boat trailer and
head for a nearby lake. Sometimes their fishing trips took them to
Minnesota or other waterways.

His community service included serving on the township and school boards.

His one dream of leaving the farm to spend a lot of time fishing never
materialized, though he was sure he could make himself at home most anywhere
and felt it was a smart man who knows when to quit while there is still
time to have some fun. Tillie died June 22, 1953 and Earl died Oct. 22,
1959.

ELDO [DICK] and LILLIE [SEIVERS] ERBE

Eldo, known as Dick to his friends, was born Oct. 1, 1922 on the home farm
seven miles southwest of Bowdle to Alvin and Ruth Erbe. His father died
when Eldo was two, requiring the family to move to Bowdle in 1928. During
his senior year Eldo was co-captain of the Bowdle High School football
team, a sport he especially enjoyed. He served in the Navy 1941-1947,
marrying Henni Former of Amsterdam, Holland. Eldo farmed several years and
worked as a mechanic.

The couple had two children. Gayle Ann, born Sept. 4, 1949, completed
college through a scholarship which included a year of study in India. Glenn
Alvin, born April 2, 1952, works in a glass factory in Hayward, CA. The
family had moved to California where Eldo worked as a mold polisher for
Glass Containers in Antioch many years.

In 1969 Eldo married Lillie (Durham) Seivers whose children are Judy Yapa
and Debra Camitz. He retired in 1981 moving to 3460 Springfield Rd.,
Charlottesville, Virginia 22901.

HERMAN and PEARL ERBE

Herman and Pearl met right at the farm where they lived for about 60 years.
In 1909 Herman's brother Howard and wife Ethel were farming the homestead
of their father John Erbe.

Later Pearl moved with her family to Wisconsin, but soon thereafter Herman
boarded the train and visited her. They were married March 19, 1913 in
Wisconsin. The next day they returned to the farm near Bowdle to plant
their new crop.

Their first baby, Leonard, was born March 5 1914, then Raleigh in 1916,
Willard in 1918, Velma in 1919, Dorothy in 1922, and last of all Margie in
1932. Raising this family of six kept everyone busy.

In 1949 Herman, Pearl, Leonard and Margie took a trip to the West Coast to
visit relatives and friends. This was the only vacation they took during
their married life.

The Erbes lost one daughter, Velma, in 1955. Pearl's parents died in the
1950's and Herman's parents in 1938 and 1940.

        1913 -- Herman and Pearl Erbe -- 1973

Herman and Pearl celebrated their 60th wedding anniversary on the farm and
their 62nd at the Bowdle Nursing Home. Pearl died in October 1975 and
Herman in October 1978. Both had reached the age of 87 when they died.

Of the children, Willard lives on the home place in a trailer. Leonard and
wife Irma live at Custer, Raleigh and wife Martha live at Ipswich, Margie
and husband Chuck Berndt live at Aberdeen and Dorothy and husband Ted Manke
live at Selby. Son Willard remembers the Dirty Thirties: "I remember when
dad had to put up Russian thistles to keep his small herd of cattle. Dad
would hitch up a team of horses on an old horse mower and mow what thistles
and grass he could find. We boys would help rake and haul them in. Then dad
would pitch the thistles and hay up through a small door in the upstairs of
the barn. Dad and Leonard would pitch the thistles up and Raleigh and I
would move them to the back.

"These Russian thistles were kind of salty. The cattle had to eat them
because there was nothing else for them. We lost a number of cattle and cows
through this drought. I think the railroad company bought many of the
cattle, killed them and buried them. We had a couple of hogs which we
fattened up so our family would have a meat supply for the winter months.

LEONARD and IRMA [STICKEL, MOSER] ERBE

Leonard Erbe was born March 5, 1914 at rural Java to Herman and Pearl Erbe.
He married Irma Moser, who was born Feb. 20, 1914, the daughter of John and
Emilie Stickel. Irma was born and educated in the Eureka area, earned a
bachelor's degree and taught in the Tolstoy, Leola, Hosmer and Bowdle
Schools.

Leonard entered the U.S. Army in 1942 during World War II. He served in the
European Theater where he was wounded and received the Purple Heart. He
received his discharge in 1946.

Irma Stickel married Raymond Moser at Eureka June 26, 1938. He was the son
of Mr. and Mrs. Jake Moser of Bowdle. Irma and Raymond lived 4-1/2 years at
Herreid, then a year in Mobridge and moved to Bowdle in 1943. Their son
Roger and daughter Susan were born in Bowdle. Raymond worked for
Montana-Dakota Utilities Co. and was burned electrically Sept. 28, at the
Hosmer Subtation. He died in Eureka Hospital Oct. 10, 1947.

When Leonard and Irma were married in 1951 they moved to the farm west of
Bowdle and lived there until Jan. 13, 1984. Leonard farmed and worked for
the Bowdle Flour Mill and Liteheiser Grain Company. Irma taught in the city
school. In 1984 they retired from the farm and now make their home in
Custer.

Roger Moser, who was born Sept. 20, 1941 at Eureka, is living in Mound City
and is married to Wanda Moos. They have a son Rodney.

Susan Moser, born July 16, 1946 in Aberdeen, is the wife of George Voller.
They live in Powell, WY and have one son Todd.

ALVIN and EDNA [HINTZ] ERLENBUSCH

Alvin Erlenbusch was born at Lowry Jan. 19, 1927 to Daniel and Katherine
(Saur) Erlenbusch. He is the youngest of 10 children and grew up in the
Lowry, Java and Tolstoy areas, where he attended rural and town schools. He
married Edna Hintz of Bowdle on Easter Sunday, March 28, 1948 at the
Congregational Church in Bowdle. Edna was born in Bowdle Aug. 16, 1927 to
John and Magdelena (Merkel) Hintz. She is the youngest of her three
brothers and one sister.

Alvin and Edna's parents were born in Russia. Alvin's mother died Aug. 21,
1953 and his father on Sept. 12, 1967. Three of his brothers and two sisters
have also died. One brother lost his life in action during World War II.
Alvin also served his time in the Armed Forces. Edna's mother died June 13,
1933 when Edna was only five years old. Her father died Nov. 19, 1967. Her
oldest brother, John, died Nov. 30, 1983.

Before Alvin married Edna he was living with his parents at Tolstoy and was
employed by Dakota Transfer as a truck driver. His first place of
employment upon coming to Bowdle was for Ray Commet in his Auto Body Repair
Shop until the building housing the Body Shop was purchased by Dumdei and
Treichel. Alvin continued working there for a short time until he became
employed by J. Kurle & Sons as their mechanic. In 1953 he started work at
the Chevrolet Garage as an auto mechanic and in 1985 he began working for
Erv's Furniture.

        Edna and Alvin Erlenbusch

Edna has been a lifelong Bowdle area resident. She grew up on the family
farm northwest of Bowdle, attended rural grade school and Bowdle High
School. After graduating from high school she took a correspondence course
in bookkeeping and took care of the household chores for her father,
working also for a short time as a nurse's aide in the Bowdle Hospital. She
started her work with the Bowdle Creamery June 30, 1947 as the secretary
and bookkeeper, becoming the manager Aug. 26, 1970, which position she
still holds.

Alvin and Edna also operated roller skating rinks from January 1951 through
1967. Besides providing skating in Bowdle they also traveled to Hosmer and
Selby with their skates, providing the sport for young and old alike.

Alvin and Edna are members of St. John's Evangelical Lutheran Church, where
Alvin is serving his 15th year on the church council. They reside at 4076
7th Avenue in the house that was known as the Bonen house, which they
purchased from Ruben Gehring in 1955.

DIANA ERLENBUSCH

Diana Erlenbusch was born Aug. 3, 1948 in Hoven, the daughter of Herbert
and Eleanora Erlenbusch. Her parents moved to town when she was a small
child. She graduated from Bowdle High School and since 1975 has been
employed in Sioux Falls where she is the insurance manager for the Iseman
Corp.

Saturday nights stand out in her memories of Bowdle when she says,
"Everyone came to town to buy groceries and would sit in cafes and talk
about what happened all week. The kids would walk up and down main street
(until they were old enough to drive up and down main.) It always seemed
like Bowdle was a very large town on Saturday nights. "I always enjoyed
Bowdle and I still like to come home to visit once in a while. It is one of
the nicest looking towns. As you drive through all the towns in South
Dakota, when Bowdle comes, it looks so nice."

HERBERT and ELEANORA [SCHLECHT] ERLENBUSCH

Herbert Erlenbusch was born Jan. 28, 1925 at Lowry. His parents were Mr.
and Mrs. Daniel Erlenbusch, who immigrated to the United States from
Russia. Daniel Erlenbusch was born Nov. 5, 1884 and died Sept. 12, 1967.
His wife was born June 30, 1885 and died Aug. 31, 1953.

Herbert completed the eighth grade and married Eleanora Schlecht June 3,
1947. She was the child of Henry and Magdalena Schlecht who were Java
residents. Henry was born March 30, 1897 and died April 29, 1963. Magdalena
was born Nov. 25, 1900 and is a Bowdle resident.

Herbert was a buttermaker 22 years at Bowdle Creamery. Eleanora is the
janitor for Bowdle State Bank. They had four children.

        Diana, Deb, Eleanora, Herbert Erlenbusch

Diana was born Aug. 3, 1948. She is a manager for Isenman Mobile Insurance
Co. in Sioux Falls. Donna was born Oct. 9, 1949 and died Oct. 28, 1967.
Dale was born and died Dec. 17, 1954. Debra was born Nov. 9, 1958 and is an
elementary teacher at Gregory.

Herbert and Eleanora think of life as having sad and happy times. But the
time most momentous was a trip the family took to Powell, WY, when they saw
Old Faithful in Yellowstone National Park, the Black Hills and Big Horn
Mountains. They said the 1974 trip was the only one their family got to
take together and all had a wonderful time.

WILLIAM and HULDA [SCHLECHT] ERLENBUSCH

William Erlenbusch was born March 27, 1911 at Java. His parents were Daniel
and Kathryn Erlenbusch, who were born in Russia. Daniel was born Nov. 5,
1884 and died Sept. 12, 1961. Kathryn was born June 30, 1885 and died Aug.
31, 1953.

William Erlenbusch married Hulda Schlecht, daughter of Henry and Magdalena
Schlecht April 20, 1945. She was born on a farm southwest of Bowdle. Henry
Schlecht was born at Java March 30, 1897 and died April 30, 1963. Magdalena
was born at Java Nov. 24, 1900 and lives in Bowdle.

William and Hulda received grade school educations and Hulda worked in
different places and homes around Bowdle until she went to Tolstoy to work
in the grocery store. They made Tolstoy their home since their marriage.
They had four children.

Kenneth was born Sept. 27, 1946. He married Sharon Jung and they live at
Pierre where Kenneth is employed with the Federal Highway Department. Their
children are Guy and Joy.

Donald, born Feb. 9, 1948, is associated with Peterson Accountants. He

and Derek.

Mary Ann was born Oct. 25, 1949 and is attending Oahe Adult Education Inc.
at Pierre.

Larry, born March 3, 1964, is a student at Northern State College in
Aberdeen.

        Back: Donald, Larry, Kenneth Front: Mary Ann, Hulda, Bill Erlenbusch

Hulda Erlenbusch writes that when they were first married her husband
worked in Tolstoy for Ed Bieber Implement. In 1949 William and his brother
Herbert built a mechanic shop and started the business of overhauling cars,
tractors and other farm machinery. William's health restricted him from
working after 1960, but he still continued to help out at the garage
selling soft drinks, beer and snacks. It was a favorite place for the men
of the town to congregate and enjoy each other.

Herbert moved to Bowdle in 1953 and William died Aug. 18, 1979. Hulda
continues to make her home in Tolstoy where her children visit her
frequently and she does housework for different families. She keeps busy
with sewing, quilting and other hand work and with her church, St. James
Lutheran.

REV. RICHARD and KATHERINE [STELLJES] FEHLAU

Pastor Richard Fehlau was one of the first Lutheran pastors in Bowdle. He
was born Sept. 12, 1870 at Gombin, Poland. He married Ida Roger who died in
1894 and was buried in Buechler Cemetery. Pastor Fehlau came to the United
States in 1889 and entered Martin Luther Seminary at New Ulm, MN. He
graduated in 1891 and came to Bowdle.

After the death of his wife, his sister Olga Fehlau Jacobs came to the
United States and they lived in the parsonage until Olga married Johannes
Ketterling. Pastor Fehlau married Katherine Stelljes soon after that and
two of their nine children were born in Bowdle.

        Rev. Richard Fehlau

Adelia was born June 1, 1897 in Bowdle. She married Julius Stohs and died
March 21, 1971 at Lawrence KS. Edgar was born Dec. 15, 1898 in Bowdle. He
married Esther Pennekamp and died May 5, 1984 at Portland, ME. He was a
Lutheran pastor and served Redeemer Lutheran Church at Lewiston, ME 47
years.

Irma was born Nov. 17, 1900 at LaCrescent, MN and died in 1905 at
Chunchula, AL. Otto was born May 23, 1902 at Balaton, MN. Uland was born
March 19, 1904 at Balaton, MN and died April 8, 1962 at New Orleans, LA. He
was a pastor and head of the German Department at Tulane University.

Yngurd was born March 24, 1907 at Chunchula, AL. Irmela was born May 10,
1910 at Chunchula, AL. Verona was born June 10, 1913 at Cullman, AL and
Martin was born Oct. 1, 1916 at Cullman, AL.

The Fehlau family left Bowdle the summer of 1900 and the pastor served
congregations in LaCrescent and Balaton, MN before becoming a traveling
missionary for southern Alabama and Mississippi from 1904 to 1912. He
served a congregation in Cullman, AL 1912-1917. He was able to preach in
German, Polish and English and in the fall of 1919 the family moved to
Trenton, NJ to a Polish congregation. He served this parish until his death
in 1929.

CHRISTIAN and JOHANNA [SIEWERT] FEIOCK

Christian "Christ" Feiock with his wife and baby Elisabeth left
Glueckstahl, South Russia for a new life in Butte, NE. He was born Sept.
27, 1876 and left for the United States in 1905. His wife died leaving
Christ a widower with three children: Elisabeth (Schick) born May 7, 1905,
died Dec. 18, 1984; Freda (Lee, Franklin) born Oct. 10, 1907, resides in
Denver, CO and Christian Jr., born Oct. 2, 1909 and died Nov. 24, 1970.

Dec. 11, 1911 Christ married a widow, Johanna (Siewert) Gall in Naper, NE.
She had a son Christian Gall, who was called John to distinguish him from
his stepbrother. To this union was born Ella Johanna (Krueger) Nov. 19,
1912, died Aug. 30, 1964; William Ludwig Oct. 28, 1914, died April 28,
1961; Ruth Regina (Eder) Jan. 14, 1916 and Theodore Gustoph Jan. 18, 1919,
missing in action in 1943 while on submarine duty. In 1945 he was declared
dead and in 1959 a memorial marker was placed in the Black Hills National
Cemetery at Sturgis.

The Christian Feiock family with Theodore only a few months old in the
spring 1919 purchased the Hart farm two and one-half miles northeast of
Bowdle.

Hilda Marie (Rodeen) was the first child born in Bowdle May 26, 1923. She
lives and teaches in Milwaukee, WI. Reuben Fred, born Feb. 11, 1926, lives
in Rapid City. Alvin Albert was born March 28, 1928 and works as a
serviceman for Northwestern Power in Billings, MT. Wanda Lucille (Rodeen)
was born June 15, 1931 and lives in Rocky River, OH. Arnold Otto, born May
7, 1933, served in the army, retired and now lives in Phoenix, AZ.

        Christian and Johanna Feiock

Four of the Feiock sisters attended Northern State College to become
teachers: Ella, Ruth (who has retired in Bowdle,) Hilda and Lucille. Reuben
and Lucille have had successful kidney transplants. Hilda is on dialysis
regularly and awaits a transplant.

Early in the morning the youngsters would rise to milk up to 17 cows by
hand before walking to school. That chore was waiting when they returned so
there was no dallying after school. Much hard work was required to keep the
family clothed and fed. Christ would haul loads of wheat to the Bowdle Mill
in exchange for flour and grits for their yearly supply of food. Grandma
(Regina Feiock) made her home with Christian and brother Peter until her
death in 1925. In the 1930's Christ bought the Weisgram home in Bowdle and
semi-retired. Some of the boys stayed on the farm to continue the work. In
1942 Mrs. Johanna Feiock died following surgery in the Bowdle Hospital
leaving three young children Alvin, Lucille and Arnold to look after
themselves with the help of their father.

Christian contributed articles about the "old country" to the German
newspaper Stadt's Anzeiger or town reporter, published in Bismarck. He
married Emilie Sattler of Germany in the early 1950's. They took the last
of three trips to Germany in 1965 to visit her family. Christian Feiock died
Nov. 12, 1966 at the age of 90 in Rethem, Germany, where he is buried.
Arnold was stationed in Germany at the time and attended the funeral.

WALTER and CLARA [MULHBEIER] FISCHER

Walter was born May 23, 1917 in Leola to Christ and Minnie (Potratz)
Fischer. Clara was born to Jacob and Lulu (Fulker) Muhlbeier Nov. 26, 1919
in Leola.

Clara and Walter were married Nov. 27, 1938 at St. James Lutheran Church in
Leola. They have two children. Robert was born Dec. 14, 1939 at Leola and
Catherine was born Oct. 27, 1953 at Aberdeen. Robert married Marilyn
Weiszhaar Aug. 16, 1959 and in 1961 he graduated from NSC in Aberdeen. They
have two children: Bryan and Brad and reside in Rapid City. Catherine
married Glenn Blumhardt Aug. 9, 1974 and after graduating from SDSU
returned to live in Bowdle.

        Clara and Walter Fischer

After marriage Walter worked at different jobs until 1941 when he became a
truck driver and station attendant for Leola Equity. January 1945 he was
drafted into the Army. He was discharged August 1946 and went back to work
for Leola Equity. In August 1947 he moved to Bowdle to manage the Farmers
Union Oil Co. Clara assisted with some bookkeeping. Walter was manager for
33 years and then accepted the position of assistant manager and bookkeeper
until his retirement.

Walter joined the Bowdle Fire Department in 1948 and served many years as
assistant chief. He was chairman of the Commercial Club and other
committees. In 1984 Walter was Edmunds County American Legion Commander and
1959 he was elected Legionnaire of the Year for District 14. He was elected
chairman of the Bowdle Senior Citizens, has served in various church
offices and committees and on the Northeast South Dakota Energy
Conservation Corporation. Walter also served on the Bowdle Board of
Education for eight years.

Along with raising her family, Clara has remained active in ALCW and
American Legion Auxiliary by serving in offices and on committees. She also
remains active in senior citizens.

CONRAD and HILDEGARTH [SCHLEPP] FIX

Olivia Leona Hildegarth Schlepp was born to Adam and Magdelena Reiner
Schlepp Nov. 25, 1913 in New Leipzig, ND. Her brother Roland was born Sept.
11, 1916 in New Leipzig. These two children enjoyed the life of their
mother for only a few short years as tragedy struck and she died Nov. 3,
1918 during a flu epidemic. In 1919 their father married Eugenia Dubs and
moved to Bowdle where the children attended grade school at two different
country schools.

Hildegarth entered high school in Bowdle. She married Conrad Fix Feb. 11,
1933. Conrad was employed by the Bowdle Creamery 1924-1948. Three children
were born to the couple while they lived in Bowdle. Joan lives in Rapid
City; Wayne and Kay live in Minneapolis.

        Conrad and Hildegarth Fix


In 1948 Conrad moved his family to Spokane, WA where he worked in a
creamery. In 1949 the family moved back to South Dakota and lived in
Aberdeen for 10 years. Conrad worked for Equity Union Creameries and
Hildegarth was manager of Fanny Farmer Candy for several years. In 1959 the
family moved to Minneapolis and Conrad worked for Creamery Package
Manufacturing Company as a service engineer until his retirement Jan. 1,
1984. Hildegarth went to beautician school and operates a beauty salon from
her home. They are currently making their home in Hopkins, MN.

Conrad is the son of Katherine and Thomas Fix. His parents came to this
country from Russia in 1907. His father worked for the Milwaukee Railroad.
Five sons: Joseph, Bernard, Felix, George and Conrad, as well as four
daughters: Julie, Mary, Maggie and Emma were born to the couple. Conrad,
who is 74 and Emma, who is 81, are the lone survivors of this family.
Conrad's mother and father died in 1930.

BERT and ALICE [DIETER] FULLER

Bert F. Fuller was a depot agent for the Milwaukee Railroad in Bowdle
during the early thirties, until he was transferred to the district office
in Aberdeen and elevated to the position of dispatcher. Bert was born May
1, 1893 in Webster to Sam and Rosella Fuller. Bert Fuller died in Aberdeen
May 5, 1965.

Bert married Alice E. Dieter June 6, 1916. She was born March 17, 1894 at
Fairfax, MN to Eugene and Alice L. Dieter. She died Sept. 11, 1959 at
Aberdeen.

Bert and Alice had four children. Lois was born April 2, 1917. She married
a mortician, Glenn O. Nickols. They live in Blooming Prairie, MN and have
two children: Paul and Clennis (Mrs. Kenneth Sandvik.)

Wanda was born Sept. 26, 1920 and is the wife of Douglas Tall. They live in
Robbinsdale, MN and have three children: Marc, Kevin and Kathleen. Douglas
bought a drug store on East Henning and called it Tall s Drug.

Dean Norman was born in June 1922 at Bowdle and died at the age of 2l,2
years in January 1925.

Dorothy was born Feb. 1, 1928 and married John Wagner. They live in Fort
Myers, FL and have six children: Michael, Clifford, Steven, Debby, Douglas
and Jack Jr.

Wanda recalls the time she lived in Bowdle. "I had a great childhood in
Bowdle. In 1936 we celebrated the 50th anniversary of the town. I decorated
my bike and wore my red-plaid shorts outfit in the parade. My older sister
Lois marched and wore an old-fashioned hoop skirt dress that mother had
sewn. Little sister Dot had a red, white and blue dress Mom had sewn and
with her decorated doll buggy, paraded the street.

"My grandmother Alice L. Dieter made her home with Doug and me for many
years. She was a wonderful lady. I am still wearing mended mittens that she
knitted for me while I was in high school 46 years ago. While living in
Bowdle, Gram and Mrs. Mary Boyd were very good friends."

and have three sons: Casey, Collin and Cody.

Tim Geier was born Aug. 25, 1963 and is operating the farm with his father.
Patty, born Jan. 2, 1967, is a 1985 graduate of Bowdle High School.

JOSEPH and ELIZABETH [HARTMAN] GESE

Joseph Gese was born Aug. 10, 1895 in Russia and came with his parents to
the United States in 1900. His future bride, Elizabeth Hartman, was also
born in Russia Feb. 14, 1897 and emigrated with her parents to Bowdle in
1900. Both families settled on farms in the Bowdle area.

Joseph and Elizabeth were married and made their first home on land 3-1/2
miles west of Bowdle on what is now known as the Clarence Schumacher farm,
or Tom O'Malley farm. O'Malley was Bowdle's first saloon keeper. The farm
is just over the line into Walworth County.

Joseph and Elizabeth became disillusioned with farm life in the late 1920's
when grain prices fell so low farmers could hardly finance their operation
and care for a family, so they moved to Hosmer, where Joe purchased a
tavern. In 1930 they returned to Bowdle where Joe again owned a tavern
several years. Then he worked for the highway department, operating a road
grader on Highway 12 and county roads several years. He then owned a cream
station on Main Street until the fall of 1944 when he and Elizabeth took
their family to the Yakima Valley in Washington, living in Prosser.
Elizabeth died Sept. 25, 1967.

        Leo, Bob, Marina, Joe, Larry, Albert Gese

Joe and Elizabeth had four sons and one daughter. Albert attended Northern
State College in Aberdeen and taught in Frederick. While attending Bowdle
High School he also worked in Adolph Braufman's store. Then he went to
Seattle, WA where he attended the University of Washington and worked for
the Boeing Aircraft Corporation until he volunteered for the U.S. Air Force
during World War II. He became a P-38 fighter pilot, stationed in England,
flying missions over Europe until six days after the invasion when he was
shot down in France. Farmers in Normandy kept him hidden from the Germans
2-1/2 months. Freedom came when the British liberated the area.

Albert continued his education after his discharge and received his
master's degree in labor economics from the University of Washington. He
worked for the National Labor Relations Board 10 years and then transferred
to the Federal Mediation Service. He is now retired, but keeps busy with his
own personal arbitration service and golfing. Albert and his first wife
Linda had four sons and one son and one daughter were born to him and his
second wife Terri.

Lawrence Gese was born Feb. 2, 1922. While in high school at Bowdle he
worked for Ernie Merkel at the meat market. During World War II he served
in the U.S. Navy 3-1/2 years, seeing action in the South Pacific, including
the invasion of Leyte in the Philippines. Upon his discharge he married Vera
Geib of Bowdle and took her to Tacoma, WA where he worked as manager of a
grocery store, a segment of a small Tacoma grocery store chain for 35 years.
Larry retired in 1984 and he and Vera spend their winters in Yuma, AZ and
summers in Roy, WA enjoying their six children and grandchildren.

Leo Gese moved west with the family and entered the military service
serving in the South Pacific and then returned to the Seattle area. He
attended the University of Washington and earned a bachelor of arts degree.
He then completed the University of Washington Law School and was admitted
to the Bar. He and his wife Desa raised seven children. One daughter
followed in her father's footsteps and became an attorney. She practices
law in Tacoma, WA and her husband finished law school in 1986.

Leo has been in private law practice 25 years and makes his home in
Edmonds, WA. He also worked for Ernie Merkel while living in Bowdle. Robert
Gese completed his high school education in Washington and then went to the
Los Angeles area where he was employed by Southern California Aircraft
Company. He and his wife Roxie have four children. In 1970 he returned to
Seattle and engaged in the recreation vehicle business. He has since
retired and lives in Tulsa, OK.

Marina Gese traveled west with her parents while young and completed her
education in the Yakima Valley area. She attended the Seattle University,
receiving a degree as an X-ray technician. After some years in California
she returned to the Seattle area, where she married Leo Petosa. He is in
the grocery business and Marina works part-time as a vacation replacement.

Leo Gese writes that his family expects to celebrate the Centennial in
Bowdle and his father Joe, now 90 years old, plans to be here to greet old
friends.

LAWRENCE and VERA [GEIB] GESE

Lawrence Gese writes of his life as follows: "Vera Geib and I were married
in 1946 while I was still in the Navy. I spent 3-1/2 years in the South
Pacific in the New Guinea Islands. My parents (Mr. and Mrs. Joe Gese) had
lived in Bowdle and I worked for Ernest Merkel in his store while I was in
high School. Vera Geib and I were married in 1946 while I was still in the
service.

"When the war was over we went to Tacoma, WA where I managed a super market
39 years. Vera was employed by an airlines catering service. We both
retired when I was 60 years old.

"We had six sons Lovell, Joe, Mike, Ron, Tim and John and now that they are
on their own, Vera and I have moved to a small town (Roy, WA) about 25
miles south of Tacoma. We live on a small five acre farm and man it nicely.

        Lawrence Gese Family Lovell, Joe, Mike, Lawrence, Vera, Jim, John,
        Ron

"We enjoy 17 grandchildren and became great grandparents in August 1985. We
spend the winters in Yuma, AZ and will be going back there in October.
Herewith is my address so that anyone from Bowdle may find us at 1152
Magnolia Avenue, Yuma, AZ 85364."

HENRY and KATHERINE [SCHERBENSKI] GIEDT

Henry Giedt was born to John and Mary Giedt in Naper, NE Nov. 10, 1901. In
1919 his family moved to the Bowdle area and farmed south of town. Henry
married Katherine Scherbenski, daughter of Christian and Christina (Limle),
Oct. 20, 1921 in Bowdle. They made their first home on a farm near Tolstoy
where they farmed until 1923 and moved to another farm south of Bowdle in
Odessa Township.

        Katherine and Henry Giedt

The couple retired and moved to Bowdle in 1970. Mr. Giedt was an Edmunds
County Commissioner for 12 years. He was a member of the church council,
served on the Odessa Township Board Farmers Elevator of Bowdle and the
first Hospital Board. Mrs. Giedt worked as a nurse's aide at the Bowdle
Nursing Home and Bowdle Hospital. Five children were born to this union.
Deloris Kay died in infancy, Dorothy (Mrs. Ernest Mertz) of Bowdle and her
children Ernest, Ruth, Paul, Dean, Mike and Garry; Eloise (Mrs. Eugene
Huber) of Napa, CA and children Marsha, Cecil, Don and Jon; Ward lives in
California and Lester (Dick) married Joyce Merkel, lives in Bowdle and
their children are Steve and Randy.

Completing this family are 12 grandchildren and 16 great-grandchildren.

LESTER and JOYCE [MERKEL] GIEDT

Lester (Dick) is the son of Henry and Katherine Giedt. He married Joyce,
daughter of Ernest and Lola Merkel. They live on a farm 2-1/2 miles south of
Bowdle.

Besides being a farmer Dick was active with the Bowdle Jaycees, served on
the Selective Service Board in Edmunds County and works at the Sales Barn
in Bowdle. Dick is also well-known for his auction and square dance
calling. Joyce has been the City Finance Officer since 1977.

They have two children. Steven married Lori Rudnick and lives at Groton. He
is employed with a feed company in North Dakota. Randy married Leigh Ann
Garness and they live in St. Peters, MO where he is in the Marine Corp.

THEODORE [TED] and DOROTHY [DERHAM] GIEDT

Theodore J. Giedt was born June 21, 1912 in Naper, NE the son of John and
Mary (Hauf) Giedt. John Giedt was born in Danzig, Germany in 1870 and died
in 1912. His wife Mary was born in Russia in 1870 and died in 1951.

Ted attended Northern State College in Aberdeen. He married Dorothy M.
Derham Oct. 25, 1947. She was born Oct. 9, 1920 at Portland, OR, the
daughter of Peter and Dorothy (St. Marie) Derham of Pocatello, ID. Mr.
Derham was born Oct. 19, 1891. Mrs. Derham was born Nov. 11, 1900 and died
Sept. 7, 1961. Dorothy attended Glendale College in California.

Ted and Dorothy have four children. Susan was born Oct. 22, 1948 and is the
wife of Harvey Leidholt of Bowdle. They have three sons Thomas, Douglas and
Michael.

Nanci was born June 28, 1952 and is the wife of Mark Sanchez. They have a
daughter Sarri Ann. Nanci is a teacher.

Lori (Giedt) Sanchez was born April 28, 1954 and has a daughter Laurel
Terese. Lori is a nurse.

Jeffery Giedt was born Aug. 23, 1958 and is an electrician. All of the
Giedt children were born in Los Angeles and live there with the exception of
Susan Leidholt, who lives in Bowdle.

Theodore Giedt moved to Los Angeles in June 1937. August 1942 he entered
the U.S. Army and spent three years in the European Theater of Operation.
After his discharge Ted (as he is called) went to work for the Los Angeles
Department of Water and Power, where he spent 35 years before retiring as
chief clerk of the aqueduct system. This job required his supervision of
all clerical employees, not only of Los Angeles, but in Mojave, Lone Pine
and Bishop, CA.

When Ted's oldest child Susan graduated from Hoover High School at Glendale
in 1966, the family took a trip back to the Midwest where they met all the
Giedt family relatives. They enjoyed the experience of being in a small
town and on the farm since they were all "city kids." The following summer
Susan, after a year at Glendale College, went back to Bowdle to be in the
wedding party of her cousin Ruth Mertz and liked it so well she got a job
and stayed. Susan met and married Harvey Leidholt and still lives in Bowdle.

BERKELEY and HELEN [SANTOS] GISI

Berkeley (more commonly known as Rocky) was born in Hoven in 1951 and
raised on a farm 3-1/2 miles west of Hosmer. He is the son of Benedict
(born October 1922) and Maggie (born March 21 1924) Gisi. Rocky attended
the Hosmer schools.

After graduation Rocky reminisces, "I moved to Aberdeen to work at the
Flame Cafe until 1970, at which time I was called for active duty in the
military service. I entered the Air Force June 1970 and spent six weeks of
basic training at Lackland AFB, Texas and nine weeks of electrical
technician training at Sheppard AFB, Texas. In October 1970 I was sent to
Minot AFB, ND and was stationed there until January 1973. I was responsible
for all electrical services at (5) Minute Man Missile sites which manned
(10) missiles per site.

        Helen, Michelle, Bruce, Berkeley Gisi

In February 1973 I received orders for overseas duty at Clark AFB,
Philippines until June 1974. After being discharged from military service,
I took a few months vacation and traveled from San Francisco to Seattle and
then a long interesting trip to Columbus, OH and back.

"I started employment as electrician at Bowdle Hardware in November 1974. I
also learned plumbing, heating and backhoe operations until I quit in April
1981. I got married in Bowdle in June 1975 to Helen Santos, whom I met in
the Philippine Islands. She is the daughter of Federico (born November
1920, died in 1961) and Iluminada (born November 1921) Santos. We have two
children. Michelle was born Feb. 7, 1976. Bruce was born July 19, 1980.

"Since May 1981 my partner Ward Oster and I have a successful business
doing electrical, plumbing, heating, digging, trenching and septic tank
pumping. Our business name is G & O Electrical & Plumbing.

PETER and ELIZABETH [GEIER] GLATT

Peter Glatt was born in 1889 at Zeeland, ND where he grew to manhood. He
farmed with oxen, as did all the other settlers. However, as soon as money
was available he purchased a team of horses.

Oct. 30, 1910 he married Elizabeth Geier and 11 children were born to them.
Their first child Frank arrived in 1912 followed by Magdalena, Elizabeth,
Ann Marie, John, Clara, Helen, Joe, Rose, Wendlin and James.

        Elizabeth and Peter Glatt

In 1919 Peter moved his family to the Bowdle area where they lived until
1923, when they moved across the Missouri River, seven miles northwest of
Trail City. In 1936 they returned to Bowdle where Peter farmed until 1944
when they moved into town and Peter took a job as a Milwaukee Railroad
section worker. In 1955 the Glatts moved to Hosmer with their son Frank.

Peter died May 1936. His wife died November 1967 and their son Frank died
Feb. 5. 1984.

GOTTLOB and CHRISTINA [LANGE] GOETTLING

Gottlob Goettling was born in Beinstein, Germany June 8, 1865. He was 14
years old when they came to America. From New York City they went to New
Dundee, Ontario, Canada where they found a small farm and settled.

In 1886 Gottlob, his brother August and wife came to South Dakota to take
up a homestead, but things went so adversely for August and his wife that
they became discouraged and left the Dakota Territory, ending up in Tacoma,
WA.

Gottlob stayed in South Dakota. He worked on farms near Leola and Ipswich.
Later he went to Aberdeen and worked on the railroad which was being built
to Ipswich and in October 1886 it had reached Bowdle.

Gottlob was united in marriage with Christina Lange Dec. 3, 1889. She also
homesteaded with her father in Odessa Township. Gottlob and Christina built
their house of sod and all their children were born in the same sod house.
They were William, Oscar, Paul, Gertrude, Walther, Rudolph and Theodore.

Gottlob held school and township offices many years. He was county assessor
in Edmunds County and the only auctioneer in Bowdle and surrounding
territory for many years. He died Oct. 5, 1958. Christina died in 1932 and
William died in 1942.

OSCAR and MARGARET [STINSON] GOETTLING

Oscar Julius Goettling was born Aug. 24, 1895 to Gottlob and Christine
(Lang) Goettling in Odessa Township south of Bowdle.

Oscar attended rural school and farmed with his parents. He joined the U.S.
Army during World War I June 24, 1918 and served in France. Following his
discharge he returned to the Bowdle area.

Oscar married Margaret Stinson Sept. 1, 1928 in Canton. She was the
daughter of Thomas A. and Margaret E. (Craney) Stinson of Clark.

The Goettlings lived on the farm four miles south of Bowdle all their
lives. Their daughter Geraldine was born Jan. 27, 1934. She became the wife
of George Heilman and they now operate the Goettling farm.

Oscar Goettling died Nov. 13, 1983 and is buried in Black Hills National
Cemetery in Sturgis.

This picture was taken at Meakins Park on Oscar's 80th birthday in 1975 and
shows Oscar and Margaret with their daughter Geraldine and her husband
George and their children.

PAUL E. and BERTHA [NICKISCH] GOETTLING

Paul E. Goettling was born April 22, 1897 in Bowdle. His father Gottlob was
born in Germany June 8, 1865 and he died Oct. 5, 1958. Paul's mother
Christina was born in Russia Dec. 6, 1865 and died Dec. 15, 1932. Paul
attended the York (NE) College of Business and Kansas City (MO) Electrical
College.

        Doris, Paul, Bertha, Alice Goettling

Paul married Bertha Nickisch Jan. 12, 1922. Her parents were A.G. and Anna
Nickisch, both born in Germany. George was born Jan. 14, 1856 and died Nov.
25, 1920. Anna was born July 25, 1863 and died in April 1935.

Bertha Goettling was born in Marion Oct. 8, 1898 and came to Bowdle with
her family when she was four. Her father bought land a half mile from town
from Dr. Wm. Edwards. She received her education from Bowdle and attended
the Snow School of Dressmaking in Aberdeen.

Paul and Bertha have two daughters. Doris Ann was born May 8, 1926. She was
employed at the Bowdle Post Office and is the wife of Vincent Hoven, a
local rancher. They have two children. Corrine is a registered pharmacist
who lives with her family in Anchorage, Alaska. Perry is a college student.

Alice Naemi Goettling was born Feb. 7, 1933, is married to John Iler and
lives in Aberdeen where she is a secretary for the Social Security
Administration.

Paul E. Goettling managed the first City Liquor Store, a bottle shop, for
eight years. During that time the city took out all the old wooden
sidewalks, put in cement walks and black-topped the streets. In 1945 Paul
was appointed Chief of Police and Street Commissioner until 1962 when he
retired.

While a young lady Bertha accompanied her parents and brothers Nathaniel
and Theodore to Europe where they toured the continent one summer from May
to September. For several years she clerked in Braufman's store and the
Bowdle Mercantile Co., which was located where G & O Electrical & Plumbing
is now. During World War II she was appointed clerk in the Bowdle Post
Office and held that position 25 years.

Paul and Bertha have lived through two world wars, the Korean and Vietnam
wars. They have been married 62 years, have done some traveling and
visited a number of the states and Canada, but still think South Dakota is
the best state in the union.

GAYLON and CONNIE [BUECHLER] GOETZ

The phrase "Down on the Farm" became a reality as the Goetz family moved in
1978 from Aberdeen to the Buechler homestead two miles northwest of Bowdle
(the former Otto Buechler farm.) According to records this farm will be a
Centurion farm in 2001.

Gaylon, born Sept. 10, 1943 at Eureka, is the son of Oscar and Stella
(Jurief) Goetz. He grew to adulthood on a farm northeast of Java and
attended Java schools.

Gaylon married Connie July 18, 1965 at Redeemer Lutheran Church in Bowdle.
They were the first couple to be married in that church.

Connie, daughter of Otto and Gertrude (Bentz) Buechler, was born June 26,
1942 at Bowdle. Although Connie lived in Edmunds County she attended the
rural Buechler School in Walworth County where the credit to her education
was given to the only two instructors she had, Mr. I.A. Stoecker and Miss
Arlene Blumhardt of Bowdle. Connie continued her education graduating from
Northwestern Lutheran Academy at Mobridge and Northern State College at
Aberdeen.

        Connie, Selena, Jarrod, Gaylon Goetz

After marriage Gaylon and Connie lived in Mandan, ND and later moved to
Aberdeen where the couple lived many years with Connie teaching in the
elementary schools and Gaylon self-employed as a trucker, welder and seed
salesman.

Both their children were born in Aberdeen. Selena Gail was born Aug. 1,
1970 and Jarrod Gaylon Nov. 20, 1976. They are students in the Bowdle
School System and active members of the Busy Bowdle Stars 4-H Club.

The Goetz family continues to farm specializing in a sheep operation and
grain farming. Gaylon was one of the first few farmers to raise sunflowers
in this area.

PETE and RUTH [JOHNSON] GOLDADE

ELMER and MARLENE [KALMBACH] GREGER

Elmer Greger, son of John and Emma (Lemley) Greger, was born on his parents
farm northwest of Bowdle. Elmer, his brother Edward and sisters Verna and
Agnes went to the country school, walking the mile from home most of the
time and wintertime meant nearly frozen toes and fingers by the time they
arrived at school.

On occasion they rode a horse and carried their lunch in a syrup pail.
There were no fancy lunch buckets then and no modern conveniences such as
running water and electricity until years later. During the summer the
children were required to pick up dry cow chips which were stored to be used
in the cook stove in winter and to help heat the house.

Farming and milking were done by horses, not tractors and no milking
machines, that was done by hand. The milker was lucky if the cow didn't
decide to put her foot into the milking pail. Trips to town were few and
far between and winter was the time the family stayed at home.

Elmer served in the U.S. Army during the Korean War, taking his training in
Texas. After receiving his honorable discharge in 1954, he returned to the
farm to help his parents.

Elmer and Marlene M. Kalmbach were married in 1956. She is the daughter of
Jacob and Ella (Neumiller) Kalmbach of Mobridge and Akaska area. They made
their home on one of John Greger's farms. Their children are Kenneth Elmer,
born in 1956; Arlin Ray, born in 1958; Lonnie Lyle, born July 24, 1961;
Maryann Kay, born Feb. 16, 1968 and Darren Duane, born Dec. 22, 1969.

Elmer Greger bought the Balzer Schuh farm in 1959, moving his family
there in February. Assisted by Marlene, they milked cows, planted and
harvested corn, grain, hay and also raised stock cows and calves.

June 24, 1983 Elmer and Marlene and their two youngest children moved into
Bowdle. Their son Kenneth graduated from Java and attended SDSU at
Brookings. He married Virginia Heesch. They have a son Christopher. Kenneth
and his family returned to Bowdle in June 1983 to live on the family farm.

Arlin graduated from Java and the School of Science in Wahpeton, ND. He
lives in Ogunquit, Maine.

Lonnie married Lois Reimer. They live in Mobridge and have three children:
Leo, Matthew and Jamie Lynn.

Maryann is a senior at Bowdle High School and Darren is a sophomore.

        Elmer and Marlene Greger

        Lois and Lonnie Greger, Jamie, Leo, Matthew

        Kenneth and Virginia Greger and son Christopher

        Maryann and Darren Greger

JOHN and EMMA [LEMLEY] GREGER

Martin Greger and his wife Carolina were the first generations of Gregers
to live on the farm 5 miles west and 1-1/2 north of Bowdle. Their family
included several children of whom John was the one to follow in their
footsteps. He became a farmer and lived on the Martin Greger farm.

John married Emma Lemley of Java Nov. 13, 1925. They made their home on the

Emma continues to make her home there.

        Emma and John Greger

BALDASER and GRACE [BLOSSEY] GRISMER

Aberdeen.

Marie was the child of William F. and Lucy Nehl Blossey. William was born

Edmunds County June 30, 1896 and died Oct. 11, 1936.

married Floyd Hoerner, a farm laborer. Their children are Mark, Jo Ann,
