BENJAMIN and BARBARA [REINBOLD] GRISMER

Benjamin, born Feb. 9, 1881 in Russia, was the son of Jacob and Elizabeth
(Ochs) Grismer. He married Barbara Reinbold. She was the daughter of
Baldaser and Elizabeth Mardian Reinbold, who were born in Baden, Germany.
Barbara was born Feb. 2, 1886 in Edmunds County.

The family lived six miles north and four east of Bowdle. They worked with
oxen. Often they reminisced how they carried feed to the oxen with baskets.

Benjamin and Barbara were blessed with nine children: Frank B., Margaret
P., Theresa R., Jacob, Agnes, Elizabeth A., Baldaser P., Sussie J. and
Edward E.

FRANK and MARLYN [SCHMIDT] GRISMER

Frank was born on a farm nine miles northeast of Bowdle March 21, 1936 to
Frank B. and Magdalena (Fix) Grismer. He attended rural school near their
farm, riding horseback to-and-from school. In winter months he did a lot of
trapping. He helped his parents with farm work and had some livestock of his
own. Frank also did work for neighbors, mainly his uncles.

Marlyn was born at Tolstoy on the family farm of her parents George T. and
Lucille (Lunders) Schmidt Sept. 22, 1937. Her parents still own that farm.
Marlyn attended St. Anthony's Catholic School at Hoven and graduated
from Hoven High School in May 1956.

Frank and Marlyn were married June 26, 1956 at St. Anthony's Catholic
Church in Hoven by the Rev. William L. Schmitt. They farmed a year with her
parents and then rented a farm north of Bowdle for a year. The farm was
sold and they moved to Bowdle where they went into the Watkins business.
Frank did custom feed grinding, along with his selling Watkins feed. Frank
hired his brother Leo to help with the feed grinding for a few years. Frank
and Marlyn sold feed and household products 1960-1966 and then bought his
parents farm in November 1966. Frank's parents moved into the house in
Bowdle. Frank and Marlyn continued to sell Watkins products on the farm for
a short time and were a farm dealership for Furst McNess a number of years.

        Back: Carol Ann, Allan, Mary Ann Front: Gary, Frank, Marlyn, Amy
        Grismer

While in the Watkins business they were the USA Champion Salesmen of the
week in 1966, with sales of $9,192 for a week. They also won District
Championship trophies 1962-1966 for each year in sales.

After 16 years they sold the farm to Walter and Mary Grismer of Hosmer and
moved to Bowdle again and Frank buys and sells cattle. Marlyn works at
Bowdle Hospital and Bowdle Nursing Home. Before moving to the farm she held
the office of treasurer for the city of Bowdle.

They have five children. Mary Ann lives at Hettinger, ND and is attending
Dickinson State College, studying for her bachelor's degree in mathematics
in secondary education. Carol Ann is at Tucson, AZ where she is studying a
surgical technician's course. Allan, Amy Lynn and Gary are attending school
at Bowdle. The couple also has one grandchild.

CHRIST and CLARA [GUNDERT] GROSS

Christ C. Gross (better known as C.C.) like the rest of his brothers and
sisters, (except Martin) was born in Russia coming to America at age 5-1/2
with his parents, Christian and Katherine Gross. The family homesteaded
north of Bowdle.

In 1906 Christ came to Bowdle to work with his brothers John C. and Henry
C. in the implement business. In 1908 he went to work at First State Bank,
which was opened the previous year by Jacob Gundert and John C. Gross. In
1909 the Gross Brothers purchased the H.A. Mason Store which had gone
bankrupt due to the railroad extending to Mobridge. Thus cutting down the
trade territory. Christ continued to work in the store as manager of the
shoe and clothing department until his retirement.

In 1912 Christ Gross married Clara Gundert, a native of Menno. She had
moved to Bowdle with her parents at an early age. Clara was the second
Gundert child to marry into the Gross family. Her sister Lydia was the
bride of John C. Gross. In later years Martha, the youngest sister, married
Martin C. Gross.

Christ and Clara Gross were active in community and church affairs all the
years they lived in Bowdle. They were the parents of four sons. Donald is
deceased, Norman is a banker in Yankton, Gordon died while in high school,
a victim of an athletic accident and Erv is in business in Bowdle.

Christ and Clara celebrated their 50th wedding anniversary in June 1962.
Christ died in 1967 and Clara died in 1984.

CHRISTIAN and KATHERINE [LAPP] GROSS

Christian Gross, his mother and three brothers migrated from South Russia
on or about April 10, 1889. They set out searching for land and Christian,
being the oldest of the family and which was the custom, acted as the head
of the family.

They located a tract of land near the county line between McPherson and
Edmunds counties, finding just what they wanted, they set out filing on that
land. Each one of the brothers, including Grandma, filed on three quarters.

        Back: Henry, John, Martin, Rose, Katherine Front: Christ,
        Christian, Katherine Gross

Originally the Grosses were Lutheran, but after giving much thorough
consideration, they thought the Congregational Society was best to join.
They built a frame church, which they called the Gross Church. Not having a
minister Christian would read the sermon.

Christian died July 25, 1925 and the other brothers died at Eureka.

ERVIN and LAVERNE [THOMMEN] GROSS

Ervin, son of Christian C. and Clara Gross, was born in Bowdle, graduated
from high school in 1940 and attended Yankton College and University of
Minnesota before he was called into the Armed Forces in 1943. He was taken
a prisoner by the German Army during the Battle of the Bulge.

Ervin married LaVeme (Ole) Thommen in 1948. They had five daughters. Cathy
(Mrs. John Bennett) lives in Illinois. They have one son. Margaret married
Bill Bobby and they live in Bowdle with their three sons. Carmen married
Steve Barbera and they live in Ohio with their two children. Ann Gross
attends South Dakota State University at Brookings and Donald Gross attends
the University of South Dakota at Vermillion. Christy Gross was killed in
1974 at age 19.

Erv's father and uncles dissolved the Gross Brothers partnership in 1955,
which was organized in 1909. Erv's brother Donald became manager of Gross
Bros. Super Valu and Fumiture Store, serving in that capacity 1946-1951,
when Erv succeeded him. The Super Valu Store was sold to Ozzie and LaVaughn
Schlepp Jan. 1, 1966 and Erv bought the Furniture Department.

The furniture store was on the ground floor and Erv and Ole have been in
business in Bowdle for 35 years. Erv has served as president of the
Commercial Club, was a member of Bowdle School Board and Volunteer Fire
Department. He also sponsored amateur basketball teams and their success is
attested by the 24-plus trophies on display in the store. Erv says his only
trouble is he has run out of basketball players.

COL. GARDNER and MARIE [CULHANE] GROSS

Gardner Baker Gross was born Nov. 6, 1907 at Bowdle to John and Lydia
(Gundert) Gross, both deceased. Gardner graduated from Bowdle and earned his
bachelor of science degree in 1932 from South Dakota State University at
Brookings.

While at the University he married Marie Culhane of Elkton Sept. 11, 1932.
He taught school two years at Veblen and the next five years he worked as
an auditor for the U.S. Department of Agriculture at Lincoln, NE.

In 1940 he joined the U.S. Army as a 2nd Lieutenant and served with the 2nd
Infantry Division at Fort Sam Houston, TX. After graduating from Infantry
School at Ft. Benning, GA he joined the 45th Infantry Regiment in the
Philippine Islands. He was divisional supply officer at the time of the
fall of Bataan, early in World War II. He was taken prisoner by the
Japanese, was a survivor of two Japanese "Hell Ships" and the Bataan Death
March. He was in a Japanese prison camp 3-1/2 years. After spending 7
months in an Army hospital Major Gross was reassigned to duty with the U.S.
Constabulary in Occupied Germany where he spent three years. He returned in
1940 and attended Air Command and Staff College at Maxwell Air Force Base
in Montgomery, AL. Upon graduating he was reassigned to the Second Armored
Division at Fort Hood, TX where he commanded the 12th Armored Infantry
Battalion and Combat Command A. At this time he was promoted to full
Colonel.

His last assignment was Senior Army Advisor to the National Guard and ROTC
with the Louisiana Military District, headquartered in New Orleans, LA. He
retired in 1953 having received many service medals. After his retirement
he worked towards a doctorate of psychology degree at Trinity College in
San Antonio, TX.

When his father died Col. Gross returned to Bowdle where he and his
brother, attorney Robert Gross of Ipswich assumed management and ownership
of Bowdle State Bank and Gardner became bank president in 1962.

Gardner was a great community leader and was instrumental in building the
present Bowdle Hospital, Bowdle State Bank, Bowdle Nursing Home and the
elementary addition to the school. He also ramrodded Bowdle's 75th Diamond
Jubilee in 1961. Col. Gross died Nov. 27, 1970 at Keesler Air Force Base in
Biloxi, MS.

        Marie and Col. Gardner Gross

Marie Gross now lives in Portales, NM near her sister Mrs. Gordon Thomas.
Old-timers will recognize Gordon as the son of Levi Thomas of Ipswich who
had the record for the longest years of service to the county. Levi held
the position of County Clerk of Courts more than 20 years.

Gardner and Marie had two sons. John Gardner married June Bieber at Bowdle.
Their children are Melody Schulte, John G. Gross II, Frederick, Eric, and
Ingrid, all of whom were born while their parents lived in Bowdle. The
family now lives in Iowa City, IA.

James Gordon Gross married Glenna Skitworth of Ft. Isabel, TX in 1963. They
make their home in Alamogordo, NM. Their children are Cary, Greg and
Kimberly.

HENRY C. and ELSIE [LUECK] GROSS

Henry C. Gross was born in Glueckstahl, South Russia near the Neister River
in 1879. At age nine he came with his parents to the United States. Mr. and
Mrs. Christian C. Gross homesteaded 12 miles north of Bowdle in 1889, where
Henry attended the district school. He also attended Redfield College and
Sioux Falls Business College.

Shortly after the turn of the century Henry and his brother John C. opened
an implement, harness and feed store in Selby, which Henry operated until
its sale a few years later. He then worked at the bank in Selby and in 1908
came to Bowdle where he entered the banking business. He married Elsie
Lueck of Ripon, WI in 1909.

Henry was in the banking business 53 years and served as president of the
Bowdle State Bank from 1947 to 1961, when he retired. He was national
treasurer of the Congregational Church several terms. Mr. and Mrs. Gross
were devout members of the Congregational Church.

Henry and Elsie had four children. Calvin died in Tiyunga, CA March 5, 1983
at the age of 70. He was a cancer victim.

Dr. Guilford Gross served as dean of the College of Pharmacy at SDSU in
Brookings many years until his retirement in 1981. In recognition of his
service the new pharmacy building bears his name. Guil and his wife Frances
spend their summers in Brookings and winters in Arizona.

Doris Gross Belcher lives in Memphis, TN. A home economics major, she works
full-time doing free lance food commercials.

Mahlon Gross and his wife Arelene reside in Bowdle where Mahlon has been
employed at the Bowdle State Bank more than 30 years, serving in many
official capacities.

After Henry retired from the bank, he continued to serve the public from
his home as advisor until his death Dec. 25, 1969 at the age of 90. Mrs.
Gross continued to live in Bowdle until she died Jan. 20, 1976 at the age
of 87.

JACOB and MAGDALENA [BUECHLER] GROSS

Jacob Gross came to America from Glueckstahl, South Russia with his parents
Jacob Sr. and Louise Gross in 1885. They homesteaded eight miles south of
Bowdle.

Magdalena Buechler came to America from Glueckstahl, South Russia with her
parents Michael and Magdalena (Herman) Buechler in 1878 when she was five
years old. They made their home on a homestead seven miles northwest of
Bowdle, where they built a sod house.

        Jacob and Magdalena Gross

Jacob and Magdalena were married Dec. 6, 1902 and made their home on a farm
eight miles southwest of Bowdle. Nine children were born to this union,
seven died in infancy. Hilda Gross was born June 11, 1911 and died Oct. 6,
1932. Their surviving child is Mrs. Alvin (Erna) Reuer of Bowdle.

Jacob Gross and his family left the farm in 1919 and moved into Bowdle
where he went into the oil business. His White Eagle Bulk Service station
was located where the Farmers Union Oil Co. (Cenex) is now. Jacob was in
partnership with his brother George.

Jacob died Sept. 13, 1956 and Magdalena died June 6, 1977.

JOHN A. and BARBARA [STAHLICKER] GROSS

John was born to Christian G. and Katherine (Muller) Grosz May 17, 1893 on
their farm home south of Bowdle. He grew up and farmed this homestead.

Barbara was born in Russia Jan. 26, 1895 to Peter and Katherine Stahlicker.
When the family came to this country they homesteaded near Hoven.

John and Barbara were married in 1915 and shared their married life
together 64 years. Together they started their life with a deep commitment
to God to serve Him all the days of their lives.

        Back: Victor, LeRoy, Norman, Milton Front: John, Regina, Barbara
        Gross

After John's parents retired, he and Barbara took over the homestead place.
They farmed until 1945 when they moved to Bowdle and their son Norman
continued to farm. John was employed with Northwest Mutual Insurance of
Eureka as an agent.

The couple was blessed with four sons and a daughter. Milton married Mary
Hopfinger. They have six children, live in Bowdle and are retired.

LeRoy Gross married Edna Lutz. They live in Watertown, WI; are in the

Norman Gross is married to Lenora Barth. They have three children, live in

pastor and they have three children.

Regina Gross married James Breitling and live in Ipswich. They have six
children.

John Gross died Aug. 4, 1979. Barbara still lives in her home at Bowdle.
She has one of the largest gardens in town which she still tends and does
her own housekeeping. She celebrated her 90th birthday in January 1985.

MAHLON H. and ARELENE [SCHLEPP] GROSS

Mahlon H. Gross, son of Henry C. and Elsie Gross, was born Sept. 7, 1926 in
Bowdle. After graduating from Bowdle he served in the U.S. Navy two years
and then attended SDSU at Brookings, majoring in forestry and attended the
Milwaukee School of Engineering.

He worked as a carpenter for J.K. Kurle & Sons before following his
father's footsteps at the Bowdle State Bank. He progressed from teller to
cashier and is presently a vice-president of the bank, secretary of the
board of directors and manager of Gross Insurance Agency.

Mahlon married Arelene Schlepp, daughter of John W. and Lena Schlepp, in
Bowdle March 21 1954. Mahlon and Arelene are members of the Bowdle State

American Legion Post and secretary-treasurer of Prairie View Housing Inc.

        Mahlon and Arelene Gross

They are members of the United Methodist Church where Mahlon has served as
a trustee and auditor and Arelene is on the pastor-parish and communion
committees, secretary of the administrative board and treasurer of the
women's fellowship.

They have two sons. Timothy was born Nov. 24, 1958 and Thomas Dec. 7, 1959.
Both have earned their bachelor of science degrees at Northern State
College in Aberdeen. Timothy is a diversion program coordinator at the Boys

is a layout artist for the Aberdeen American News and a self-employed
commissioned artist. He is a very talented person and has had one-man

open house events.

MARTIN C. and MARTHA [GUNDERT] GROSS

Martin C. was the son of Christian and Katherine (Lapp) Gross. Martin was
born in McPherson County, attended grade school and graduated from Selby
High School. He continued his education at Aberdeen Business College. He
entered World War I in 1918 and was stationed in France.

        Martin and Martha Gross

Martin was a very civic minded person. He was in business with his brothers
in the Gross Bros. Department Store until his death in May 1939.

Martin was remembered by the community for owning a blue pickup known as
"The Blue Bird." This vehicle was used to haul much of the freight for the
store but Martin, having a special heart for the school children, would
often haul the cheer leaders or students to the ball games.

Martin married Martha Gundert in September 1917. She was born in Menno. Her
parents moved to Tolstoy and Hosmer where she attended school.

Martin and Martha had a daughter LaVaughn, who married Oswald (Ozzie)
Schlepp. Martha Gross died Oct. 8, 1970.

MILTON and MARY [HOPFINGER] GROSS

CHRISTIAN G. and KATHERINE [MULLER] GROSZ

Christian G. Grosz, at the age of 20, migrated from Russia to the United
States, making his first home in Menno in 1884. Two years later he came to
Bowdle where he filed on a homestead six miles south of Bowdle May 1, 1886.

In 1888 he was united in marriage to Katherine Muller of Eureka, to which
union 12 children were born.

Christian retired from the farm in 1915 which he homesteaded and moved to
Bowdle where he resided until his death May 10, 1940. He was a lifetime
member of German Congregational Church.

LESTER and MARCELLA [MASHEK] GROSZ

Lester Grosz was born Jan. 19, 1923 in Bowdle, the son of Fred G. and
Theodosia Grosz. He was a graduate of Bowdle, Mankato Business College and
University of Wisconsin School of Banking.

Fred Grosz was born July 6, 1894 in Hillsview and died Dec. 26, 1959 in
Bowdle. He was a public spirited citizen of the community, serving as city
auditor, an officer of the Bowdle State Bank for many years and in many
ways contributed to the progress of the city.

Mrs. Grosz was a graduate of the Canadian Conservatory of Music in Boston,
MA and taught piano to many Bowdle young people for more than 50 years. She
contributed in many ways to the community through her music by playing for
church, weddings, funerals and other public functions. Theo Grosz was born
Sept. 2, 1895 in Ipswich and died in Marshall, MN Jan. 2, 1983.

Lester married Marcella Mashek May 16, 1944. She was the daughter of Edward
and Rosie Mashek. Edward was born Sept. 14, 1880 in Spillville, IA. He was
employed by the Milwaukee Railroad in Bowdle. Rosie Mashek was born in
Odessa, Russia Dec. 26, 1895. She operated a cafe in Bowdle for several
years. Ed died July 23, 1948 and Rosie died Oct. 30, 1971. Marcella
graduated from Bowdle.

Mr. and Mrs. Lester Grosz presently live at 508 Central Ave., Marshall, MN.
He followed his father's footsteps in his banking career, having been
employed in the Bowdle State Bank, Farmers and Merchants Bank in Aberdeen
and Webster, the bank in Breckenridge, MN and is presently president of
the First American Bank and Trust in Marshall.

They have three sons. David, born Nov. 25, 1945 in Bowdle, married Darlyce
Childred of Aberdeen. They have two children: Terisa and Daniel. David is
an electrical engineer in Houston, TX.

Peter was born Feb. 13, 1957 in Aberdeen. He is a mechanical engineer in
St. Paul, MN.

Chris was born May 20, 1958 in Aberdeen and lives in Marshall, MN where he
is a graduate student and manages a Perkins Restaurant.

SISTER DARLENE GUTENKAUF

        Sister Darlene Gutenkauf

ERVIN and LUCILLE [HETTICH] HAAR

RAY and HELEN [ZEEB] HAAR

Raymond Haar was born to David and Christina Haar March 19, 1909 in North
Dakota. His mother died when he was a child and Ray lived with his sister
Minnie much of the time. He attended grade school and married Helen Zeeb
Nov. 21, 1928. She is the daughter of Christ and Pauline Zeeb of Streeter,
ND. Helen was born Oct. 15, 1910. She attended grade school. At an early
age she worked for others, as she came from a large family.

Ray and Helen settled on a farm known as the Adam Mertz place near Bowdle,
where their daughter Genivieve was born. Later they moved to the Fred Gross
farm and were blessed with a son Lester. Their next move was to the Kurle
farm. Here they had a big surprise when twins, Larry and Darlene were born.
Marcella was also born on the Kurle farm.

Farming was not prosperous with a big family but they worked hard tilling
the soil, milking and raising a large garden to help supply the family's
needs. Helen remembers Ray having to work for the W.P.A. The dry years were
especially hard, but there proved to be good times later as she recalls a
trip to Oregon with neighbors in their Model A Ford which took almost a
week.

They moved to one more farm, now known as the Alvin Eisenbeisz farm. About
1948 they moved to Bowdle where Ray and Emil E. Haar had a blacksmith shop.
Ray was also a part-time trucker. Later he and son Larry became full-time
truckers and Ray continued in that work until his death in 1979.

The Haar home was always open to visiting ministers, for they were active
in church work, helping wherever they could. Helen worked at the Bowdle
Nursing Home until retiring in 1983.

        Helen and Ray Haar

Genivieve married Harold Weber. They had four children: Clayton, Linda,
Kathy and Gail. Genivieve is a nurse's aide at the Bowdle Nursing Home.

Lester married Joyce Brosturm and they have four children: Sharon,
Charlene, Darla and Randy. Lester and Joyce live in Minneapolis. Lester has
retired from railroad work.

Larry married Gloria Ellis. Larry is running a trucking business at Bowdle.
Their children are Anita, Lisa, Patricia, Myron, Timothy and Amanda.

Darlene and husband Kenneth Marcuson live at Milnor, ND and have an
upholstery shop. They have two children Brian and Barry.

Marcella and husband Quentin Walz live in Bowdle. They had four children
Cheryl, Darvin, Derrick and Annette. Darvin was fatally injured in a car
accident. Quentin has an auto body shop.

CHRISTIAN and BARBARA HABERER

Russia was the homeland of Christian (born 1881) and Barbara (born 1877.)
At the age of 11 Christian came to the United States and Barbara came to
this new land at the age of 22.

They homesteaded 10 miles south of Bowdle on a farm where they were blessed
with three sons Jacob, Edwin and Emil and three daughters Emma, Lydia and
Hulda. All of them grew up to adulthood on this farm except Edwin who died
at the age of four. The parents and all the children are deceased, except
Lydia (Haberer) Huber and Hulda (Haberer) Paulson.

The main occupation was farming for Christian and Barbara. When it was time
to sell the eggs and cream, they had to be hauled with horse and buggy. The
horses also hauled all the grain to market in wagon boxes. It was a long
journey, about 10 miles one direction, which was difficult to complete as a
round trip in one day.

        Back: Emma, Jacob, Lydia, Hulda Front: Christian, Emil, Barbara
        Haberer

The farming was done with horse power. Three horses were hitched on a sulky
plow and five horses were hitched on a two lay-plow. Corn was cultivated
with two horses, one row at a time. Christian farmed all his life with
horses, never owning a tractor.

Christian died in 1937 and Barbara in 1939.

JAKE and EMMA [HUBER] HABERER

Jake Haberer was born Nov. 11, 1906 at rural Bowdle to Christ and Barbara
(Seefried) Haberer. They came from Russia in 1902. Christ was born April
23, 1881 and died March 2, 1937. Barbara was born Dec. 19, 1877 and died
Feb. 21, 1939.

Jake married Emma Huber of rural Hosmer Nov. 4, 1930. Emma is the daughter
of Jacob J. and Magdalina (Hoff) Huber. Emma's father emigrated from
Glueckstahl, South Russia in 1897. He was born Sept. 3, 1879 and died Jan.
7, 1961. Magdalina was born at Tripp Nov. 24, 1883 and died May 29, 1957.

        Back: Wyman, Orval, Merle Front: Emma and Jake Haberer

Jake and Emma lived on a farm 10 miles south of Bowdle until 1956, when
they moved into a home they built in Bowdle. In 1958 they purchased
Aldinger Mobil Gas Station. Eventually they built an additional shop area
onto the station. Their son Orval assisted Jake in the business. Jake was
active in the gas station and shop until his death Nov. 11, 1965.

Four sons were born to Jake and Emma: Merle, Dewaine, Wyman and Orval.
Dewaine died in 1936. Merle and Florence (Lindamen) Haberer have four
children. Their daughter Dotty is married to Virgil Scherr and their
children are Christopher and Dean. Merle and Florence have a son Carney who
married Beth Adajar and they have a daughter Crystal. Stacy Haberer married
Lori McDonald and Kenny Haberer married April Hoffman. All five families
live in Aberdeen.

Wyman and Janice (Schack) Haberer have a daughter Dawn and a son Perry. The
family lives at Long Lake, MN.

Orval and Judy (Heupel) Haberer have a son Bryan at home and a daughter
Tamara, who is married to Jeff Gnat. They have a daughter Lea and make
their home in Watertown.

ORVAL and JUDY [HEUPEL] HABERER

Orval Haberer was born Dec. 30, 1940 at Bowdle to Jacob and Emma (Huber)
Haberer. Jacob was born Nov. 11, 1906 at Bowdle and died Nov. 11, 1965.
Emma was born Jan. 18, 1906 at Hosmer.

Orval graduated from Bowdle High School. In February 1958, in partnership
with his father he purchased the Mobil Gas Station from Eugene Aldinger. In
January 1959 he went to Toronto, Canada where he attended Chicago Vocational
Tech. College earning a degree in auto and diesel mechanics.

        Tammy, Bryan, Judy, Orval Haberer

Orval married Judy Heupel Sept. 10, 1961, daughter of Otto and Lea
(Guthmiller) Heupel. Judy was born Aug. 20, 1943 and graduated from Eureka
High School. Otto Heupel was born April 6, 1912. His wife Lea was born Jan.
5, 1914 and died Oct. 20, 1972.

After his father's death Orval became sole owner of the gas station, making
the purchase in December 1965. In August 1967 he acquired the Case Farm
Equipment franchise and May 1974 saw the business in a new building in the
south industrial area of Bowdle. Orval expanded the business in July 1974
purchasing Mobridge Iron Works and started a Case and Versatile dealership
there. He sold the Bowdle and Mobridge businesses to DeWayne Weiszhaar and
Richard Keller in November 1979.

Since that time Orval and Judy Haberer have occupied their hours fishing,
traveling and sightseeing, including a trip to Alaska in 1983. He now
manages Haberer Brothers farm south of Bowdle and transformed the old Mobil
Station into a medical clinic, which is leased to Dr. Adajar.

Orval and Judy have two children. Bryan was born April 23, 1962 at Bowdle.
He attended one year at Northern State College and was employed at McFleeg
Inc. in Bowdle. He is currently attending Lake Area Vocational Tech. in
Watertown. Tamara Haberer was born Nov. 2, 1963. She attended Lake Area Vo.
Tech. at Watertown and is employed at the Champion Auto Store. She married
Jeff Gnat April 28, 1984 and they have a daughter Lea.

DAN and EDNA [SIEWERT] HAGELE

Dan Hagele was the third child born to Edward and Mary (Reiner) Hagele Oct.
30, 1912 in the Bowdle area. This family had four boys. Ted (now deceased)
was married to Alma Knecht now of Sunnyside, WA. Emil was married to Ethel
Johnson and resides in Staunton, VA. Elmer married Elsie Eisenman and they
live in Lincoln, NE. Delpha is married to Carrol Johnson and now living in
Hamburg, PA.

        Dan, Edna, Joyce, Clyde [in front] Hagele

Dan used to tell how their little sister would get talked into playing,
"Feed the Chickens," by her youngest brothers. An original game with a
strategy. When she would get a bag of yellow and orange Candy Corn, those
being the See's and Russel Stovers of the day, they would tell her they
will be chickens and need to be fed corn. She would scatter some on the
table, while they clowningly pecked at the candy until the corn bag was empty
and tears were the result.

Edna (Siewert) Hagele was born to Mike and Rosena (Dollinger) Siewert May
6, 1914. She was the oldest in a family of three children. Ellen was
married to Wm. (Bill) Hagele, son of Christ and Minnie Hagele and lives in
Lodi, CA. Aaron the youngest, now living on the home place south of Bowdle,
is married to Pearl (Vollmer) Siewert.

Dan and Edna were married June 4, 1935. They had two children. Joyce, born
July 12, 1941, married Merlin Heim of San Diego, CA. They are both employed
with Paradise Valley Hospital in San Diego -- Joyce with continuing
education and teaching and Merlin as a microbiologist. Their son Kevin is
in college. Clyde Hagele was born May 2, 1946. He died Feb. 14, 1952 after
a year of illness.

        Joyce, Merlin, Kevin Heim

Dan and Edna farmed on the Ed Hagele farm southeast of Bowdle until 1974
when Dan became ill and died Sept. 16. 1974.

Edna attended Northern State College and taught rural schools. By attending
summer school night classes. correspondence and the caring encouragement of
Nellie Weiszhaar she got her BS Degree. She spent 1964 to 1975 teaching
third grade in the Roscoe School System. She said, "In spite of having to
work overtime many times, teaching children was a most enjoyable and
rewarding experience."

For the past number of years Edna has joined the Snow Birds going to spend
the winter months with her children in San Diego where, even though she
feels comfortable and loved, there is a magnetic force that draws her back
to Bowdle which she calls home in the spring.

GOTTLIEB G. and MAGDALENA [DOLLINGER] HAGELE

Gottlieb and Magdalena (Dollinger) Hagele were born in Odessa, Russia.
Gottlieb was the son of Adam and Rosina Hagele and was born in 1880.
Magdalena was born to Philip and Barbara Dollinger in 1883.

Gottlieb immigrated to the United States with his parents in 1888. They
settled on a homestead in Odessa Township south of Bowdle. Magdalena and
her parents came to America in 1889. They also took a homestead in Odessa
Township one mile from the Hagele farm.

As a young man, Gottlieb hauled lumber with a team and wagon from old
Everetts south of Glenham to build business places in Bowdle. Gottlieb and
Magdalena were married in 1901 and homesteaded in Hudson Township. They
later moved to Odessa Township and built their farmstead seven and one-half
miles south of Bowdle. This farm is still in the Hagele family.

        Gottlieb and Magdalena Hagele

Gottlieb was a member of the Odessa Township Board, the township school
board and also served as assessor. For many years Gottlieb served as an
elder of the Bowdle Seventh-day Adventist Church.

In 1944 the Hageles retired from farming and moved to Bowdle. They had the
pleasure of four children. Lydia married William Heinrich, Tillie became
the wife of Walter Johnson, Ellie married Art Holweger and Milton and his
wife (Minnie Eisenman) succeeded Gottlieb on the farm and later moved into
Bowdle.

Gottlieb died Feb. 25, 1958. Magdalena lived 16 more years, dying June 11,
1974.

MILTON and MINNIE [EISENMAN] HAGELE

Milton Hagele was born Sept. 19, 1916 on the farm seven miles south of
Bowdle, where his parents, Gottlieb and Magdalena Hagele had homesteaded in
1903. He attended the district school in Odessa Township, Bowdle High
School for three years and finished his secondary education graduating from
Plainview Academy in Redfield. He attended Union College in Lincoln, NE one
semester, but returned to the farm in 1939 as his father was unable to run
it alone.

        Milton and Minnie Hagele

Milton married Minnie Eisenman of Glenham Sept. 15, 1941. She was a school
teacher and was born Nov. 13, 1920, the daughter of Gottlieb and Louise
Eisenman. Farm life kept Minnie busy, but she also found time to give piano
lessons and serve the Seventh-day Adventist Church as organist, continuing
to the present time.

The Hageles continued to operate a cattle, dairy and grain farm until 1954
when Milton purchased the Bowdle Livestock Sales Barn from E.B. Moser, but
continued with grain farming. He sold Bowdle Livestock Commission Co. to
Kermit Ulmer and Norbert Simon in 1961 and continued to farm. In 1976
Hageles purchased the Christ Voegele house and moved to town, but continued
farming until 1984 when Milton's health forced him to retire.

        Arden Hagele Family

Milton was the only son of a close-knit family, living in a circle of
relatives who farmed nearby. His sisters are Lydia (Mrs. Wm. Heinrich),
Tillie (Mrs. Walter Johnson) and Ellen (Mrs. Art Holweger.)

        Cordell Hagele Family

Farming is a hazardous trade. Accidents can happen when least expected as
Milton found one spring day when plowing with five horses hitched to a
two-bottom plow. The barbed wire fence of a pasture next to the field had
been loosened during the winter to permit the cattle access to graze off
the field. Making the turn, the plow came too close to the downed wires,
frightened the horses and they took off for the next county. The rough ride
was short. Milton held on to the reins, but was unable to stop the horses
and jumped off. However, the horses had not reckoned with rocks in the
pasture. The plow hit a big one, tripped and went into the sod. Plowing sod
is much harder than plowing tilled ground and this brought the horses to a
stop. Aside from the short rough ride, the repairing of the broken eveners
and torn harness, little damage was done. Incidentally Milton felt he learned
a lesson too, not to drive too close to the fence on the turn when plowing.
The family was all duly thankful he was not injured.

Milton has served on the Odessa Township Board a number of years. A member
of the Seventh-day Adventist Church, he has served on the Seventh-day
Conference Committee, was treasurer of the local church and is now the head
Elder. He was re-elected to a second term as alderman for the city of
Bowdle in 1984.

Mr. and Mrs. Hagele are parents of three children: Adren whose wife is the
former Barbara Heinrich. They live in Zephyr Hills, FL, where Adren is
controller of a hospital. They have two daughters Tana and Traci.

        Dean Hagele

Dean Hagele is an X-ray technician and lives in Loma Linda, CA and Cordell
and his wife Kathleen (McCulley) live in Wapello, IA where he is the
funeral director. They have two sons Michael and Matthew.

JOHNNY and ADELINE [SPITZER] HALLER

Johnny Haller was born on a farm southwest of Ashley, ND. He received his
education in the country school near the farm where his family lived. In
1935 he married Adeline Spitzer, his sweetheart from a neighboring farm.

The same year they moved to Eureka where he began his career in the grocery
business, starting at the bottom helping unload trucks of groceries and
doing odd jobs at the local Red Owl Store. Soon he had a job as clerk and
shelf-stocker. After a few years he was promoted to assistant manager at
Ellendale, ND. He also filled in as manager at other stores when the
managers were on vacation.

Their sons Gary John and Maylan Roy (Mel) were born in Eureka. In 1945 the
couple decided to strike out on their own and opened a Red Owl agency store
in Bowdle. After having promoted a good business they sold the store, but
it did not prosper under the new owner. At the urging of friends the
Hallers again took over and ran a successful business until 1961. The
family lived in an apartment over the store.

After selling the Bowdle store again they were interested in owning a
variety store. The family spent several months looking over likely
locations in California, Oregon and Washington, but decided the West Coast
was not for them. They returned to the Midwest and opened a Ben Franklin
Store in Eureka. After a highly successful 15 years in Eureka they sold the
business. In 1976 Johnny and Adeline bought a home in Sun City, AZ and
retired there. Johnny died in 1984 at age 72. Adeline still lives in Sun
City.

Gary Haller lives in the Philadelphia area. He married Mary Ellen Ferris of
Vermillion and is employed by Smith-Kline Beckman, a pharmaceutical
company. They have two children. Kevin lives in Atlanta, GA and Amber is at
home.

Maylan (Mel) Haller married Debra Plotkin of Denver and is a high school
teacher in that area.

ALBERT G. and OLGA [MELLAND] HAM

Albert George Ham was born Oct. 28, 1911 to Robert and Mary (Seboick) Ham
of Hoven in Walworth County. He was one of eleven sons and four daughters.
He attended school in Walworth County. Albert married Olga Melland Oct. 6,
1940 at Forbes, ND. She was born to John N. and Bertha (Kaalaas) Melland
Oct. 28, 1918 at Bradley in Clark County. She attended Bradley and Redeem
rural schools and Aberdeen Business College.

        Olga and Albert Ham

Albert and Olga have three children: Richard, Judith and Shirley. Richard
Arlen was born Aug. 2, 1941 at Aberdeen. He married Lorraine Faye Hart of
Bowdle Aug. 28, 1960. She was born May 22, 1942 in Utah. Richard and

seven children. Machelle, age 23, married Jeff Iverson of Rapid City Aug.
2, 1980. Their daughter Jennifer is four and they live in Mesa, AZ.
Kimberly Ham is 21 and attends BHSC in Spearfish; Bradley is 19 and attends

Judith Ann was born April 21, 1946 at Hoven. She married Creighton W.

Shirley Jean Ham was born Oct. 16, 1951 at Hoven and died in infancy.

As a young man Al worked in the timber mills in Montana. After his marriage

returned to the Ham family farm at Hoven and in 1952 Al and Olga purchased
a farm nine miles southwest of Bowdle and lived there until 1975 when they

DWAYNE and KATHLEEN [JOHNLE] HAM

Dwayne Ham was born June 10, 1939 at St. Luke's Hospital in Aberdeen, the
son of Berton and Frieda Erlenbusch Ham. In his sixth year his parents
moved to Loyalton where he attended school through the eighth grade. He
then attended School of Agriculture at South Dakota State University at
Brookings and after graduation he returned to help his father with farming.

In January 1959 he enlisted in the U.S. Air Force and was stationed in
Texas, Illinois, Montana and spent a year at Thule Air Base in Greenland.
After the four-year tour of duty he returned to the farm.

        Dwayne, Kathleen, Mark and John Ham

Dwayne married Kathleen E. Johnle Sept. 28, 1968. She is the daughter of
Sam and Bertha (Baer) Johnle and was born Oct. 15, 1943. Kathleen attended
Hillside Township District School and graduated from Roscoe High School in
1961. She attended Aberdeen School of Commerce and accepted a position with
W.N. Van Camp Insurance Co. at Pierre.

Dwayne and Kathleen made their first home on the family farm. In 1970 they
moved to Watertown where Dwayne attended Lake Area Vocational Institute.
Upon graduation he was employed in Algona, IA.

Their children are John Leon, born Sept. 16, 1970 and Mark Jay, born Feb.
19, 1979. Both attend Bowdle School.

The Ham family also spent several years in Pollock where Dwayne was a
mechanic for Pollock Implement Co. In August 1974 he began to work at
Haberer's Implement Inc. in Bowdle and in 1985 he started working for
Edmunds County Highway Department.

The Ham family are members of St. John's Evangelical Lutheran Church in
Bowdle.

LEROY E. and FRANCES [WILLIAMS] HARING

LeRoy, born May 9, 1909, is the son of Sam and Amanda Haring. He graduated

MELVIN and OLIVE [HUNDSTAD] HARING

SAM and AMANDA [LECONTE] HARING

Sam Haring came to South Dakota from Savanna, IL to help with harvesting
and threshing in 1899. The next year he brought his own threshing rig and
harvested in the Bowdle area.

Amanda LeConte came to Selby from Washington, IL in 1905 to visit her
sister and stayed three years. She met Sam Haring and they were married
Sept. 1, 1908 at Aberdeen and made their home in Bowdle.

Sam was an engineer on the Milwaukee Line several years and then became
marshall and night watchman in Bowdle five years and then began farming in
the Bowdle area. Amanda worked as a dressmaker and roomed teachers at
various times.

Sam and Amanda had five children: LeRoy, Melvin, Louis, Cora and Muriel.
All were born in Bowdle and graduated from Bowdle High School, except
Muriel who died in February 1942 at age 15.

In 1942 Sam and Amanda moved to Rapid City. Sam died March 7, 1962 and
Amanda died Sept. 13, 1973. Both are buried at Bowdle Cemetery.

HULDA [MERTZ] HARTMAN

Hulda Mertz Hartman entitled her little autobiography "Country Girl Turns
City Girl." After teaching in a one-room country school, Hulda has gone on
to be a teacher in a system that has 23 elementary schools in the city of
Santa Ana, CA. At present she is on the staff of a school that has over
1000 pupils and is presently on a 12 months schedule with three-fourths of
the children in class while one-fourth are on vacation. There is a constant
rotation of classes and teachers throughout the school year.

After being divorced in 1970, Hulda joined the Phoenix Club, which includes
a German Club of Orange County ... a terrific place to meet people, dance
and have a good time.

Hulda's parents were Jacob and Elizabeth Mertz of Bowdle. Hulda's family
consists of four daughters. Karla Ann Guenzler is a teacher and the wife of
Bruce Guenzler, who is employed by Amtrack at Pocatello, ID. They have a
son Eric.

Hulda's daughter Kay Carole Rios is the mother of two children: Jesse and
Kristina. She is divorced and employed as a secretary at Santa Ana College.

Kim Marie Gavin is a competent court reporter and employed with her own
computer at home. Her husband Tim works in a muffler shop. Their children
are Amber Nicol and Matthew Patrick.

Kathleen Elizabeth Hartman Currier works as a secretary for Federal Express
in Topeka, KS. Her husband John Wendell Currier is employed as a lineman in
Topeka.

Hulda's future plans include enjoying a new grandchild born in May, her
retirement which she expects to begin in 1986 and if she can, find an
agreeable companion, maybe marriage and traveling to see the world.

MILFORD M. and EMMA [FAUSS] HARTZELL

Milford was born at Naperville, IL April 10, 1893 to Amandis and Caroline
Hughes Hartzell. He was baptized into the Christian faith Feb. 24, 1907 and
confirmed in May 1907 at Grace Church in Naperville. He attended school at
Naperville.

        Milford and Emma HartzelI

Milford came to South Dakota in 1910 and settled in the Ipswich area. He
served his country in World War I. He married Emma Fauss at Ortonville, MN
Dec. 31, 1919. Emma was born July 13, 1893 at Norwood, MN and came to South
Dakota with her family in 1908.

Milford and Emma made their first home in Ortonville, later in Bristol and
Bowdle was their final home, where Milford (also known as Jack) was
employed by Milwaukee Railroad. After his retirement he was City Treasurer
of Bowdle about three years.

He was a member of the American Legion and served many years as service
officer of the Bowdle Post. He was selected "Legionnaire of the Year for
District 14 in Aberdeen. He was honored by the Environmental Science
Service Administration Weather Bureau for 10 years as Bowdle's weather
observer. In 1956 he was honored as Bowdle's Outstanding Citizen of the
Year for his long services to many organizations and the Bowdle Legion. He
served on the Bowdle Hospital Board and was a member of St. Paul Lutheran
Church. He died at Bowdle in 1980.

Emma then moved to her daughter's in Huron. She and Milford are buried at
Black Hills National Cemetery in Sturgis. Their only child, Jayne married
George Dutenhoeffer of Huron and they have two children.

CARL and MATHILDA [BOLLINGER] HAUPT

Carl Haupt was born Nov. 14, 1887 and died May 11, 1964. He was the first
child born in Bowdle and lived in this area all his life. He married
Mathilda Bollinger, who was born Dec. 5, 1895 and died Aug. 11, 1979.

Their children were Harold, who married Elenora Schick; Raymond, who
married Mary Lou Halverson and he died in a truck accident at age 38;
Viola, who married Roy Lemke and she died Aug. 26, 1972; Irene, who married
Lester Schock; Berniece, who married Adolph Rohrbach and Delores, who
married Reinhold Rohrbach.

Carl and Mathilda Haupt lived to enjoy 21 grandchildren.

ERNEST R. and KATHERINE [JENNERl HAUPT

Ernest was born Dec. 10, 1895 at Bowdle to Wilhelm and Marie (Miller)
Haupt. He married Katherine Jenner July 3, 1924. She was the daughter of
John and Elizabeth (Bollinger) Jenner.

Prior to his marriage Ernest and his brother Henry homesteaded and farmed
near Selby. Later Ernest served in the U.S. Army in Europe during World War
I. After his marriage Ernest established his family in Bowdle where he
became Bowdle's first rural mail carrier. He served in this capacity 19
years. The family later moved to a farm near Bowdle, the present Emil Mertz
farm.

Ernest farmed that site until 1948 when he moved the family to Roscoe where
they operated a restaurant until 1951. The family then moved to Aberdeen
where he worked as a carpenter and construction contractor. He retired to
Colorado in the 1970's. Ernest died in 1982 and his wife Katherine
currently lives in Thornton, CO. Ernest and Katherine had six children.

        Back: Harris, Maybelle, Grace, Elaine Front: Dorothy, Katherine,
        Ernest, Lois Haupt

HAROLD and ELENORA [SCHICK, WOLFF] HAUPT

        Back: Ronald and Roger Wolff Front: Elenora and Harold Haupt

HARRIS B. and LINDA M. [LOEBS] HAUPT

Harris was born Nov. 28, 1943 at Bowdle to Ernest and Katherine (Jenner)

        Back: Bradley, Katherine, Ryan Front: Harris and Linda Haupt

WILLIAM and MARIE [MILLER] HAUPT

William was born Nov. 8, 1857 in Grieg, Germany. He came to America with
his family at about age 4. His family settled in the southern part of South
Dakota. Later they moved to Ipswich and then to Bowdle July 5, 1886. "At
that time," William stated, "there were only a few buildings, maybe a
dozen." William was a carpenter by trade. He, along with Mr. Buttwell,
built the Cox Brothers Store and did the finish work on the Dumont Hotel.
Other buildings he helped build were the John Rhodes house, Edward
Blumhardt home old school house and Dr. Edwards' first hospital.

In 1888 he rented land from Mr. Lindholm north of the farm where the
Hoffman Brothers used to live. They lived in a sod shanty which was half
above the ground and half dug out below the surface. Farming that year was
not successful because the crops burned up.

They were living on their homestead about 4 miles northwest of Bowdle. He
homesteaded the land in 1888 and built a frame house there that fall.
Shortly afterwards a prairie fire swept that section but luckily they saved
the house.

In 1891 the crops were hailed out, 1892 was a good year, but 1893 was poor
again. William got disgusted that year and he moved his family back to
town. In 1896 they moved back to the farm. To get the needed equipment
William traded his house in town (where Christ Bader lived) for a team of
mules, a dog, a wagon, a plow and $50 in cash. He did this trading with D.
Mason. William continued to farm with his mules and oxen. He farmed until
1916 when he again retired to town. In 1918 he built the house where his
son Ernest later lived.

William and Marie had six children. They were Julius, Carl, Ernest, Henry,
Mrs. Bertha Gange and Mrs. Hilda Schroeder. William died Dec. 11, 1937. His
wife Marie, who was born May 18, 1857 at Lodz, Poland, died Jan. 3, 1927.

Carl and Regina Heckenlaible in June 1909. His parents were born in Russia

Alfred and Alice have bachelor of science degrees and Alice completed an

She writes: "My leisure time is busy. I enjoy doing the things I didn't
have time for before. I take care of my mother, Rose Kurle, who had a stroke
two years ago, leaving her left side paralyzed. Besides this, I take care
of a two bedroom home and a garden. I visit my daughter Mary and family at
least twice a year. It's always a joy to be with them, especially the two
grandchildren."

Alice's son-in-law Keith Jansen (10-21-48) teaches music part-time. He and
Mary have two children: Joshua (10-25-78) and Tanya (4-12-80.)

MATH and MARY [MATERI] HEILMAN

Math Heilman grew up on a farm in Modena Township and has spent most of his

        Math and Mary Heilman

        Peter, Sister Vita, Margaret Heilman

Math and Mary lived with his folks a year and then moved to a small farm
one and one-half miles from the Heilman homestead. After two years they
moved back to the farm where Math grew up. All they had when they started
farming were five horses, four calves, two pigs, 35 chickens and three milk
cows. Each week about five gallons of cream were sold and with the cream
check, they bought groceries and gasoline for their car. They bought a
Model A Ford for $60. When they moved back to the homestead they bought a
F-20 tractor, plow and drill from Math's parents.

WILLIAM and LYDIA [HAGELE] HEINRICH

William D. Heinrich was born in 1897 at Enid, OK. His parents were George
and Kathryn Heinrich who had lived in northern Russia. George was born in
1864 and died in 1946. Kathryn was born in 1872 and died in 1958.

In his youth, William carne to South Dakota from Oklahoma selling books to
earn a scholarship to go to college, which he attended during the winter. He
also worked in the harvest fields. When he had the opportunity to teach
school he went back to college and earned his bachelor of arts degree from
Union College in Lincoln, NE. He obtained a teaching certificate and taught
12 years in Hudson, Odessa and Modena Districts.

He married Lydia Hagele June 11, 1923. She was born in 1901 in Bowdle and
received a high school education. Her parents were Gottlieb Hagele who
lived 1880-1958 and Magdalena Hagele, 1883-1974. They were born in South
Russia.

Lydia Heinrich was also a teacher and William said they invested their
money in land in Odessa Township where they are still living.

Mr. Heinrich recalls: "During the 30's when the drought and high winds hit
we stuck it out by milking cows, raising chickens and turkeys which
industry is still a pleasure." He recalls he was the first to have a
rubber-tired tractor, first to have a binder to cut the grain and first to
try a combine. "I used the binder as a windrower in 1942. Others laughed at
this Oklahoma boy, but perseverance paid and we won out. We planted trees
in a treeless country and when others said, 'It can't be done,' we did it.
I was registered in the two World Wars and did my first plowing with a
one-bottom walking plow, cultivated with a one-row cultivator, threshed
wheat with a steam engine, milked cows by hand under the open sky and
sheared sheep by hand.

"Later I plowed the land with a six-horse team and a gang plow. I always
rode a horse to school when I was teaching and owned the first enclosed car
in 1925. I still have a 1915 windmill which is operable and shows the wind
direction every day."

        Back: Clemens, Clayton, Roger Front: Lydia and William Heinrich

Mr. and Mrs. Heinrich have three sons. Clemens, born in 1925, is a farmer
in the Tolstoy area; Roger, born in 1933, is pastor of the Seventh-day
Adventist Church in Spokane, WA; and Clayton, born in 1943, is principal at
the Junior High School Academy in Sedro Woolley, WA. They also have three
daughters-in-law, 12 grandchildren and eight great-grandchildren as of 1984.

OTTO W. and JACOBINA [KETTERLING] HELMER

Otto W. Helmer was born in Brownton, MN Feb. 13, 1887. He died after a
heart attack in San Diego, CA April 26, 1952 at the home of his youngest
daughter.

Mr. Helmer came to Bowdle Oct. 1, 1914 where he married Jacobina (Josie)
Ketterling. She was born in Bowdle Dec. 23, 1890 and died Sept. 16, 1938.
She was being treated for cancer at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, MN when she
died.

A barber by trade, Otto had a shop a few years after he came to Bowdle and
later was in partnership with J.K. Moser in the Bowdle Hardware Store until
1948 when they sold the business to Bernard Carlson and Harold Bauer. Mr.
Helmer was the Bowdle Hardware plumber.

A community conscious person, Otto served on the Board of Education several
terms, was a member of the Hiddenwood Lodge A.F. & A.M. serving as
worshipful master and in other capacities in the lodge. He and his wife
were also members of the Order of Eastern Star--Bowdle Chapter and active
in the Methodist Church.

Otto was elected chief of the Bowdle Volunteer Fire Department in 1932,
serving in that office five consecutive years and retaining membership 20
years. He also served his country as a member of the Selective Service
Draft Board four years. After the sale of the store Helmer retired to live
his last years in California.

His children were: Sylvia, born Nov. 10, 1915 at Bowdle. She married
Kenneth Oliver May 28, 1939. Their daughter Dawn was born March 26, 1948.
Sylvia died of leukemia Nov. 2, 1964. She had been a teacher before her
marriage.

Goldie Helmer was born Jan. 28, 1917. She married Robert Fugett and lives
in Joliet, IL. She was a secretary and was employed at Federal Land Bank
Association in Bowdle.

Dale Helmer was born Aug. 24, 1920. He served in the U.S. Navy during World
War II and upon his discharge married Elenor Ruben May 16, 1946. They had
two sons. Arthur was born March 21, 1947 at Spokane, WA and Jim Wayne was
born Jan. 11, 1952 at Ipswich. Arthur (Chips) is married, has two children
and lives at Missoula, MT where he is a painter. Jim has two sons, lives in
Portland, OR and is going to college. Dale Helmer died Nov. 5, 1959 of
injuries received in a fall while working on the radar station at
Gettysburg. Dale was a farmer and plumber. Elenor has remarried to Jim
Nelson and lives in Missoula, MT.

Gloria Helmer was born Jan. 14, 1923 and is a beautician. She married
Robert A. Carr Oct. 16, 1946 and they live in San Diego, CA. Their daughter
Derithe Denise was born May 1, 1949 at Tacoma, WA. She is the mother of
three and lives at Burmuda Dunes, CA.

Wesley Helmer was born Aug. 18, 1931. He married Grace Krause June 22,
1958. They had two children: Candice Lynn, born Jan. 5, 1959 and Kurt
Wayne, born Oct. 9, 1960. The lives of Wesley, his wife and son ended
tragically when they were killed Nov. 23, 1960 in a car collision. Candice
(Helmer) Peterson resides in Sioux Falls. Her father Wesley had been a
farmer and plumber by trade.
