Henry, son of John and Elizabeth Herman, was born in 1876 in South Russia.
At age 14, his father died. Mrs. Elizabeth Herman with her sons Henry, John
and Christ and two daughters Mrs. Andrew Reede and Mrs. John Baer, arrived
in Freeman early in the spring of 1893. They stayed with an uncle Christ
Herman a short time and later left for Bowdle.

Henry's mother filed on a claim known as the LeRoy Perman farm 18 miles
southwest of Bowdle. Here Henry, his mother and brother John carried on the
farm expanding it to 640 acres.

In 1898 Henry married Nettie Miller, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. John Miller.
She came to this country with her parents in 1889 and settled 11 miles
south of Bowdle.

A short time after their marriage they filed on their own homestead close
to Henry's mother, which they made their home many years. Many hardships
and good years were experienced by this couple on the farm.

        Henry Herman Family Back: Reinhold, Elnora, Edward, Hulda, John,
        Martha, Albert, George. Front: Lena, Henry, Nettie, Betty.

In 1937 they retired and made their home in Mobridge. Henry died in March
1953 and Nettie died in May 1964. There were 10 children born to this
union. The only one residing in Bowdle is Reinhold.

JOE SR. and GERTRUDE [KAISER] HERMAN

Mr. Herman was born in Minnesota in 1883 and at age 3 came with his parents
to Hoven. They had a sod house. They tilled the land with a yoke of oxen.
In 1892 they purchased their first team of horses. Joe could remember the
blizzard of 1888 when it got so dark his mother lit a candle in the daytime
in order to see to perform the household duties.

        Back: Warren, Laura, Mike, Catherine, Joe Jr., Regina, Herman,
        Bernice, Alois, Charles. Seated: Joe Sr. and Gertrude Herman.

Joe Herman and Gertrude Kaiser were married Nov. 29, 1905 in the Catholic
Church at Hoven. They made their home on a homestead north of Hoven where
they lived until 1920 when they moved to a farm near Bowdle. In 1926 they
moved to the Christ Miller farm southwest of Bowdle where they lived until
1945 when they retired from the farm to make their home in Bowdle.

Ten children came to bless their home: Joe Jr. of Bowdle; Mike of Miller;
Warren of La Mesa, CA; Laura (Mrs. George Schaeffer) of Aberdeen; Charles
of Barnard; Catherine (Mrs. Otto Weber) of Plattsmouth, NE; Regina (Mrs.
Bernard Weber) of Seneca) Alois of Westport; Herman of Frederick and
Bernice (Mrs. Lowell Holmstrom) of Seneca. Joe Herman Sr. died Oct. 8, 1964
and his wife Gertrude died July 21, 1966.

JOE and MARIE [MEYERS] HERMAN

Joe Herman was born on a farm near Hoven and attended school there. When a
teenager, he accompanied his father to a farm near Bowdle, helping out with
the farm work.

Marie Meyers, when three years old, came to South Dakota from Superior, WI
with her parents. Her father had a farm home built on the land he bought
previously. Their belongings were brought to Bowdle in a large train car.
Relatives and friends helped haul their things to their house. Five years
later her father died and her mother and brothers carried on alone. Marie
loved farm life, attended a rural school and continued on to college in
Aberdeen. She taught rural schools for several years.

        Joe and Marie Herman

Joe and Marie were married Nov. 25, 1925 at St. Augustine's Catholic Church
in Bowdle. A year later they moved to the Meyer farm. In 1925 her mother
and they bought the farm from the estate. Thirteen years later they were
able to pay for it.

Joe and Marie loved animals and had horses to ride and hitch to the buggy,
enabling them to visit their friends and drive to Bowdle.

Three children blessed their home. Victor and his family live at Fargo, ND.
Kathleen and her husband Dr. Richard Isaak live at Eureka. They have two
children and the daughter is still at home. Patricia Goettsch and her
husband live at Portland, OR. A daughter Vicki is married and lives nearby.
Joe and Marie Herman still live on the farm. On their 1985 wedding
anniversary they will be married 60 years.

KENNETH HERMAN

Kenneth Herman was born to Reinie and Laura Herman July 20, 1930. He
graduated from Bowdle High School and attended Northern State Teachers
College at Aberdeen. He was a member of the United States Marine Corps. At
present he lives at Hot Springs Veterans Home. The picture of Kenneth was
taken when he lived with his parents on the farm. riding his favorite horse.

REINHOLD and LAURA [NELSON] HERMAN

Reinhold, son of Henry and Nettie Herman, was born April 13, 1904 in
southeastern Walworth County. His parents immigrated to America between
1889 and 1893 from South Russia.

Laura Herman's parents came to America from Sweden. Louis and Ellen Nelson
settled in Irene, IL where Laura was born Sept. 21, 1900.

It was in southeastern Walworth County where Reinie received his 8th grade
education and helped his father with the farming.

        Patricia, Laura, Kenneth, Reinie, Carol Herman

In 1924 Laura came from DeSmet to teach at a school in Walworth County,
located on the Hoven road and still stands at the present time. She boarded
with Matt Kaisers and bought her first new car, a 1925 Ford Coupe, at Hoven.

Laura and Reinie were married Dec. 29, 1928 at Huron. They first rented the
Boyd Place where they farmed with horses and later bought a farm 10 miles
southwest of Bowdle, known as the Fred Perman place. In 1945 they moved to
Bowdle and purchased the Herman-Baer home where they presently reside.

Reinie was a salesman for Reuer Implement until 1958 when he started
selling insurance. He was well-known as proprietor of R.J. Herman Agency in
Bowdle.

Laura and Reinie had three children. Kenneth was born in 1930, Patricia in
1932 and Carol in 1943. There were many years of hardships such as prairie
fires, drought, grasshoppers, hailstorms, rust and dust storms but the
Herman family successfully weathered all this and continued to be thankful
for the good years.

LADEAN HETTICH

LaDean Hettich, the only son of Mr. and Mrs. Lawrence Hettich, received his
education at Java Public School and Northern State College. He graduated
from college in 1973 with a major in elementary education and a physical
education minor. He was married to Nancy Kiesz of Bowdle in 1974.

LaDean taught sixth grade and elementary physical education at Bowdle
1973-1977 and he worked at the junior high level 1977-1980. He was also the
girls varsity basketball coach four seasons.

In the fall of 1980 LaDean moved to Rosholt where he has been teaching
language arts, reading, science and coaching girls varsity basketball. Two
of his Rosholt teams have earned state tournament berths. LaDean also
organized and coached a South Dakota All-Star Girls Basketball Team in 1983,
touring Europe in conjunction with team competition.

LAWRENCE and LAVERNE [HIEB] HETTICH

        Back: LeNette, LaDean, LaVon Front: LaVerne and Lawrence Hettich

Lawrence Hettich was born Oct. 4, 1925 southeast of Roscoe to Fred and
Roselia (Kahler) Hettich. He attended school in Montpelier Township. During
World War II Lawrence served in the U.S. Navy aboard the USS Chester C A 27
in the South Pacific and China Seas. After being discharged he attended
Barber College in San Francisco, CA and was employed at Hartzell Barber
Shop in Ipswich. In 1948 he purchased a barber shop in Roscoe from Walt
Penor. Later that year he built a new barber and beauty shop north of the
Roscoe Post Office. Lawrence married LaVerne Hieb Oct. 2, 1949 at Roscoe.

LaVern was born Dec. 2, 1929 at Bowdle to Fred J. and Christin (Werre)
Hieb. She was educated at Hosmer and School of Cosmetology at Fargo, ND.
She was employed at Milnor, Casselton and Fargo, all in North Dakota. In
1949 she purchased the shop owned by Mrs. LeRoy (Linda Hieb) Bieber. After
their marriage the Hettichs operated both businesses in their new building.
In 1953 they moved to a dairy farm 11 miles northwest of Bowdle where they
now live and are engaged in a grain and stock operation.

Lawrence and LaVerne have three children. LaDean was born Nov. 29, 1950 and
is an instructor in the Rosholt School System. LaNette was born Sept. 28,
1952. She is a CPA in Redwood City, CA. She married Doug Schlepp July 6,
1974 and they have two children: Larissa Ann (12-22-80) and Jonathan Adam
(5-17-84.) LaVon Hettich was born Oct. 11, 1959. She graduated from Java
High School in 1977 and SDSU at Brookings in 1982. She is currently
attending Iowa State University College of Veterinary Medicine in Ames.

FRED and EDNA [EISENBEIS] HETTICK

Fred and Edna Hettick are shown in their Bismarck home. Fred grew up south
of Bowdle near Tolstoy, the son of Jacob M. Hettick. He attended the area
school there, graduated from Aberdeen Business College and married Edna
Eisenbeis, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Jacob Eisenbeis. They moved to Bismarck
and work together in the real estate and insurance business.

They have two sons. Harley is a free lance photographer and DeWayne works
with his father.

Fred has a sister Mrs. Maggie Voegele in Grandview, WA and Edna's sister
Lydia Schilling lives in Bowdle.

ART and ROSE [GORNE] HINTZ

Art Hintz was born at Bowdle April 8, 1919 to John and Magdalena (Merkel)
Hintz. He attended rural school about four miles west of Bowdle. He later
worked at the CCC Camp at Custer for about one year and worked as a farm
laborer at the George Lenhardt farm near Glenham and A.H. Brown at
Mobridge. He also helped at home with the farm work until he entered the
Armed Service April 12, 1942. He served in the Aleutian Islands and British
Guiana. He received his honorable discharge in November 1945.

Gordon, Rose, Art Hintz

Upon his return from the service he married Rose Gorne of Roscoe and they
made their home on the family farm five and one-half miles northwest of
Bowdle until 1962 when they moved into Bowdle and he became manager of the
City Liquor Store until 1976. He then worked at Phillips 66 for about three
years. Presently he works part-time for Wilbert and Glenn Blumhardt on
their farm. His wife Rose worked at the nursing home until 1983 when ill
health forced her to retire.

They have one son Gordon. He is married to Gayle Dutt of Tolstoy. Gordon
works in the insurance department of Citizens Bank at Mobridge.

JOHN and MAGDELENA [MERKEL] HINTZ

John Hintz was born in South Russia Oct. 10, 1884. He immigrated to the
United States with his parents Dan and Wilhelmina (Quast) Hintz in 1886 and
they homesteaded on a farm five and one-half miles northwest of Bowdle.
John was the oldest of six children.

He married Magdelena Merkel, daughter of Jacob and Elizabeth (Hinger)
Merkel Feb. 7, 1911. They continued making their home on a farm northwest
of Bowdle, building near John's home place.

They were blessed with five children. John Jr. was married to Lydia Dabbert
of rural Bowdle. He died Nov. 30, 1983 and his wife Lydia lives in
Mobridge. Dan married Martha Dabbert (Lydia's sister.) Martha died Dec. 27,
1963 and Dan then married Mary Lou Werre, daughter of Christ and Helen
Werre of Bowdle Oct. 11, 1972. They live in Mobridge. Minnie married Emil
Dabbert of Roscoe.

They made their home on a farm north of Roscoe until Emil died June 17,
1984. Art married Rose Gorne of Roscoe. They reside in Bowdle. Edna married
Alvin Erlenbusch of Tolstoy and they live in Bowdle.

        John and Magdelena Hintz Sr.

Magdelena died June 13, 1933 at the age of 43. This left the oldest
daughter Minnie (16 at the time) to take over the household duties. As the
three boys left home to go on their own or into the Armed Forces John Hintz
and his two daughters Minnie and Edna continued operating the farm. He knew
hard times during his lifetime, but never complained. Hard work seemed to
be his spice of life. He was a faithful member of the Congregational Church.

John and his two daughters moved into Bowdle in 1945, but he remained very
active helping his son Art, who took over the family farm, as well as
helping many others. In 1947 he married Christine (Stadel) Roemmick in
Eureka. They continued to make their home in Bowdle. John Hintz died Nov.
19, 1967 at the age of 83. His second wife Christine died March 28, 1977.

WILLIAM and ROSINA [SCHICK] HINTZ

        William and Rosina Hintz

William Hintz was born to Daniel Hintz and Wilhelmina nee Quast Oct. 17,
1889 in Freeman. They moved to the Bowdle area northwest of Bowdle and
farmed many years. He married Rosina Schick, daughter of William Schick Sr.
and Margaret nee Wagner, Nov. 19, 1912. They remained on the farm until he
moved to town in 1953.

They had two daughters. Ida was born June 29, 1913 and married Rudolph Fix
Nov. 11, 1937. They have a son Maurice and two grandsons. All live in
Sacramento, CA. Bertha was born April 27, 1915. She married Ruben Aldinger
and they had one son Donald, who is married and has one daughter and four
sons.

William and Rosina adopted one son Edgar. He was born Aug. 16, 1924 and
married Loraine Fleck, daughter of Alex Fleck, Nov. 11, 1949. Two daughters
were born to them and they live in Dallas, TX.

William Hintz died May 30, 1963. Rosina Hintz died Sept. 9, 1953.

BALTHASAR and ELIZABETH [KIEST] HOERNER

Balthasar and Elizabeth (Kiest) Hoerner and daughter Rosalia migrated from
Crimea, Russia in 1893. They entered through the Port of Montreal, Canada
and rode the rails to the end of the line near or at Bowdle. They only had
$2 left when they arrived here.

How Balthasar and his family got to work for an English farmer at Hoven is
not known. Balthasar could speak no English and the Englishman could speak
no German. It must have been fun to watch them try to talk.

        Balthasar and Elizabeth Hoerner

Mike, Henry, Mary and John were born at the Miller farm, which today is the
Klocker Dairy farm near Hoven. Leo was born on the move to the homestead
6-1/2 miles east and 1/2 mile south of Bowdle or 1/2 mile south of Gretna.
The rest of the family was born here. The 13 children were:

Rosalia, born Sept. 5, 1892, married John Lowenstein and lived in Belfield
or New England, ND; died May 29, 1968.

Mike, born Dec. 9, 1893, married Louise Jistel and lived on the homestead;
died Jan. 24, 1972. Henry, born Feb. 26, 1895, a Catholic Monsignor lived
at Aberdeen; died Dec. 13, 1970.

Mary born July 31, 1896, married Philip Blondo and they lived at Grandview,
WA; died July 4, 1983.

John, born June 10, 1898, married Rose Wald and they lived at Crompton, CA;
died May 23, 1975. Leo, born March 27, 1900, married Florence Kasal and
they live at Ipswich.

Francis, born March 16, 1902, married Joe J. Heier and they lived at
Hosmer; died Jan. 20, 1975.

Genevieve, born Jan. 6, 1903, married Joe G. Dewald and they lived at
Bowdle; died Sept. 15, 1984.

Joseph, born Oct. 3, 1906, died of pneumonia Feb. 3, 1921.

Anton (Tony), born June 26, 1907, married Martha Madden and they lived at
Sioux Falls.

Peter, born June 10, 1909 worked for Singer Co.; died Feb. 20, 1976.

Anna, born Sept. 16, 1910, married Martin Abler and they live at Hoven.

George, born Nov. 20, 1912, married Rosalie Geier Baumgardner and they
lived at Aberdeen; died Sept. 6, 1981.

Balthasar was the highest contributor when St. Augustine's Catholic Church
was built in 1918. He also helped collect money for its construction.

MICHAEL and LOUISE [JISTEL] HOERNER

Mike was born to Balthasar and Elizabeth (Kiest) Hoerner Dec. 9, 1893 at
Hoven. When he was 6 years old the family moved to the homestead 6-1/2
miles east and 1/2 mile south of Bowdle or 1/2 mile south of Gretna.

Mike was the oldest son of the family. When his dad died in 1919 Mike
helped his mother run the family farm. Elizabeth died in 1923. The boys
helped farm until they finished school or found different work.

Mike and his brother John farmed as the Hoerner Brothers until the
depression year 1936. John then sold his share and Mike took over the farm.
Mike and his brother had the first radio in this part of the country. They
bought an Atwater in 1924. They also had a 32-volt light plant for the
house and barn which they purchased in 1923.

        Back: Raymond, Mike, Louise, Floyd Front: Paul and Norbert Hoerner

Mike married Louise Jistel of Cameron, TX at Sioux Falls March 3, 1924.
Four sons were born to them: Raymond Nov. 25, 1928; Floyd July 23, 1932;
Paul Oct. 3, 1940 and Norbert Feb. 2, 1944.

Mike was active in the Democratic Party Edmunds County Crop Improvement and
was Cottonwood Lake Township Clerk many years.

Mike and Louise farmed the family farm until 1971 when they moved to
Bowdle. Mike died Jan. 24, 1972. Louise died July 10, 1980.

RAYMOND and BARBARA [SCHERR] HOERNER

Raymond is the oldest son of Michael G. and Louise Hoerner. He married
Barbara (Scherr) Hoerner. Their children are as follows:

        Back: Pat, Michael, Ray, Teresa Front: Dianne, Barbara, Renae
        Hoerner

Dianne married Charles Crompton. They live in Aberdeen and have three
children. Michael was married in September 1985 and lives in Colorado.

Patrick married Joanne Reed. They live in Aberdeen and have one child.

Teresa married Timothy Stump. They have two children and live in Midland,
MI.

Ranae is the youngest daughter and lives in Denver, CO.

FLOYD and MARY [GRISMER] HOERNER

Floyd Hoerner was born at Bowdle July 23, 1932 to Michael and Louise
Hoerner. He attended country school southeast of Cottonwood Lake Township.
He was in the Army 1953-1955. He received his basic training at Fort
Campbell, KY and was stationed at Camp Rucker, AL.

        Mark, Louise, Bernice, Georgia Ann, JoAnn, Floyd, Mary Hoerner

Floyd married Mary Grismer Feb. 19, 1966. They lived with his folks on the
farm and later on bought a farm north of Hosmer. They lived there a few
years, then sold out and moved to Frederick. Floyd is now employed as a
hired hand for a farmer. They have five children: Mark, Jo Ann, Bernice,
Louise and Georgia Ann.

PAUL and BARBARA [BAUS] HOERNER

Paul was born to Mike and Louise (Jistel) Hoerner at Bowdle Oct. 3, 1940.
He attended grade school at Cottonwood Lake Southeast School and graduated
from Bowdle High School in 1958. He earned a B.S. Degree in education from
Northern State College in May 1963. Paul coached at Bonilla 1963-1964 and
Hague, ND 1964-1966.

Sept. 11, 1965 Paul married Barbara Baus at Ipswich. She is the daughter of
Alfred and Edith Baus of Ipswich. She graduated as a registered nurse from
St. Luke's School of Nursing in September 1965. She worked at the Herreid
Hospital and Bowdle Nursing Home.

        Back: Anthony, David, Paula Front: Paul, Barbara, Andrea, Andrew
        Hoerner

Paul taught physical education and coached grade basketball at Bowdle
1966-1967. They moved to Madison, WI and were city distributors for Watkins
products. They moved to Willow Lake in 1969 where Paul taught, coached and
was elementary principal until 1973. While teaching there he attended
summer school and obtained a master's degree in elementary administration.

The family moved to Aberdeen in July 1973 where Paul became employed with
Dahme Construction and still works there today.

They have five children. Anthony was born Sept. 17, 1966. He is a student
at Northern State College and employed at Kessler's Supermarket. David was
born Feb. 26, 1969. He is a sophomore at Roncalli High School in Aberdeen.
Paula was born March 17, 1972. She is in the seventh grade at Roncalli
Junior High. Andrea and Andrew were born July 22, 1978 and attend
kindergarten at Lincoln School in Aberdeen.

NORBERT and ROSEMARIE [GEIER] HOERNER

Norbert was born to Mike and Louise Hoerner of Bowdle Feb. 2, 1944. He
attended grade school at Cottonwood Lake Southwest School and graduated
from Bowdle High School in 1962.

        Back: Kevin, Dale, Craig Front: Norbert, Jason, Rosemarie Hoerner

Norbert was drafted into the Army Oct. 20, 1965 and after basic training at
Fort Leonard Wood, MO and six months of schooling at Fort Belvoir, VA, he
served the rest of his duty in Ascom, Korea. After his discharge in July
1967, Norbert started farming on the Hoerner homestead and remains there
today.

Norbert went to artificial insemination school in 1969 and raises
registered Simmental cattle holding annual production sales.

Norbert married Rosemarie Geier of Roscoe Jan. 30, 1971. She is the
daughter of Wendelin and Maggie Geier.

They have four sons: Dale, age 13; Kevin, age 10; Craig, age 9 and Jason,
age 8. They are students of the Bowdle School.

EMIL and BARBARA [BENTZ] HOFF

Emil and Barbara Hoff are best known by Bowdlelites as owners of the cafe.
They moved to Bowdle in 1950 from a farm near Eureka and purchased the cafe
from the Mertzes.

Their new venture was to remodel the business. They also made their living
quarters upstairs. After operating the cafe successfully five years they
moved back to Eureka.

        Back: Shirley, Kathy, Salona, Priscilla Front: Emil and Barbara Hoff

Their only daughter to graduate from Bowdle was Salona. She is now married
to Roger Wendt and lives in Largo, FL where she teaches and is a librarian.
They have three children.

Priscilla was married to Harvey Pfeifle of Eureka, who was accidentally
killed in a farm accident. She lives in Aberdeen and is a secretary at
Central High School. She has four children.

Kathy lives in Aberdeen and is in the real estate business. She and her
husband Robert Undlin have two children.

Shirley married Leslie Bucholz, who died. She has two children and lives in
Mobridge where she works for the Mobridge Tribune.

After being in the cafe business at Eureka, Emil and Barbara decided to
move to Aberdeen. Emil was a home contractor building and remodeling many
homes. They are now retired there.

EGART and EMMA [MARTZ] HOFFMAN

Egart Hoffman was born Oct. 3, 1903 near Onaka, the son of Jacob B.
Hoffmann and his wife Marea, nee Ketterling. Egart attended the Bowdle
Schools and Feb. 6, 1927 married Emma Martz, who was born Jan. 6, 1906.
They lived on his parents farm 8-1/2 years until Egart Hoffman's health
failed and he could not continue with the hard work on the farm. They moved
into Bowdle the fall of 1935 and Egart entered the hospital at Shakopee, MN
for care.

        Egart and Emma          Marvin and MaeNerva

His health improved and he was able to manage the pool hall in Bowdle a few
years and in 1944 he bought the Champlin Filling and Bulk Station which he
managed until his health failed and he died July 7, 1969.

Egart and Emma had two children, four grandchildren and five great-
grandchildren. Their son Marvin Glenn was born Nov. 25, 1929 and married
Ellen Walth of Hosmer. He was employed at the Walth Store until it closed.
Then he was employed at the State School for Children in Redfield where he
died Nov. 14, 1981. They had one daughter Mrs. Sheila (Steve) Nelson. After
Marvin's death his widow remarried Arlys Winegar of Redfield.

Emma and Egart's daughter MaeNerva Jane married Russel Bender of Java.
After graduating from Bowdle High School she attended an airline school in
Minneapolis and worked as a teletype operator for an airline company in
Chicago. She is now employed at the nursing home in Selby. They have three
daughters Susan (Mrs. Dan Luning) of Spring City, TN; Patricia (Mrs. Bill
Stickney) of Mobridge and Jennifer Marea who lives with her parents.

GOTTFRED and ELIZABETH [BUECHLER] HOFFMAN

Gottfred Hoffman was born in Kulm, Bessarabia, South Russia Jan. 15, 1890.
His father Johann Hoffman died in a fire that destroyed his flour mill in
Russia. In 1898 Gottfred's mother Louise (Hintz) Hoffman brought his two
sisters Maria and Matilda and him to the United States. His older brother
Nathanial had come over some years before. They came over on the S.S. Kaiser
Friedrick the Great, arriving in New York Nov. 8, 1898.

They then traveled to Bowdle by train. They stayed with his uncle Daniel
Hintz Sr. for several months until his mother married Andreas Laib April
27, 1899 in Hosmer.

Nov. 7, 1910 Gottfred married Elizabeth (Buechler.) They farmed about five
miles west of Bowdle. Nine children were born to Gottfred and Elizabeth
Hoffman.

        Gottfred and Elizabeth Hoffman

Magdalena: born Oct. 10, 1911 near Bowdle, married Carl Presser in Sidney,
MT. They farmed in the Vida area many years. Five children were born to
this union: Darlene, Arlene, Robert, Walter and Harvey. Carl died Sept. 1,
1968. Magdalena now lives in Wolf Point, MT.

Albert: Born Sept. 27, 1913 near Bowdle, married Martha (Eggebrecht) July
22, 1939 in Circle, MT. They farmed in the Vida area until they retired.
They now make their home in Wolf Point, MT. Two daughters were born to this
union: Jeanette and Bonnie.

Theodore: born Sept. 24, 1919 near Bowdle joined the Army in 1940. He died
while serving his country during World War II Dec. 15, 1942. He was buried
in Schofield Barracks Cemetery. After the war his body was moved to the
National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific in the Punchbowl Crater.

Hilda: Born Jan. 7, 1917 near Bowdle, married Elga L. Green March 6, 1936
in Wolf Point, MT. They followed construction work until 1942 when Elga
went to work for the Housing Authority of the city of Los Angeles until his
retirement in 1974. Hilda went to work in 1954 at Harbor General Hospital
until retiring in 1974. There were three children born to this union: Lyle,
Lelend and Janice. They have lived in Torrance, CA since 1950.

Emma: Born Aug. 4, 1918 near Bowdle, married Clarence Madison Feb. 14, 1938
in Wolf Point, MT. They were in the restaurant business. Four girls were
born to this union: Bernice, Sylvia, Gracie and Dianna. Emma died May 15,
1953.

Elsie: Born April 23, 1921 near Bowdle, married Denny Denholm in Spokane,
WA. They were later divorced and she married Donald Emrick. He died a few
years ago. Elsie is now living in the nursing home in Circle, MT.

Elnora: Born Oct. 14, 1922 near Bowdle married Howard Remmich Dec. 8, 1941.
He entered the Army and served in the Pacific. After his military duties
Howard went to college and then to the seminary to prepare for the
ministry. Rev. and Mrs. Howard Remmich have served many churches in Iowa,
Kansas, Montana and South Dakota. They are now retired and living near
Pierce NE. Five children were born to this union: H. Dale, Shirley,
Kathren, Anthony and Rick.

Eva: Born May 29, 1924 near Bowdle, married Virgil Rogers in Yuma, AZ Sept.
9, 1950. They had their own landscaping business. Virgil died March 17,
1974. Eva now lives in Roswell, NM. There were no children born to this
union.

Edgar (Hoffman) Hintz: Born Aug. 16, 1925 near Bowdle, married Lorraine
(Fleck) Nov. 27, 1949 in Java. Edgar was only two weeks old when his mother
died. He was raised by his father's cousin and wife William and Rosina
Hintz on their farm west of Bowdle. In recent years Edgar has been a
salesman and travels throughout South Dakota. There were two daughters born
to this union: Linda and Carol.

After the death of Elizabeth in 1925, Gottfred married Rosina Sandmeier
Jan. 10, 1927 in Bowdle. They continued to live on the farm west of Bowdle
until February 1928 when they loaded the eight children into a Model T Ford
and moved to Vida, MT where they farmed. There were five children born to
this union.

Lorraine: Born November 1928, died January 1929.

Phyllis: Born Feb. 6, 1930 near Vida, MT, married Raymond Abraham May 7,
1949 in Wolf Point, MT. They farmed in the Vida area. There were 12
children born to this union: Kenneth, Leslie, Rosa, Mary, Anna, Abe, Nancy,
Sally, Brenda, Henry, Betty and Vicky.

Harold: Born May 9, 1931 near Vida, MT, married Helen Johnson Feb. 28, 1953
in Sidney MT. They farmed near Richey, MT. Three children were born to this
union: Mark, Judy and Jerry.

Dorothy: Born Jan. 11, 1936 near Vida, MT, married Bert Thorpe June 22,
1963 in Billings, MT. Dorothy is a registered nurse at Harbor General
Hospital in Torrance, CA. They live in Carson, CA. No children were born to
this union.

Donald: Born May 14, 1942 in Wolf Point, MT, married Faith Perry June 15,
1965 in Billings, MT. Donald is working for Peery Painting Contractor in
Milwaukie, OR where they reside. There were two daughters born to this
union: Kimberly and Kathryn.

Rosina (Sandmeier) Hoffman died April 6, 1981 in Sidney, MT.


JOHN and BERTHA [SEEFRIED] HOFFMAN

Their honeymoon trip brought John Hoffman and his bride, the former Bertha
Seefried, from their native land Russia to the United States. John was born
Jan. 7, 1888 to Mr. and Mrs. Philip Hoffman. He received an eighth grade
education. Bertha was born Jan. 14, 1888. They made their first home on the
Jergenson farm with John's brother William and family.

John and Bertha had three children. John was born Nov. 30, 1910. He married
the former Virginia Wilson and they have one son Robert. Oscar was born
March 3, 1914. He was killed in an automobile accident in 1936. Erna was
born July 21, 1916 and married Reinhold Huber. They had two children:
Darlene and Bruce.

        John, Bertha, Erna, John Hoffman

After some years spent farming the Hoffman brothers brought their families
to town in 1920. John bought the house on 3rd Avenue which is just north of
the present Methodist Church and William built the house just south of the
church for his family. John operated the Standard Oil Station and a dray
line and when that was not a successful venture, he sold out and bought the
Dorwin farm. In 1933 they again sold the farm machinery and spent a year in
California where John worked in a winery, returning in 1934 to live on the
farm. Erna graduated from the Bowdle High School in 1935.

In 1946 John and Bertha again sold the farm and came to town to live on 4th
Avenue. He worked for Charles Commet and for the electric high line that
brought electricity to the REA customers.

John Hoffman died June 23, 1955. Bertha died Sept. 21, 1979.

ARTHUR and KATHERINE [LEMKE] HOFFMANN

Arthur and Katherine Hoffmann were born and reared in the Bowdle area.
Arthur was the son of Jacob and Marea Ketterling Hoffmann, born Aug. 24,
1907 at Onaka. His father was born in South Russia in 1877 and died in
1966. His mother was born in Russia in 1875 and died in 1955. Arthur was a
Bowdle High School graduate.

Katherine M. Lemke was born in 1912 at Bowdle to Richard and Ella Lemke.
After graduating from Bowdle she attended college in Brookings and
graduated with a bachelor of science in home economics and was employed in
this field 10 years.

Arthur Hoffmann and Katherine Lemke were married in 1944 at Bowdle.
Previous to their marriage Arthur completed his military service. They
established their home in Bowdle where they lived 25 years until Arthur
died in 1969. He had been in business with his father and brother in the
Hoffmann Bulk and Gas Station. Arthur sold his interest in the business and
became a rural mail carrier for 25 years.

        Back: Eileen, Ellan, Ernestine Front: Art and Katherine Hoffmann

Arthur and Katherine had three daughters. Ellan Hoffmann Vannoy is the

Care Unit in Children's Hospital in Milwaukee, WI.

Eileen Hoffmann McEnroe is a homemaker in Moffit, ND. Her children are
Thomas and Martha.

Ernestine Hoffmann is a chemist for a precious metal plating company in
Milwaukee, WI.

Arthur Hoffmann was an avid hunter, a firstrate target shot and fisherman.
He became a cabinet maker, carpenter and mechanic in his spare time. He
also served on the Edmunds County Draft Board 15 years.

The Hoffmann daughters were active in 4-H activities. They raised and
showed sheep, completed many home economic projects and raised a variety of
garden vegetables and fruits which they exhibited at state and county fairs
and also completed handicrafts.

The family was devoted to their church and pursued many building and
maintenance projects to show their devotion.

JACOB B. and MAREA [KETTERLING] HOFFMANN

Jacob B. Hoffmann was born Feb. 12, 1877 at Narenberg, Russia to Fred and
Katherina (Merkel) Hoffmann. His parents were of German birth and had gone
to Russia. His father died when J.B. was a young man and his mother
remarried.

When the Russian Czar began calling the young German men, as well as
Russian, to serve in the military, J.B. decided to go to America where he
had a sister living at Eureka. Out of funds for traveling the young man
managed to stowaway on a luxury liner anchored in the Black Sea near Odessa,
Russia. After several days of hiding until the ship was out to sea, he
volunteered his services in the kitchen (galley) to pay for his passage.
Upon arrival at New York City in 1900, he called his sister who sent him a
train ticket to come be with her family. He was then 23 years old.

Mr. Hoffmann recalled his first night in Bowdle looking for work. It was a
bitterly cold winter night when he arrived on the train. That night a fire
started in the wooden structure that housed the Mason Store. It had
smoldered a long time before it was discovered. Mr. Hoffmann helped carry
out merchandise, including caskets, hardware and groceries. He joined the
townspeople carrying water from hand pumps in a bucket brigade, but that
building and all others on that side of the street were destroyed. It was
thought the fire started in the basement storage area where a lighted
kerosene lamp was being used to keep potatoes from freezing.

Mr. Mason then built the brick building that housed his store and First
State Bank of Bowdle (later known as Bowdle State Bank), now the site of
Ozzie's Super Valu and Erv's Furniture.

Mr. Hoffmann took up land five miles northwest of Onaka in Madison Township
in Edmunds County. In September 1902 he married Marea Ketterling. She was
born in Bartegoba, South Russia April 4, 1875 to Valentine and Elizabeth
Ketterling. The young couple started out like all pioneers in those days
with little to go on. They built a five-room house where Egart, Arthur and
Martha Orvella were born.

Egart Hoffman was born in 1903, married Emma N. Martz and died July 7,
1969. Arthur Albert Hoffmann was born in 1907, married Katherine Lemke and
died Sept. 13, 1969. Martha Orvella lived two short years and died in
December 1924.

After some years farming Mr. Hoffmann bought a threshing rig, complete with
a cook car and sleeping car. Besides his farmwork he hired out to thresh
grain for neighboring farmers. The crew in those days had to pitch the
grain in bundles into the separator and included a bundle hauling rig and
power for the engine was created by steam, so a straw rig with a team of
horses had to bring in the straw for burning, then there was the water rig
and man to haul water for the engine also. It meant rising very early in
the morning for the engineer, fireman, straw haulers and water rig.
Threshing usually went on until the snow fell. Hoffmann sold the threshing
rig before leaving the farm.

J.B. Hoffmann held several township offices and served on the school board.
The family moved to Bowdle in the fall of 1918 and purchased the house
where Dr. Adajar now lives from Henry B. Baer shortly after it was built.

In 1918 J.K. Kurle and J.B. Hoffmann started the Western Oil Bulk Service
selling gasoline, kerosene, oil and greases of all kinds. In 1921 Hoffmann
sold his share to Kurle and in 1923 Kurle resold to J.B. Hoffmann and son
Art who started a filling and bulk station. In 1944 they sold it to Egart
who operated the business under the name of Champlin Filling and Bulk
Station.

        Jacob B and Marea Hoffmann

Jacob B. Hoffmann was active in community affairs, served as mayor of
Bowdle three successive terms and was mayor during the Golden Anniversary
celebration in 1936. He held various offices in St. John's Ev. Lutheran
Church and for years rang the bell calling members to worship.

Marea Hoffmann died Aug. 15, 1955. Jacob remarried to Mrs. Frieda Martz.
Jacob died Jan. 17 1966 and his second wife died Feb. 27, 1974.

From Bowdle they moved to Rapid City where they spent 24 years in the Rapid

ROBERT and ARLENE [RILEA] HOLSWORTH

Robert Holsworth was born March 19, 1921 in Willow Lake to Walter and Edith
Simpson Holsworth. Arlene Rilea Holsworth was born Jan. 31, 1922 near
Worthington, MN to Elmer and Bulah Wagar Rilea.

Bob and his family moved considerably during the Dirty Thirties, his father
finding work wherever possible as a caterpillar operator and mechanic with
road construction outfits, in logging camps and on corporation farms. In
1935 the family moved to Carlton, MN where the elder Holsworth became a
star route mail contractor for the next 25 years. Bob attended all four
years of high school at Carlton, having attended 13 schools in the previous
eight years in three states.

Arlene's family moved from the Worthington area to a farm near Mahtowa and
later to Barnum where she graduated from Barnum (MN) High School in 1940. It
was during this time Bob and Arlene began going together and in the fall
1941, having completed five years of printing apprenticeship at Carlton,
Bob went to Chicago and March 28, 1942, Arlene and Bob were married in
Chicago.

Jan. 2, 1943 Bob entered Army service at Ft. Sheridan, IL and Arlene
returned to Minnesota to reside with her parents and await the birth of their
first child and Bob's discharge which came in October 1945 after spending
two years in England, France and Germany in the Chemical Warfare Service.

Following his discharge the Holsworths returned to Chicago where Bob was
employed by the C&NW Railroad. In 1953 he resigned from his position of
investigator in the freight claim department to become a linotype operator
on the Wheaton (IL) Daily Journal. The pull of newspapering had lured him
from railroading and the following year they returned to northern Minnesota
and a series of newspaper jobs finally led to Bowdle by way of Barnum, MN;
Clarkfield, MN; Bryant, Gregory and Redfield.

They have three children. Mike is married to Mary Rubio Holsworth and an
engineering officer on a search ship of the Arco Oil Fleet. They live in
Kingman, AZ. Dan is married to Roseanna Schmierer Holsworth and is sports
editor of the Madison Daily Leader in Madison and they have two children.
Sheila married Joel Hoffman and is a registered nurse at the Bowdle
Hospital. They have one daughter.

In 1971 Bob suffered his second heart attack and was forced to sell The
Bowdle Pioneer to Bill Jahraus. They moved to Redfield for two years and
then to Hoven where Arlene was employed by their son Dan who had purchased
the Hoven Review. When Dan sold that paper in 1978, Bob and Arlene moved
back to Bowdle.

ART and ELLEN [HAGELE] HOLWEGER

Art Holweger was born in Harding County Oct. 5, 1912. He was the son of
Fred and Louise Huber Holweger, who were some of the first settlers to
homestead in that county. He attended rural school and later attended
Plainview Academy in Redfield.

Ellen Hagele was born south of Bowdle in 1913. She was the daughter of Mr.
and Mrs. Gottlieb Hagele, early settlers in Odessa Township. The Hageles
migrated from Russia in the 1880's. She attended rural school and graduated
from Bowdle High School.

Art and Ellen were married in June 1941 in the Bowdle Seventh-day Adventist
Church, of which they are still members. They purchased the former Em.
Knecht farm in Hudson Township, which they still call their home. They have
two daughters Kathy and Peggy.

        Art and Ellen Holweger and Families Back: Kathy, Gary, Lance,
        Peggy, Ellen, Art Front: Heathe, Jodi, Heidi, Amanda, Hans

Kathy married Gary Widicker. They are living on a farm near Heaton, ND.
They have three children Heathe, Hans and Heidi. They are farming as a
family which keeps them busy.

Peggy married Lance Liebelt. They live in Thousand Oaks, CA. They have two
daughters Amanda and Jodi. After graduating from college Peggy taught two
years at Boys Town, NE. She also taught when they moved to North Carolina.
At present she does secretarial work and is a part-time receptionist. Lance
is employed at The Voice of Prophecy.

Life on the farm has changed considerably since they started farming. The
coming of REA changed things. Farming has had its ups and downs. Hail wiped
out the crops in 1969 and 1972.

The winter 1950 will long be remembered. Being snowbound for three weeks
was rather trying. The only communication was by telephone and that didn't
always work. There was no way to get produce to town. Mail service was nil.
Once during that time the mail carrier arranged to have mail delivered by
plane. There was no out-going mail. Children had to walk to school. Relief
finally came when some Caterpillars were hired to open the roads as other
snow removal proved inadequate.

Not all winters have been bad. There have been some very mild ones. The
summers have been rather pleasant. Crops seem to have made up in the good
years what was lost in the bad ones.

Art and Ellen are semi-retired. They still live on the farm but spend some
time visiting the children and grandchildren. They usually try to spend some
of their vacation in California during the winter months. During the summer
they seem to be busy on the farm and enjoy having the family come home.

JOHN and MARY [KOHNER] HOVEN

John J. was the first white child born in the Hoven Territory June 28,
1883. In 1905 John and his brother Pete started a livery stable in Lebanon
and continued until the railroad came to Hoven in 1907. Then John sold his
interest and moved back to Hoven where he started his own livery stable.

He drove passengers places and also was a driver for Dr. Mertens, MD. Often
he drove many miles, sometimes as far as the Missouri River.  He also did
dray work, hauling much of the bricks and supplies for St. Anthony's School
from Bowdle. He ran a meat market, butchering much of the meat himself.

        Mary and John Hoven

In 1910 he married Mary Kohner. He built a home in Hoven and lived there
until 1914, when they sold their home and livery stable and moved to Bowdle
where John went into partnership buying stock with Joe Wendling.

In the early part of 1915 the Hovens and Wendlings moved to Hump Creek, 12
miles south of McIntosh to homestead, living there until the spring of 1918
when they sold their ranch and moved back to Bowdle and John continued to
buy livestock from time to time.

They purchased the Judge Ham home and lived there until the fall of 1948.
John's chief occupation was stock buying, farming and ranching. In 1935
John and his son Vincent purchased the first rubber tired tractor which was
equipped from the factory. It was a John Deere Model D. In 1948 they moved
to an apartment above the theater where they lived until 1954 when they
purchased a home in Santa Barbara, CA.

John and Mary had three children: Mrs. John (Genevieve) Mertes of Hoven,
Mrs. William (Vivian) Snethen of Santa Barbara, CA and Vincent of Bowdle.

John died Nov. 19, 1975 and Mary died Aug. 10, 1984. They are buried in
Calvary Catholic Cemetery at Santa Barbara, CA.

VINCENT and DORIS [GOETTLING] HOVEN

Vincent was born June 15, 1912 to John J. and Mary Hoven. He married Doris
Goettling, daughter of Paul and Bertha Goettling. Doris was born May 8,
1926 at Bowdle.

Vincent has been a longtime rancher and farmer. He built the Bowdle

        Vincent and Doric Hoven

Doris was employed many years as a postal clerk at Bowdle Post Office and

Democrats many years. She is also chairman of the District 25 Democratic

They have two children. Corrine, now Mrs. Philip Brewster, lives in Eagle
River, AK, a suburb of Anchorage. She has her master's degree and is a
registered pharmacist. Perry is a student at Worsham College of Mortuary
Science in Chicago. The Hovens have one grandchild, Marissa Corrine
Brewster, who is 4 years old and lives with her parents in Eagle River, AK.

Vincent has been a member of Bowdle Volunteer Fire Department 50 years and
has been active in the Democratic Party as committeeman and is now the
State Central Committeeman of Edmunds County.

BRUCE and DOLORITA [THOMAS] HUBER

Bruce Huber was born Aug. 13, 1938 to Reinhold and Erna (Hoffman) Huber. A
graduate of Bowdle High School, he married Dolorita Thomas, daughter of
Adam and Jennie (Malsom) Thomas Jr. She grew up on a farm northeast of
Bowdle and after graduating from Bowdle High School she worked at Bowdle
State Bank. Bruce and Dolorita (Del) were married Sept. 3, 1961 and they
made their first home in Bowdle.

In October 1962 they moved to the Walter Reiner farm southeast of town and
milked cows. Bruce had been in the combining business with his father,
which was started in 1950.

Farm life memories include the 1966 March Blizzard when they had to use the
car and tractor to power the milking machines. Then, due to the shortage of
water, they tried to get the cows to drink the milk. Snowbanks were so high
they had to break out a bedroom window to get out of the house. And because
there was no electricity, they went to their basement, blanketed off a
small area and by the use of a small propane stove, were able to keep warm.
During the three days they were without electricity, Bruce managed to get
water for their use by hand turning the wheel on the pump.

        Back: Shonda and Carla Front: Del, Bruce, Marc Huber

At that time they had two daughters. Shonda was born Jan. 12, 1962 and
Carla Feb. 5 1964.

They moved to the Art Buechler farm nine miles north of Bowdle April 1.
1967 and their daughters started school in Hosmer. They moved again July
17, 1971 to a farm just north of Bowdle. The following year Bruce gave up
the combining work and its travels.

Del started working in the office at Bowdle Hospital and in 1977 she
accepted a position with Montana-Dakota Utilities Co. and Bruce started
working at Bowdle Livestock Sales Co. One surprise to the Huber family was
the arrival of a son Marc, born in November 1979. Two years later they
purchased the Fred Rieger house and moved into Bowdle and as Del says, "No
more milking cows."

EDWARD and LYDIA [HABERER] HUBER

Edward Huber was born Sept. 29, 1907 at Hosmer, the son of Mr. and Mrs.
Jacob Huber, natives of Russia. As a young lad he went to work for farmers
in the neighborhood and on threshing crews, besides helping at home. At the
age of 12, he started working full-time with the threshing crew from August
until November each year.

He recalls that in 1934, the first year of his marriage, they did not get a
bushel of grain and lived by working for the W.P.A, a government program,
for which he received $3.75 a day and this included the labor of the man
and his own team of four horses. That was their total living income. They
had to sell all except two or three milk cows due to no feed and those two
or three head came through the winter with only two sacks of thistles for
feed. That was the year the government paid farmers $3 a head for calves
and $13 a head for cows, then they were shot and buried in ditches.

        Lydia and Edward Huber

Edward Huber married Lydia Haberer Nov. 16, 1933 at Bowdle. She was born
June 23, 1910 to Christian and Barbara (Seefried) Haberer, natives of
Russia. Lydia worked for Adolph and Sarah Braufman for two years for $3 a
week and after the first year she got $1 a week raise. Then she was
employed at Robert deMalignon Funeral Home, the home of Morris Jones who
owned the City Drug Store and for E.L. Riba, the buttermaker at the Bowdle
Creamery.

Lydia Huber tells of working all week, walking three miles to work and then
babysitting on weekends and all summer for no pay at all. The children she
took care of were 8, 10 and 12 years old.

The Hubers were married during the Depression Years and moved onto the farm
north of town. She recalls using a lantern in the basement to keep their
vegetables from freezing and a kerosene lantern upstairs which they carried
room to room for light. The 1934 drought was most severe. Mrs. Huber
recalls how they tried to get feed for the cattle to bring them through the
winter. She and Edward each sat on a side of the stone boat (a wooden flat
bed with wooden runners) drawn by a horse. They went through the cornfield,
each pulling up the stunted cornstalks to save for feed. Then the cattle
refused to eat the corn--lack of rain had made the corn bitter. All that
work and nothing to feed the animals. Such was the life in the 1930's.

Their lives changed in 1965 when they moved to Bowdle and Lydia went to
work at the Bowdle Nursing Home, where she is still employed.

Edward and Lydia have three children. Janice was born Oct. 23, 1936 and is
the wife of Tom Stangl. They live in Sterling, VA and have three children:
Janell, Janeen and Tom Allen. Lyle Huber was born May 11, 1944 and married
Rita Haar. They live on the Huber farm north of Bowdle with their children
Weylin, Brent and Kevin. Roger Huber was born Sept. 3, 1949. He married
Margie Anderson and is a trucker.

HENRY and HULDA [SCHLECHT] HUBER

Hulda W. Schlecht, daughter of Gottfried and Minnie Schlecht was born near
Java Jan. 22, 1919 and since March 1937 has made her home in Mobridge. She
attended schools in Trail City and the country school near Bowdle. She
married Henry Huber of Mobridge Aug. 29, 1938 at her parents home. Henry
worked for the B & R Motors as manager of the Body Repair Shop until ill
health forced him to cease this labor in 1970. Hulda worked at several
stores in Mobridge and her last job was with the Brown Palace Hotel. She
retired in April 1981. Henry died Dec. 21, 1980.

        Henry and Hulda Huber

        Patricia and Charles Fenske     Susan Rae Fenske

Hulda writes, "We were blessed with a daughter Patricia (Pat) Ann Huber who
graduated from Mobridge High School, Class of 1958. She married Charles
Fenske of Herreid Dec. 19, 1965. Charles was the son of Carl and Clorice
Fenske of Mobridge. The nuptials took place at Trinity Lutheran Church.
They have a daughter Susan Rae, who was born Dec. 20, 1970 and attends
Mobridge School. Charles works for Montana-Dakota Utilities Co. and Pat is
working at McCullan-Swanson Dental Clinic. All are residents of Mobridge."

Hulda reminisces: "I can remember going to school at Trail City, my dad
driving the school bus. Those were fun days. My dad made over a Dodge car
to be used as a school bus.

"When we lived near Bowdle we had a bad thunder and lightning storm.
Lightning struck about a quarter of a mile west of our home, killing some of
our cattle. I was sitting by the open door and it knocked me across the
room. My brother was supposed to go get the cows so we could milk them, but
didn't go which was good because he would have been there about the time
lightning struck."

"We had bad times and good times and worked hard but enjoyed every bit of
it. In those days we did all our field work with horses. We had no
tractors. We really enjoyed school, made a lot of nice friends and had nice
teachers."

"Another thing that sticks with me was when the government dug trenches and
shot the cattle and put them in the trenches and covered them up. I thought
that was terrible. I remember one evening we could not go home from school
because it was storming too bad. We stayed at the Henry Leidholt farm home
near the school and thought that was fun."

"I get to Bowdle once in a while, have aunts and cousins living there and
like your meat market at the south edge of town."

JACOB and SABINA [WALZ] HUBER

Jacob Huber was born to Conrad and Wilhelmina Mueller Huber in 1858 in
Heilbronn, South Russia. In 1884 he married Sabina Walz, daughter of Jacob
and Fredricka Walz, also born in Heilbronn in 1861.

They had nine children, six of whom grew to adulthood. They were Anna (Mrs.
David Leidholdt), Charlotte (Mrs. Christ Jakober), Eugene, Olga (Mrs. Edwin
Herrboldt), Otto and Richard.

The Hubers moved to the United States in 1887 and settled in the Freeman
area. In 1896 they came to the Bowdle area, homesteading five miles east
and two north of Bowdle. Grandpa Huber had about five quarters of land he
eventually divided among his children. In 1919 he retired to Bowdle. Jacob
Huber could speak Armenian, Russian, Turkish, English, as well as German.

Oct. 2, 1922 Jacob Huber was burned on the hands and face while fighting a
prairie fire. He reportedly saved three men. He never fully recovered from
his burns and died March 15, 1929 at the age of 71.

JACOB J. and MAGDALINA [HOFF] HUBER

Jacob J. Huber was born Sept. 3, 1879 in Glueckstahl, South Russia. He
immigrated to America with his parents in 1897. The family settled near
Hosmer. Jacob worked for the railroad and on various farms. He married
Magdalina Hoff, daughter of Jacob and Magdalina (Ladner) Hoff, Feb. 1,
1903. She was born Nov. 24, 1883 at Tripp. Her family moved to the Eureka
area when she was 8 years old.

After their marriage Jacob and Magdalina homesteaded east of Eureka. In
1908 they moved to a farm north of Leola. Their last farm was located six
miles southeast of Hosmer. In 1943 they retired in Bowdle.

Their ten children include Jacob Jr. (died 1930,) Edward, Albert, Reinhold
(died 1984,) all of Bowdle; Rueben of Portland, OR: Eugene of Napa, CA;
Calvin of Napa, CA (died 1982,) Mrs. Emma Haberer of Bowdle, Mrs. Martha
Kiesz of Aberdeen and Mrs. Anna Polloreo of Antioch, CA.

        Jacob J. Huber Family Back: Martha, Albert, Calvin, Reinhold,
        Reuben, Edward, Emma. Front: Eugene, Jacob J., Magdalina, Anna
        Huber.

Jacob Huber had two brothers Carl and John and two sisters Barbara Heyne
and Margaretha Bieber, as well as two half sisters. Magdalina had three
brothers Jacob, Henry and John Hoff and four sisters Mrs. Kate Opp, Mrs.
Christina Gohl, Lydia Bertch, all deceased and Mrs. Emma Mehlhoff, who is
90 years old and living in Colonial Manor at Ipswich.

Magdalina Huber died May 29, 1957 and Jacob Huber died Jan. 7, 1961.

JOHN and KATHRINE [VOEGLE] HUBER

John was born in Odessa, Germany in 1875. He and his older brother Jake
came to America in 1889. They settled in Bowdle where John stayed while
Jake moved to Oregon. John married Carolyn Merkel in 1903 and built their
house in Bowdle, which still stands today.

John and Carolyn had six children. Emma (Erbe) served as postmaster in
Bowdle from 1940 until her death in 1957; Mary Huber, Bowdle (deceased;)
Adela Rush, Sioux City, IA (deceased;) Albert Huber, Glenwood Springs, CO
(deceased; ) Bertha Rerdesil, Stockton, CA and Eva Chilstrom, Gold Bay, WA.

Carolyn Huber died in 1916 during the big flu epidemic. In 1924 John
married Kathrine Voegle and had six more children: Alvina Huber, Bowdle;
Delorse Benthin, Arlington, WA; Wilmer Huber, Minneapolis, MN; Violet
Miller, Cresbard; Alvin Huber, Denver, CO and Cletus Huber, Newell.

John died in 1946 and Kathrine in 1973.

John, one of the first residents of Bowdle, was a farmer and owned a farm
one mile east of Bowdle and one-half mile north of old Highway 12. He was a
jack of all trades and helped build many of the first buildings in Bowdle.
John built and owned the building on main street now known as the Main
Stop. Along with his home, John built a cement smoke house on the Huber
property. It is believed to be the only smoke house still standing.

        John Huber

John was quite active in the community. He served on the city council and
school board. He was also a member of St. John's Evangelical Lutheran
Church and a member of the church council. He had 14 grandchildren and
eight great-grandchildren.

LYLE and RITA [HAAR] HUBER

Lyle was born at Hoven May 11, 1944 to Ed and Lydia Huber. He attended
Bowdle School and after graduation continued farming with his father.

Lyle married Rita Haar Sept. 19, 1965. She was born Oct. 16. 1946 at Hoven
to Ervin and Lucille Haar of Onaka. Rita attended Roscoe School and after
graduation she was employed at Bowdle State Bank. Later she was bookkeeper
at Bowdle Hospital until it closed and then was bookkeeper at Bowdle
Nursing Home.

Lyle and Rita operate a dairy and grain farm just northwest of Bowdle. This
farm was owned by Ed Huber, which was previously owned by Christ Haberer.
Besides farming Lyle has the hobby of flying, belonging to a flying club a
number of years.

Lyle and Rita have three children. Weylin was born March 28, 1972, Brent
June 30, 1977 and Kevin May 3, 1983.

The Huber family are members of the Church of God and active in many church
activities.

OSCAR E. and JUDITH [SHEPPARD] HUBER

Oscar E. Huber and Judith E. Sheppard Huber are at home five miles east and
two miles north of Bowdle on the farm homesteaded by Jacob and Sabina Huber
in 1896. Oscar and Judith were married in 1974 and have four children: Paul
Jacob, 1975; Kirk Allen, 1977; Ryan Richard, 1981 and Rosann Inez, 1983.

Judy, the daughter of Wilbur Sheppard and Inez Cooper Sheppard, was an
Extension Home Economist for Brown County at the time she was married. She
received her training and degree from North Dakota State University in
Fargo.

        Back: Oscar, Paul, Kirk, Judy Front: Ryan and Rosann Huber

Oscar made his home on the farm most of his life, but also taught one year
in a rural school, 11 years at Roscoe High School and one year at Hosmer
High School. He served 12 years in the South Dakota House of
Representatives. He graduated from Bowdle High School, received a degree at
Northern State College in Aberdeen and earned graduate credits from the
University of Minnesota and Northern. Being vice-president of Edmunds WEB
he helped with the membership drive and spent time promoting the WEB
domestic water project.

OTTO and HELEN [GROSZ] HUBER

Otto A. Huber was born Nov. 11, 1897 to Jacob and Sabina (Walz) Huber, who
immigrated to South Dakota from Krimea, Russia. Otto was the fifth of six
children and grew up on a farm near Bowdle. He married Helen Grosz Sept.
1, 1924 in Eureka. (The name Grosz was later changed to Gross.)

        Helen and Otto Huber

Helen Grosz was born Dec. 24, 1893 to Christ G. and Katherine (Mueller)
Grosz. Helen was the fourth of twelve children. Five died of scarlet fever
in 1907. Helen's mother died in 1909.

Otto and Helen first lived in Timber Lake and McLaughlin. They returned to
Bowdle where he was meat department manager in the Bowdle Super Valu Store
until he retired in 1963. He was also the city auditor and finance officer
for 25 years.

Otto and Helen had two sons. Robert was born April 10, 1927. He married
Ramona Schaible July 20, 1948 and they have two daughters Roxanne and
Randee. They have taught in several South Dakota cities and for the past 16
years have lived in Sioux Falls where Bob is a math instructor at Lincoln
High and Ramona works part-time in the district office of the Hoover
Company.

Dale Huber was born Nov. 16, 1934. He married Jeanne Sampson March 1, 1957.
Their children are Danny, Jeff and Jan. They have taught in South Dakota,
Iowa and for the past 16 years have been with the Hills-Beaver Creek School
System in Minnesota where Dale is a coach and history teacher and Jeanne is
an elementary instructional aide.

Otto Huber died Oct. 6, 1983. Helen is currently a resident at Bowdle
Nursing Home.

REINHOLD and ERNA [HOFFMAN] HUBER

Reinhold Huber and Erna Hoffman were married May 19, 1936. Reinhold, son of
Mr. and Mrs. Jacob Huber, was born April 20, 1914 in Leola and received his
high school education there. Erna, daughter of John and Bertha Hoffman, was
born June 21, 1916 on a farm near Bowdle. She was a member of the class of
1935 of Bowdle High School. They made their home in Bowdle for two years and
then moved to a farm a mile south of Bowdle. In 1940 Reinhold began working
for Fred Dollinger and held this job two years.

        Erna, Bruce, Darlene, Reinhold Huber

Like most newlyweds Reinhold and Erna found there were a lot of things they
could not have and their Sunday diversion was to walk two miles to spend
the day with her parents, carrying their little daughter all the way. A
good crop helped them buy a two-door Ford the next year. In 1941 they bought
the Jacob Hoffman farm and lived there until 1949 when they sold to Matt
Huft as Reinhold could no longer take the hard work. With the help of his
father and Erna's father they built their home on east Main Street in
Bowdle. Reinhold worked for Al Engelhard's trucking firm.

Then Reinhold and Erna went into the combining business, pursuing this for
21 years, harvesting crops from Texas to the Canadian line. Erna states it
was very hard work in hot weather and sometimes a problem to keep the men
of the crew happy when it rained. One year Reinhold and two men were held
up in Oxford, KS six weeks due to the continual rains. They operated from
two to four combines.

During the last years Reinhold and his son Bruce farmed together. Bruce is
still in the business, but custom combines only for farmers in the state.

In 1954 Erna took advantage of a Nurse's Aide Course offered at the Bowdle
Hospital by Director of Nurses Tena Stevens and Mrs. McMann. Since that
time Erna has spent over 30 years working as an aide at the hospital.

They had two children. Darlene was born Aug. 24, 1936. She married Henry
Raszler and is Director of Nurses in Phoenix, AZ. They have two children
Scott and Dana. Bruce Huber married Dolorita Thomas. He was born Aug. 13,
1938. They have three children: Shonda (Rau,) Carla (Knecht) and Marc Bruce.

Reinhold died Dec. 26, 1984 due to what is known as Farmers Lungs, caused
by combine dust.

RICHARD F. and ROSINA [SCHLAHT] HUBER

Richard F. Huber (1890-1969) and Rosina Schlaht Huber (1890-1981) spent
most of their married life on the farm five miles east and two miles north
of Bowdle. They were married in 1916 and spent one year on land they
homesteaded near Trail City, west of the Missouri River. They had one son
Oscar. When World War I started in 1917 they moved back to the farm near
Bowdle.

        Richard and Rosina Huber

Rosina Schlaht was the daughter of John Schlaht and Barbara Eisenbeisz
Schlaht. She was living in Hosmer at the time of their marriage. She moved
to a farm near Hosmer with her parents in 1896.

Richard F. Huber was the son of Jacob Huber and Sabina Walz Huber and moved
from Freeman to the homestead with his parents in 1896. He was active in
township government and served on the ASC Board.

Their early farming was mostly seeding wheat and oats and milking a few
cows. In the 1920's a Case tractor and horses were used with the field
work. Later a 1530 Farmall with steel lugs was used. In 1927 a new
McCormick Deering combine with a 12-foot platform was purchased for $1500.
This made harvesting much easier. It was the first in Edmunds County and
many people came to see it work. The windrowing was done with horses pulling
the header.

A new Model A John Deere with rubber tires was purchased for $1,165 in
1941. In 1947 a new 30 Cockshutt tractor with a price tag of $1,742 became
a part of the farm operation. In 1948 a 1-1/2 ton Reo truck was purchased
for $3,903 which included a 16-foot box. In 1952 a new Massey Harris
four-plow diesel tractor was added for $2,925. From there on equipment
prices went up faster than prices for farm produce.

There was no plumbing in the house until 1926 when a gravity flow water
line was installed. The pipes also went to the hog barn and to the cattle
barn from a 3,000 gallon reservoir. In 1934 a sewer system was added and a
water pressure pump was installed in the house. In 1950 REA electricity came
to the farm and the 32-volt battery system became obsolete.

With adequate electrical power came deep freezers, refrigerators, electric
motors, electric stoves and a modern home.

ROBERT and MARILYN [MITTLEIDER] HUBER

Robert Lee Huber was born Dec. 14, 1941 to Albert and Alice (Eisenbeisz)
Huber. He was delivered by his Grandma Eisenbeisz with the help of his
father. His boyhood was spent on the farm and in Oregon where his father

        Back: Chad, Shawn, Shayne, Courtney Front: Bob and Marilyn Huber

Bob worked with his uncle Reinhold Huber as a custom combiner, as a

Bob married Marilyn J. Mittleider Oct. 4, 1968 at Trinity Lutheran Church
in Mobridge. Marilyn was born June 23, 1948 in Mobridge to Fred and Viola
Mittleider. She attended Freeman Davis School and graduated from Mobridge
High School in 1966. She studied at the National School of Business in

The couple's children are Chad Robert, born Sept. 1, 1969; Shawn Marie, May
17, 1971; Shayne Michael Feb. 1, 1973 and Courtney Lee, born Aug. 9, 1974.

JACOB and JOHANNA [WALD] HUFT

Jacob was born in South Russia May 8, 1890. Johanna was born in Russia May

moved with their family to a farm five miles north of Bowdle. A sod house

        Jacob Huft Family Back: Mary, Johanna, Jacob, Jake, Adam Front:
        Helen, Henry, Josephine, David, Philip, Tillie

JACOB M. and EDNA [SANDMEIER] HUFT

MATT and GRETCHEN [LEMKE] HUFT

Matt was born in 1910 near Bergdorf, Russia. At the age of three he came to

their home north of Bowdle.

Matt was orphaned by the death of his father in 1925. To survive he worked

        Matt and Gretchen. Darrel and Carolee Huft
