ALBERT and BERTHA [BUECHLER] LEIDHOLT

Albert Alvin Leidholt was born March 5, 1913 at Roscoe. His parents were
Jacob and Margaret (Pietzke) Leidholt. Albert married Bertha Magdalena
Buechler Sept. 20, 1936 at the American Lutheran Church in Bowdle. She was
the daughter of John J. and Magdalena (Bossert) Buechler. John was born
Jan. 18, 1890 in Russia and Magdalena was born Feb. 27, 1892 at Artas.

Bertha was born on a farm west of Bowdle which her father had bought from
his father John Buechler Sr. She loves to tell that her Grandmother
Buechler says her father was born in Russia and came with his parents to
the United States. He was the best baby on the boat. He only cried once and
that was when they started over and he quit when they landed in America.

John J. and Magdalena had two daughters Bertha Leidholt and Edna Aldinger.
Edna now lives in Aberdeen. She tells of having to help in the fields and
also at home and says she was usually picked to help in the field. When
they had finished the evening chores and were too hot and tired, they used
to play cricket and sing. Edna and Bertha sang for many school programs.
One special song was "Putting on the Style."

The girls went to country school on the Yellowstone Trail, where there were
up to 30 children in a one-room school with all eight grades to teach. Edna
says she usually enjoyed the opening exercises when the teacher would read
a chapter from a storybook. "Pollyanna" was her favorite. They also went to
religious summer school at the old Neuglueckstahl Church, walking part way
and then catching a ride with the teacher Rev. Hanselman. "We were taught
to read and write German," and Bertha adds, "I really have to thank my
parents for that education. It has helped a lot to read and translate the
German."

Many interesting things happened in their young lives. "We had tough years
and then were blessed with a daughter Geraldine Jean Sept. 17, 1937. Our
son Harvey Albert was born Jan. 8, 1941. We bought the Hoffman farm where
we are living and when my parents decided to move to Bowdle, we were asked
to move to their farm. Jeanne Ann was born Feb. 2, 1944," Bertha relates.

Albert bought a threshing machine and threshed for 12 farmers in the area.
This was work for the men, but the women found they also had work in the
hot kitchen--as the saying goes Do Kommen Die Freasser (here comes the
eaters.) Then came the combines, which were a blessing, no more shocking
the grain and threshing. Albert also sheared sheep for hire which helped
buy the first regular Farmall tractor with steel wheels. They enjoyed every
bit of their farming, despite bad times such as the dry years when nothing
grew, the grasshopper and Morman cricket invasions when the crops were eaten
almost overnight and just they just kept telling each other, "maybe next
year will be better.

        Albert Leidholt Family Bertha, Harvey, Joanne in front, Geraldine,
        Albert

Albert and Bertha enjoyed many vacation trips with their family and later
without them. Geraldine Jean married Leonard Winchester and their children
are Brenda Kay Winchester and Debbra Ann, wife of John Davis.

Harvey Albert married Susan Giedt. Their children are Thomas Harvey,
Douglas James and Michael John.

Joanne Ann married Terry Nehlich. Their children are Gregory Chad, Gary Lee
and Kara Ann. Joanne and son Gary Lee have died.

Albert and Bertha moved a mobile home to Bowdle in September 1980 and are
living there now.

HARVEY and SUSAN [GIEDT] LEIDHOLT

Harvey Leidholt was born Jan. 8, 1941 at Bowdle Hospital, the son of Albert
A. and Bertha Buechler Leidholt. Harvey has an older sister Geraldine and a
younger sister Joanne. The family lived on a farm 4-1/2 miles west and 1/2
mile south of Bowdle. Harvey attended Spring Lake District School #21 and
graduated from Bowdle High School, Class of 1959.

His first job was driving gravel truck for Bradbury Construction for the
resurfacing of U.S. Highway 12. At the intersection of Highways 83 and 12,
a car turned in front of Harvey's truck and stopped. He had 13 tons of
gravel on and an instant decision was vital. He decided to take the ditch
to miss hitting the car. The gravel truck was totaled, but Harvey was lucky
to come through with only a broken nose, broken eye glasses and minor cuts
and bruises. He then decided to go into farming with his folks. In 1966 he
purchased some land from his grandparents Mr. and Mrs. John J. Buechler.

In 1968 Harvey married Susan Giedt of Glendale, CA. Her father Ted Giedt
was a Bowdle native. Susan was born Oct. 22, 1948 in Los Angeles. Her
mother was Dorothy Derham Giedt. Susan graduated from Herbert Hoover High
School in 1966 and attended Glendale Junior College. Harvey and Susan made
their first home in Rapid City where he was employed by Barton Masonry.
That following spring they returned to Bowdle where Harvey farmed, worked
for Walz Body Shop and was also a bus driver for Bowdle School District.

They are the parents of three sons. Thomas was born April 18, 1970:
Douglas, June 18, 1972 and Michael, July 22, 1981.

In June 1975 Harvey and Susan bought his parents farm and became the fourth
generation on that land. Harvey's mother was born there, his grandfather
Buechler had farmed the land and his great-grandfather homesteaded it
during the days of the early settlers.

        Back: Tom and Douglas Front: Michael. Susan. Harvey Leidholt

The year 1975 brought sorrow to the family when Harvey's younger sister
Joanne died of cancer. Harvey continued to farm and work part-time in
Bowdle. In 1976 he worked for Everet Lemke at Bowdle Meat Market and he
continued to work for Bob Huber when he purchased the business.

A special day for the family was May 1, 1981 when they moved into their new
home just in time for the arrival of their third son Michael, who was born
in July.

April 1, 1982 Harvey and Susan came home to find their 90-year-old barn on
fire. With the help of neighbors, Harvey managed to get the cattle and
sheep out before the barn was engulfed in flames. They rebuilt a new barn
that fall and before it was finished, Thanksgiving Day 1982 they returned
home in the evening from a family gathering in Aberdeen to find their new
home on fire. They fought the fire all night. The building was a total
loss. The fire was caused by a faulty chimney.

The family rented a trailer house to use on the farm and rebuilt, moving in
May 15, 1983 -- this time without a woodburner stove and chimney. Harvey is
still farming and has a cow-calf operation and continues to hold the job
begun 18 years ago as bus driver and assistant at the meat market.

HENRY and LYDIA [SCHLEPP] LEIDHOLT

Henry Leidholt was one of five sons born to Philip and Marie Leidholt in
Grimm, Russia. He was born Jan. 4, 1882. In 1899 Henry was 17 and his
parents brought the family to the United States, making their first home on
a homestead near Roscoe. Henry helped his parents with farming and learned
the English language.

In 1911 Henry married Anna Herrwald, daughter of William and Wilhelmena
Herrwald of Bowdle. Henry and Anna lived on a farm near Lowry and they had
two children: Bernice and Ted. Anna died April 20, 1919.

In 1921 Henry married Lydia Schlepp, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Jacob
Schlepp. Eight children were born to them while living on the Gust Bieber
farm. In 1929 Henry bought a farm four miles west of Bowdle where they
lived 17 years. He was fond of horses and farmed with them until tractors
were commonly used.

        Henry and Anna          Lydia and Henry
        Leidholt                Leidholt

        Back: Mable, Rueben, Shirley, Bert, Jerry Front: Janice, Vivian,
        Bernice, Ted

Henry was active in community affairs and served on the rural school board,
was a member of the Equity Exchange and active in the Lutheran church. Ill
health forced him to give up farming in 1946 and he retired to live in
Bowdle. Lydia kept busy with rearing the family and making a home for them.
Henry died July 21, 1946. Lydia died July 18, 1952. Their surviving
children include: Bernice who married Norman Lindbloom and lives in Pierre.
Ted married Irma Buechler and lives in Bowdle. Vivian married Palmer
Schumacher and their home is in Bath. Rueben married Ruth Dirkson of
Bancroft and lives in Ft. Pierre. Jerry married Corrine Wiebe and lives in
Pierre. Lucille married Delbert Schaible and lives in Minneapolis, MN.
Berdell married Virginia Bachman and lives in Minot. Shirley married Bob
David of Commerce City, CO. Janice married Danny Bergeson and lives in Ft.
Pierre and Mabel married Paul Schumacher and lives in Pierre.

JACOB and MARGARET [PIETZKE] LEIDHOLT

Jacob Leidholt was born in Russia to Philip and Maria (Dubbs) Leidholt,
came to America Nov. 15, 1899, settled in Freeman and moved to Roscoe.

Jacob married Margaret Pietzke, daughter of Frederick Pietzke of Bowdle in
Cloyd Valley Township of Edmunds County Dec. 26, 1902 at the Lutheran
Church.

        Jacob and Margaret Leidholt

They were blessed with seven sons and five daughters. They retired in
Bowdle in 1939. Jacob moved a house from the Glenham area in which they
lived until he died July 1941 and Margaret died in November 1951. A son
Robert was killed in 1945 during World War II.

Jacob Leidholt fixed shoes while he lived in Bowdle and Margaret was a
housewife.

LARRY and GLORIA [PETERSON] LEIDHOLT

Larry, son of Ted and Irma Leidholt, was born in Aberdeen April 27, 1947.
He graduated from Bowdle High School and served in the Armed Forces
1966-1968, stationed in Washington and Colorado.

Larry was married June 5, 1970 to Gloria Peterson, daughter of Frank and
Christina Peterson. Gloria was born July 30, 1951 at Ipswich. She operated
a beauty shop before her marriage.

After their marriage Larry opened Leidholt Body & Repair Shop and in 1978
they purchased Schaible Chevrolet Garage. Gloria aided her husband by being
secretary of the company. In 1985 they sold the business then known as
Leidholt Chevrolet Inc. to David McCarlson and moved to Groton. Larry works
for Abeln Brothers and Gloria is secretary for Trail Chevrolet & Olds Co.

        James, Tabitha, Gloria, Larry Leidholt

They are parents of two children. James was born Dec. 13, 1972 and Tabitha
Aug. 24, 1975. Both are students in the Groton School System.

TED and IRMA [BUECHLER] LEIDHOLT

Ted Leidholt was born in Bowdle July 28, 1913 to Henry and Anna (Herrwald)
Leidholt. Ted's mother died in 1918 and his father raised him on a farm 18
miles southwest of Bowdle. Ted attended grade school and was confirmed. The
next home was on a farm four miles west of Bowdle when Ted attended Dr.
Martin Luther High School in New Ulm, MN and graduated from Bowdle High
School.

June 29, 1941 Ted was married to Irma Buechler, daughter of Fred B.
Buechler. Irma was born Oct. 15, 1918 near Bowdle in Walworth County. She
attended one through eight grades at Buechler School in Spring Lake
Township.

Three children were born to this couple. Carol was born April 10, 1944 and
married David Gurath of Fon du Lac, WI. They have four children: Paula,
Mark, Matthew and Michael. A daughter Brenda died in infancy in 1982. David
is assistant manager of Walgreen Drug in Fond Du Lac. Carol, a former
parochial school teacher, is a homemaker.

Larry, born April 27, 1947, is married to Gloria Peterson of Bowdle. They
have two children: James and Tabitha. Larry owned Leidholt Chevrolet Inc. in
Bowdle, but now lives in Groton.

Janell, born Feb. 3, 1963, lives in Little Rock, AR. After serving eight
years in the U.S. Air Force, she is now employed by the Internal Revenue
Service.

Ted and Irma farmed 26 years 2-1/2 miles southwest of Bowdle in Bowdle
Township. They experienced the trying droughts and dust storms of the era.
Ted served as a director of the Bowdle Farmers Union Oil Co. and of the
Equity Farmers Elevator. He also served on the Bowdle Township School Board
and Swan Creek Telephone Co. for many years. Irma held various offices as a
member in Extension Club, Mothers' Club, 4-H Club, Farmers Union Youth
Group, Ladies Aid and has instructed pre-school children in Sunday School
and Vacation Bible School. Her faithful service to the Lord and to the
children of the community is reflected in the 38 continuous years she has
taught Sunday School.

        Back: Janell, Larry, Carol Front: Ted and Irma Leidholt

In 1968 they built a home in Bowdle where they are retired. The participate
in Sportsmen's and Golf Clubs, as well as taking part in church activities.
Fishing in the Great Missouri River is a favorite pastime for the couple.
They enjoy traveling to visit their children and other relatives. Ted and
Irma recall with fondness the harvesting, haying, butchering and building
done cooperatively with neighbors. They feel long hours, hard work and
hardships are balanced by wonderful memories. They consider America to be
truly "The Land of Opportunity." They look with pleasure at the many
changes that have taken place in Bowdle during their lifetimes. In this
community they have lived in happiness.

CARL and ULRIKE [BRANDT] LEMKE

Carl Lemke was born in Milwaukee, WI Feb. 15, 1890. At age four he came
with his parents William L. & Hanna Lemke, his brother Richard and his
sisters to Bowdle. Carl's parents homesteaded a farm northwest of Bowdle.

After Carl's marriage to Ulrike Brandt in 1918, he bought his parents farm,
which is still remembered for the original barns and fences made of native
stone plastered with mud. Carl loved horses and they provided him a source
of power, as well as much pleasure throughout his lifetime.

In 1954 they retired to live in Bowdle. At that time their son Roy and his
wife Viola made the farm their home and their son Curtis farms the land
today.

        Carl, Ulrike, Wilma, Gretchen, Roy, Alfred Everet Lemke in front

The Carl Lemke children were Roy, Alfred, Owen (deceased), Everet, Gretchen
(Huft) Sprenger and Wilma of Washington, D.C.

Ulrike Lemke died in 1959 and Carl in 1960.

EVERET and ANGIE [BIEBER] LEMKE

Everet Lemke was born July 16, 1929 to Mr. and Mrs. Carl Lemke of Bowdle.
Everet married Angeline Bieber, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Jacob P. Bieber,
born Feb. 14, 1935 at Mobridge. Jacob P. Bieber was born in South Russia
Feb. 4, 1893 and died April 30, 1966. His wife was born at Roscoe Sept. 15,
1904 and resides in Bowdle. Angie and Everet were married Sept. 17, 1952 at
Bowdle and lived on her parents farm sharing the work as they raised
livestock and farmed the land. Two children were born to them.

        Back: Candice, Cynthia. Front: Angie, Everet Lemke

Candice was born April 28, 1954 and Cynthia arrived March 27, 1959. Mr. and
Mrs. Jacob P. Bieber retired to live in town in 1959 and Everet and Angie
took over the farmwork. Angie says there were many joys and troubles of
living through the years of farming, schooling for their daughters and
church activities.

In 1964 they bought Wm. Schilling's garage, remodeled it and established a
recreation center. They sold it to Robert Stappler in 1965 and bought
Waltman Meat Market, changing the name to Bowdle Meat Market. After 10
years they sold it to Robert Huber in 1978.

Candice Lemke married Ron Williamson of Atoka, OK Nov. 1, 1974. They have
two children. Jennifer was born Nov. 24, 1976 and Anthony June 13, 1978.
They live in Edmond, OK.

Cynthia Lemke married George (Chips) Lowens of Jacksonville, FL Sept. 19,
1981. They make their home in Pueblo, CO.

Everet and Angie say the years have been busy ones and at times the
sledding was rough, but "we made it through." Angie does aide work at Bowdle
Hospital besides raising a big vegetable and flower garden and responding
to the needs of their church.

RICHARD and ELLA [CHRISTIANSON] LEMKE

Richard and Ella Christianson Lemke came with their families to live in the
Bowdle area before 1900. Each helped their family build a home and develop
a farm in the new land before they married. They met at choir practice at
the Lutheran Church and were married in 1910. That year Richard started a
new farm site by building a five-room house and a barn northeast of Bowdle.
Their children were Katherine, who married Arthur Hoffmann and Erma, who
became the wife of Melvin Maier. Another daughter Ella died as a young
school girl.

        Richard and Ella Lemke

Richard and Ella Lemke were active in farming until the fall 1943 when they
died. Their farm was mostly self-sufficient in furnishing the family food
except for salt, sugar and coffee. One important aspect of their operation
was a vegetable and fruit garden. Even during the Dirty Thirties it produced
due to a pipe system from the windmill well to the garden which permitted
unlimited irrigation whenever the wind blew. An old buttermilk tank held
water in reserve for the few times there was no wind. There were apple and
plum trees, strawberries and raspberries and all the vegetables to be
canned for use in the winter. One oak, an elm, some apple and shade trees
still beautify the farmstead.

Hogs, chickens, geese, turkeys, ducks, milk, cows, range cattle and sheep
supplied the meat and dairy products year round. Pork, beef and chicken
were canned and the holiday birds were homegrown. Butter was churned and
cheese pressed. Surplus animals were sold to pay the taxes, repairs and
improve the farm. Such buildings as a chicken house, garage, granary, corn
crib and hog barn improved the farm.

About 200 acres of cultivated land was carefully tended with regular
applications of barnyard manure. Corn, oats, wheat and alfalfa were rotated
to build a fertile soil. Besides furnishing cash for new machinery and a
new Oldsmobile in 1926, the crops helped finance school and college for the
two daughters.

Horses were the only farm power used by Richard Lemke. He thought tractors
did not add fertility to the soil and they also contributed to abuse and
misuse of the land.

Richard and Ella were active in community affairs. They helped organize a
rural telephone company and farmers organizations. Richard was one of the
best baseball players and promoters in the early 1900's. He was catcher and
manager and a well-known umpire for 50 years. He served on the school
board, was a county commissioner as well as a leader in township affairs.

Richard and Ella Lemke helped build the first St. John's Evangelical
Lutheran Church in Bowdle. They are buried in plots allotted them as early
organizers.

ROY and VIOLA [HAUPT] LEMKE

Roy Lemke was born Dec. 20, 1922 at Bowdle. His father Carl was born Feb.
15, 1890 in Wisconsin and died July 8, 1960 and his mother Ulrike (Brandt)
Lemke was born July 23, 1896 at Bowdle and died Sept. 17, 1959.

        Viola and Roy Lemke

Roy Lemke attended rural school in Bowdle Township. As a member of the U.S.
Army he served in Germany as a paratrooper during World War II. He returned
to his farm after his tour of duty and married Viola Haupt June 16, 1946.
Viola was the daughter of Carl and Mathilda (Bollinger) Haupt.

Roy and Viola conducted their farming career on the Lemke family farm two
miles northwest of Bowdle. Their two children are Arvis and Curtis.

Arvis was born July 14, 1949. She married Roger Jacobs March 31, 1968. They
live in Bowdle where Roger works for Beadle Ford Inc. Their children are
Michelle and Shane.

Curtis Lemke was born May 26, 1954. He was formerly married to Luane Oster
and they had a daughter Amber Marie. Curtis operates a custom combining
service and farms.

WILHELM and HANNA [FROEMMING] LEMKE

Wilhelm Lemke (1845-1925) and his wife Hanna Froemming Lemke (1853-1928)
were born in Pomerania in North Germany. In 1894 they, along with their
three older children, immigrated to the United States and joined other
relatives in Milwaukee.

That same year Wilhelm and Hanna Lemke brought their family, livestock and
personal goods to Bowdle. They had heard of the fine land and opportunity
around Bowdle from a niece who was living here. A long fence marked the
entrance and driveway to the house on the farm two miles northwest of
Bowdle. This fence was built by hand of native stone. Portions of it remain
standing. The barns were long structures fashioned of rock plastered with
mud. These stone buildings were unique in this area. They did support
shingled roofs.

        Hanna and Wilhelm Lemke

The Lemke family suffered its share of hardships. By 1900 they had survived
the death of their oldest daughter and their frame house had burned. They
built a similar two-story home at the same location. Their neighbors were
Valentine Ketterling, William Haupt, John Brandt and George Nickisch.

Dairying, raising all kinds of poultry, small grain, potatoes, gardening,
as well as building and repairing the stone fences kept the family busy.
Feeding the livestock, spinning, knitting, reading and worship were routine
activities for the family. Horses were the main power source for work and
travel.

The large garden had a drainage ditch near which many trees, clover,
chamomile, iris and asparagus grew. The garden contained beets for the
livestock, vegetables and potatoes for table use. Roses and wood violets
lined a sandy path that led to the hand pump downhill from the house.
Grandchildren enjoyed this fairyland when visiting for weddings, Easter egg
hunts and other events.

Wilhelm and son Richard helped build the first St. John's Lutheran Church
in Bowdle. The building had a bell tower and Gothic windows. Women sat on
the left side of its center aisle and the men were seated on the right.
Children sat in the front rows on the appropriate side. A big, jacketed,
black stove warmed the lofty building.

Wilhelm and Hanna spent their last 10 years in Bowdle. Their eight
children: Bertha, Richard, Elizabeth Doheer, Clara and Hanna Schlomer, Carl
Helen O'Brien and Frieda Rieger have all died. Car lived on the farm and
later his son Roy lived there. The farm is now owned by Roy's son Curtis
Lemke.

HELMER and ALMA [SCHUMACHER] LENO

Helmer, fourth son of John Sr. and Leontina (Fuchs) Leno, was born Jan. 19,
1916 in Broadus, MT. His parents had homesteaded there and built a flour
mill. In 1923 the family moved to Timvick, ND. In 1931 the family purchased
the flour mill in Bowdle from Gross Land and Loan Co. Because Helmer began
working for his father at age 15, he was unable to finish his high school
education. With a Reo truck he delivered flour orders to the northcentral
area of South Dakota and southern part of North Dakota

        Helmer and Alma Leno

Helmer married Alma Schumacher May 29, 1938. She was the daughter of
Christian and Mathilda (Thurn) Schumacher and resided in Bowdle. Helmer and
his brother Reinhold operated the flour mill until 1943. During this time
daughters Janice Rae Peach (1939) and Sandra Lee Schade (1940) were born.

During World War II the mill operated 24 hours a day, 7 days a week,
exporting the flour to world markets. Peak production occurred in 1946 with
9,000,000 pounds of flour exported to South America and Europe. Flour was
also delivered to many North and South Dakota institutions.

In 1943 the Helmer Leno family moved to Spokane, WA. Helmer was employed in
the Hanford Works U.S. Atomic Energy Commission Reservation. Their third
daughter Jacquelyn Connie Axness was born Dec. 15, 1945 in Spokane. In 1946
the family returned to Bowdle and Helmer rejoined his brother Reinie in the
flour mill operation. In 1949 Helmer purchased Reinie's interest in the
mill. In 1968 a decline in production and increase in competition from
large corporations were factors in Helmer's decision to convert the flour
mill to a feed mill.

Helmer's community activities included the Sportsmen's Club, volunteer
fireman, mayor of Bowdle, school board member and an ongoing interest in
the community of Bowdle. Helmer died March 18, 1971.

In 1950 Alma returned to her profession and operated a beauty shop in her
home until 1969, subsequently selling the business to a former employee.
During this time Alma was very active in the community including school
functions that involved her daughters, St. Paul Lutheran Church, clubs and
other community events. In 1963 Alma was selected "Woman of the Year" for
Bowdle by the Jaycees and Jaycettes.

In 1972 Alma became a county outreach worker for Northeast Community Action
Program. This was a state program sponsored by the Office on Aging. The
program promoted a better quality of living for the elderly. Alma comments
that it was a great experience and enabled her to meet many new friends in
the county. The program was discontinued in 1980.

Alma recalls many childhood memories growing up on the farm. One memory
relates to entertainment involving six area farm families. The females of
these families would picnic and play games at a grove of trees near their
properties. Alma also had a trapeze located on their front porch. Hilda
Jarvis, a neighbor friend, Vernada and Alma would perform for others,
charging two cents for admission. In addition to the entertainment the
audience was treated to snacks and lemonade.

Presently Alma enjoys traveling, crafts, quilting and especially her
family. She now has five grandchildren. Alma continues her volunteer work
with senior citizens, helping whenever she is called.

EDWIN G.L. and IRENE [BIPES] LICKFELT

Edwin G.L. Lickfelt, son of Frederick and Martha (Schuft) Lickfelt, was
born Feb. 8, 1907 at Brownton, MN. As a young boy he moved with his parents
to South Dakota and settled in Bowdle. He attended grammar school eight
years and then went to work to help his mother raise his brothers and
sisters.

He married Irene Elizabeth Bipes Aug. 26, 1931 at Brownton, MN. She was
born March 12, 1913 to Mr. and Mrs. Simon Bipes of Brownton.

        Stanley, Donna, Eloise, Marilyn, Edwin Lickfelt

Edwin and Irene moved to the Red River Valley of North Dakota where he was
employed on a farm for $15 a month. They returned in 1932 and Edwin farmed
for John Gross in the summer and worked for WPA in the winter.

Four children were born: Donna Marie April 23, 1933; Eloise Mathilda Sept.
25, 1935; Marilyn Jean June 3, 1938 and Stanley Roy Aug. 3, 1939.

In March 1942 Edwin began work for the railroad as a member of a section
gang crew. Irene died May 5, 1942. Edwin and his four young children made
their home with his mother Martha until 1951. Edwin continued working for
the railroad and was eventually moved to Bowdle where he could spend more
time with his family. He also worked in the creamery on weekends a few
years. He remained in the Bowdle area to work for a year 1952-1953, but
returned to railroad work in Aberdeen.

In June 1953 he moved his family to Aberdeen where Eloise entered nurse's
training at Presentation School of Nursing. Donna was married to Bill Bohn
and Marilyn and Stanley attended high school.

Edwin retired from the railroad Nov. 11, 1971. He makes his home with his
daughter Marilyn in Aberdeen. Donna lives in Aberdeen with her husband
William 0. Bohn and their children David, Rosemary Ann, Louise, William and
Jay.

Stanley Lickfelt married Mercedes Rockstad in 1964. They live in Puyallup,
WA and have two children Kevin and Karen.

Eloise married Arthur Eisenbeisz Jr. They live on a farm north of Bowdle.
Eloise is employed part-time at Bowdle Hospital. Their children are Randall,
Edwin, Derek, Stephanie and Andrea.

FRED and MARTHA [SCHUFT] LICKFELT

Fred Lickfelt was born Oct. 15, 1879 in Minnesota. He married Martha Schuft
in Penn County, MN Sept. 21, 1906. Five sons were born: Edwin Feb. 8, 1907;
Elmer May 30, 1910; Maynard March 8, 1913; Clarence (Lefty) Sept. 17, 1914
and Marvin March 13, 1916.

        Fred and Martha Lickfelt

In 1917 Fred and Martha moved their family to South Dakota. Fred was owner
of the Bowdle Elevator until 1923 when he sold it to John Geib. He then was
a farm laborer until his death. Two daughters and a son were born in South
Dakota: Mabel May 25, 1921; Leonard (Litch) Nov. 25, 1922 and Verna July
10, 1925.

Martha supported her family after Fred died. She cleaned houses, cooked at
the school and worked at the hotel to keep her family together.

In 1942 Edwin's wife died and Martha opened her home to her four
grandchildren. Mabel died in 1943 and Martha also reared her infant son
until Martha's death in May 1951.

ANNA E. [WIEPKING, STOLZ] LONG

Anna E. Wiepking was born Sept. 2, 1908 in Cloyd Valley Township to Albert
and Mary Wiepking Sr. Anna attended Cloyd Valley District School until the
fifth grade when she had to stay home and help in the fields, as she was
the oldest of the children. When she was 13 she spent the summer in Bowdle
living with her grandmother Louise Wiepking while she attended confirmation
classes.

She recalls times of a severe drought and duststorms in the land when
livestock died and grasshoppers and blister beetles ate everything. Then
there were times of good crop yields. Her father bought seed grain for 10
cents a bushel and when the threshers charged 10 cents a bushel for their
work there was no money to pay for the seed wheat. Though the corn crop was
good that year, it had no price and what had been taken to town was brought
back and burned instead of coal, which they had no means to buy. They
managed to survive, living off the land.

Her mother clothed the family with homespun wool she knitted into stockings
and mittens, a precious gift from her hands. This was followed by five more
years of dry weather and Anna went to work in Bowdle for Mrs. Carlson at
the cafe. She received $1.50 a week for the work.

After a few months she went to Minnesota where she did housework for the
Johnson family. Eighteen months later she was invited to accompany the
Smith family to Oregon where she got a job with Mrs. Cigret. She cleaned
the 14-room house and cooked for all the company Mrs. Cigret invited and
received $28 a month.

In 1936 an invitation from her cousins Bill and Dorothy Funk took Anna to
California. There she met Peter Stolz who had recently come from Minnesota.
He had gotten a job at Lachs Dairy through Bill Funk and thus he also met
Anna. Peter Stolz was born Oct. 5, 1904 in Germany to Peter and Kathern
Stolz. His father died in 1951 and his mother in 1953.

Peter Stolz and Anna Wiepking were married in 1938 and made their first
home in Lockford, CA. Her sister Esther joined them a year later and made
her home with them. This caused a crisis in the family when Esther needed a
blue skirt to attend high school in Lodi. She had only one more year to
finish. They had only $5 left to eat on that week, but Anna took Esther to
Lodi where they got not only the skirt, but also shoes she needed. They
survived the coming week. The girls worked hard at the cannery and in the
walnut groves and sorting sheds the following summer to give Esther a
chance to go to business college. On completion of the course Esther had a
job with P.G. & E. until she joined the U.S Marines during World War II.
Her younger sister Lillian had joined the group a year earlier and also
lived with Peter and Anna.

During the war Peter Stolz went to work for Steven Brothers in the
shipyards. Their first daughter Maryann was born in 1943. She is now living
in Orangevale, CA and is the mother of three daughters Karen, Kimberly and
Lisa.

Peter and Anna spent 1945-1946 in South Dakota to be with her brother
Albert as he needed help. They built a house and in 1947 their second
daughter Elaine was born at Hoven. Elaine now lives in Auburn, CA and her
husband works for the railroad. Their children are Linda, who is employed
as a loan processor for Savings and Loan in Sacramento, CA; Kenneth who
works in retail sales and Diana who works in a clothing store.

Peter Stolz became allergic to the many pollens and farm dust,
necessitating their return to Stockton, where he worked as a boiler man,
supervisor of nine other men. He held this job until his death in 1960.

After she became widowed, Anna worked as a technician at the State Hospital
10 years and in 1965 married Andrew Long. They made their home in Auburn
and Andrew retired in 1976. Interests and pleasures for them in their
retirement are the garden, handiwork, VFW Club and Garden Club, and the
company of friends and their family.

LEONARD and ESTHER [WIEPKING] LUCY

Esther, youngest daughter of Albert and Mary Wiepking, was born on the farm
southeast of Bowdle Oct. 1, 1920. She attended Cloyd Valley country school
and Bowdle School before going to California where she graduated from Lodi
High School.

        Esther and Leonard Lucy

She worked for Pacific Gas & Electric Company in San Francisco until she
joined the U.S. Marine Corps in 1942 and was stationed in Washington, D.C.
She was discharged in 1945 with a rank of master sergeant.

Esther Wiepking married Leonard Lucy Sept. 6, 1948. She is the mother of
two children. Allen, age 32, works for the City of San Francisco Water
Department and Cheryl, age 30, works as a dental technician.

MELVIN and ERMA [LEMKE] MAIER

Melvin Delbert Maier was born to Jacob A. and Margarita (Will) Maier at
Bowdle Feb. 17, 1913. Jacob worked for Mr. Dancer on the dray line and
Maggie, as she was fondly called, worked at the Dumont Hotel. The family
lived on several farms in the Hosmer area after they left Bowdle.

During the 1920's Jacob purchased the land where the old Eldridge place was
located. It was here that Melvin and his two sisters grew to adulthood. One
sister Lillian married George Mulder, both deceased and Lenora is now Mrs.
Benjamin Mulder. A grandson Milbert Maier made his home with them.

As a young man Melvin inherited a Model "T" coupe from his Grandfather
Will. With such a vehicle it was time to seriously consider marriage.
Melvin courted the second daughter of Richard E.T. (Oct. 27, 1879 to Oct.
13, 1943) and Ella Anna (Christianson) Lemke (Nov. 30, 1884 to Nov. 3,
1943.)

Richard's family included three daughters: Katherine Marie, Erma Herretta
and Ella Leona, who died June 13, 1922 at age seven. The Lemke family lived
1-1/2 miles northeast of Bowdle where Richard had purchased land and built
a house for his bride. Richard and Ella lived their entire married life on
this farm. Erma's father was very much interested in caring for and working
with horses on his land. He was active in affairs of the community and was
especially concerned with the welfare of the local school system. He served
many years on the school board. Katherine and Erma attended town school,
walking when the weather was nice. When the weather was unfavorable Rich
would hitch up his fast team (Spot and Babe) and cover the distance very
quickly.

A family anecdote that still brings chuckles, concerns father Richard's
leaving his family visiting his parents, Wilhelm and Hanna Lemke in Bowdle,
returning home alone and unhitching and bedding down his team for the
night. Missing them when he entered the house, it was necessary for him to
harness and hook up his team and return to town for his family. This was a
favorite story of Ella's for many years.

Erma recalls teachers Theodore and Nathaniel Nickisch and Superintendent
Lloyd Lane from her earlier years as a student. She graduated from Bowdle
High School in 1932 and attended Northern where she earned a first grade
certificate in 1933. Her first teaching experience was at the N.E.
(Sunshine) School in Bowdle Township. This 19-year-old teacher instructed
21 students. Her teaching career spans a period of more than 40 years. Erma
served as instructor in the S.E. (Blondo) School and the N.W. (Lemke-Haupt)
School. These were all located in Bowdle Township.

Erma taught in rural schools in Glover, Madison, Lake and Bryant Townships
in Edmunds County; Glenn and Horseshoe Lake, Spring Lake and Hilde
Districts in Walworth County and in the cities of Bowdle, Hosmer, Roscoe
and Eagle Butte. She served as a parochial school instructor in Bowdle;
Manitowoc, WI; Watertown and Lemmon. Through the years she continued to
upgrade her educational status. She acquired a State General Certificate
through examination in 1949, a bachelor's degree in education from Northern
in 1969 and finally a master's degree in education from Northern in 1981.
Since that time she has worked in her special interest area of special
education at Tolstoy, Lebanon and Hoven in Potter County. She continues to
be very active in the field of education. She spends several weeks each
year as a substitute teacher and works as a volunteer in the general area.

Melvin and Erma were married June 6, 1943 at St. John's Evangelical
Lutheran Church by Rev. P.G. Albrecht. They were surprised to learn Helena
Lemke Kuehl O'Brien was a godparent for each of them.

Melvin was a farmer all his life. At the death of Erma's parents they
purchased the Lemke family farm. Now tractors replaced Richard's beloved
horses. Melvin also worked in an elevator in Eagle Butte and at the Bowdle
Coop for 12 years. In 1978 Melvin and Erma moved into the Schaible Building.
In late August 1981 they moved to their new home on 1st Avenue in Bowdle.
Their split level dwelling rests on a wooden foundation. The entire family
was involved in the finishing and landscaping. Erma's crafts and handiwork
are housed and displayed on the lower level. A garage and breezeway were
added in 1985. Melvin died Sept. 17, 1982 and is buried in Redeemer
Lutheran Cemetery north of Bowdle.

        Back: Rae Ann, Melvin, Erma Sherma holding Sue and Richard holding
        Russ

Richard Melvin was born to Erma and Melvin in 1945 at Mobridge. More
information about him and his family can be found elsewhere in this book.
Rae Ann Lee was born in 1953 at Mobridge. She completed her elementary
education at Eagle Butte and graduated from Immanuel Lutheran High School
in Eau Claire, WI in 1970. She married Vincent Roy Smith at Bowdle in 1972.
Jeremiah Keven was born in 1975. Rae Ann and Vinni are divorced. Vinni is
managing engineer for Friday Packing Company at Markesan, WI. He makes his
home in Ripon, WI. Rae Ann attended a technical school in Fond du Lac and
now holds a position in research and development with Specialists Inc. at
Beaver Dam. She and Jeremiah reside at Ripon. Jeremiah has been spending
his summers in South Dakota with Grandma Erma and Uncle Rich and family.

RICHARD and SHERMA [WALTH] MAIER

Richard was born to Melvin and Erma Maier April 26, 1945 at Mobridge. He
attended grade school in Roscoe and Bowdle, Northwestern Lutheran Academy
at Mobridge two years and graduated from Eagle Butte High School in 1963.
He attended two years at SDSU in Brookings.

Richard married Sherma Walth at Redeemer Lutheran Church in Bowdle June 16,
1966. They made their home on the Lemke family farm. A son Russell Wade was
born Jan. 30, 1969 at Mobridge and a daughter Sue Ann was born at Bowdle
March 30, 1971. Both attend Bowdle School.

Richard and Sherma purchased the family farm in 1982. They are doing
extensive remodeling on the house. Richard and son Russell do custom work
for area farmers.

Richard and Sherma bought Buechler's Cafe and renamed it Sam's Cafe.
Extensive remodeling was done before opening in the spring of 1984. They are
still working on the project. It has become a family enterprise with Sue
Ann helping as a waitress. Besides managing the cafe Sherma also works as an
aide at Bowdle Hospital.

REV. PAUL H. and MEG [SPAUDE] MARGGRAF

Pastor and Mrs. Paul H. Marggraf came to Bowdle in July 1984. Pastor
Marggraf is pastor at St. John's Ev. Lutheran Church (Wisconsin Synod.) He
was born June 26, 1958 at Inglewood, CA to Mr. and Mrs. Bruce J. Marggraf.
He attended high school at Northwestern Preparatory School in Watertown,
WI. He graduated from Northwestern College, also in Watertown in 1980 and
graduated from Wisconsin Lutheran Seminary of Mequon, WI in 1984.

        Pastor and Mrs. Paul Marggraf, Sara and Matthew

Marggraf was wed to Meg Spaude June 13, 1982. She was born July 16, 1958 at
Aberdeen to Rev. and Mrs. C.W. Spaude. Meg attended high school at
Northwestern Preparatory School in Watertown, WI. She graduated from Dr.
Martin Luther College of New Ulm, MN in 1980 and taught two years at a
Lutheran parochial school in Milwaukee, WI. The couple has two children.
Sara was born Jan. 16, 1984 and Matthew May 26, 1985.

PHILIP and FREDERICKA [WOLF] MARTZ

Philip Martz was born Dec. 31, 1881 in Glueckstahl, Russia, son of Jacob
and Katherina (Unhrue) Martz. He came to America when he was three years
old with his parents, five brothers and one sister in 1884. Two brothers
and two sisters were born in the United States.

He married Fredericka Wolf Oct. 15, 1904 in Java. She was born July 4, 1884
in Marienberg, Russia to Mathew and Magdalena Wolf. She came to America
when she was six years old with her parents, one sister and one brother.
Four brothers and four sisters were born in the United States.

        Fredia and Philip Martz

After their marriage they lived on a farm southwest of Bowdle near the
Kitzler farm. In 1910 they moved to Madison Township northeast of Tolstoy
and lived on various farms.

Mr. and Mrs. Martz were members of St. John's Evangelical Lutheran Church
at Bowdle. Philip died Jan. 6, 1945 at the age of 64. Fredericka then
married J.B. Hoffman March 12, 1956. They lived in Bowdle. She died Feb.
27, 1974 at age 89.

Their children and descendants follow:

Emma married Egart Hoffman (deceased 1969) and had a son Marvin (deceased
1981) and a daughter MaeNerva (Mrs. Russel Bender.)

Sadie married Gust Bomesberger and they had two sons Merle and Curtiss.

Ellen married Wm. Bomesberger. Their children are Arliss (Mrs. Don
Jakober), Judith (Mrs. Ralph Rabenberg) and Russell.

ED J. and ROSIE [RITTLE] MASHEK

Ed was born Sept. 14, 1880 to Joseph and Mary Mashek in Spillville, IA. In
1901 he was employed with the Milwaukee Railroad as a brakeman. A few years
later Ed left the railroad and moved to Java where he worked in a butcher
shop. Then he moved to the town of Lowry where he homesteaded some land and
again returned to work on the railroad. Here he met and married Rosie
Rittle. Rosie was born in 1895 in Odessey, Russia and sailed to America,
settling with her parents in the Lowry area.

After a few years the family returned to Bowdle in 1916. Ed continued to
work for the railroad, being in charge of the pump station for 30 years. He
also worked part-time on the construction of St. Augustine's Catholic
Church.

Ed and Rosie were blessed with six children. They were Warren, Rosie,
Leonard (all deceased); George, Elmer and Mrs. Marcella Grosz.

Ed died July 23, 1948 and Rosie died in 1971.

GEORGE and MAGDALEN [BACHMAN] MASHEK

George was born to Edward and Rosie (Rittle) Mashek Jan. 21, 1915 at Lowry.
In 1916 he moved with his parents to Bowdle.

George attended the Bowdle Schools. Along with school George had an
interesting business. He operated a popcorn stand in front of the Gross
Bros. store. Saturday evenings many folks were seen eating George's
popcorn. Being a successful business venture, a small new fireproof building
was built between J.D. Schazenbach's store and the First State Bank. Here
George continued to sell the popular treat during the colder months.

George married Magdalen "Mac" Bachman May 2, 1939. Mac was born June 22,
1920 to Theo and Cecelia Bachman.

        Mac and George Mashek

George was employed at the cream, egg and poultry station. His next job was
working for A.J. Englehart as a grocery truck driver for three years. Then
he experienced working with meat cutting at the E. Merkel Meat Market. A
few years later George worked as a bartender at the Bowdle Liquor Store and
became manager for 10 years. In 1959 he began to work for the Postal
Service where he is employed at the present time. Besides belonging to
several organizations in Bowdle, George was a fireman for 49 years and 39
years of that service he served as secretary-treasurer.

Mac was employed as a secretary for Montana-Dakota Utilities Co. for 10
years. As a second job she often clerked at the Bowdle Livestock Sales
Barn. Her last employment was with Bowdle State Bank for 25 years. Mac was
director and head cashier at the bank several years and the last few years
she was the vice-president until her death Nov. 8, 1984.

They have one son Jerome who is employed with a newspaper at Decatur, IL.
He was married to Dianne Haux and has four children: Robin, Barbara,
Nicolas and Christina.

CAROL JEAN [HERMAN] MATHEWS

Carol Jean was born Oct. 13, 1943 to Reinie and Laura Herman. Carol
graduated from Bowdle High School and attended SDSU at Brookings where she
received her bachelor of science in nursing in 1965. In 1983 she received
her master's degree in Health Services administration at George Washington
University.

        Carol Mathews and son Timothy

Carol has a 13-year-old son Timothy and they live at Rockville, MD. She has
had numerous jobs of which all pertained to the field of public health. At
present she is section chief for the Division of School Health Services of
Montgomery County Health Department of Rockville, MD.

ROGER and MARCELLA [FEICKERT] MAYER

Roger Mayer was born April 30, 1946 in Aberdeen, the son of Harry and Agnes
Mayer. He attended Northern State College and University of Tulsa, OK.

        Jeromy, Roger, Marcella, Jason, Joshua Mayer

He married Marcella Feickert July 5, 1972. She was born May 27, 1951 in
Eureka to Emanuel and Clara Feickert and grew up in Bowdle. The family
moved to Aberdeen after Emanuel's death. Marcella attended Presentation
College.

Roger and Marcella have three children. Jeromy Roger was born March 22,
1977; Jason Emanuel, Aug. 27, 1979 and Joshua Michael, Jan. 19, 1983.

DAVID L. and CHERYL [ALDINGER] McCARLSON

David, born Aug. 27, 1956 at Webster, is the son of Arnold and Lydia
McCarlson. He was in the Armed Services, stationed in Germany. After his
return he married Cheryl Aldinger July 1, 1978. She is the daughter of

Cheryl attended Bowdle School and in 1972 began working at Bowdle State

David worked several years as a mechanic for Taylor's Implement in Ipswich.

DR. GEORGE and DOROTHEA [ERNEST] McINTOSH

George Frederick McIntosh, MD was born on a farm bordering Swan Lake
between Bowdle and Hoven April 7, 1915. His father George Frederick
McIntosh was born March 21, 1875 in Sauk County, WI and died Jan. 9, 1967
in Eureka. His mother Bertha Gill McIntosh was born May 18, 1892 in Russia
and died in Eureka Dec. 17. 1977.

        Dorothea and Dr. George McIntosh

George was one of three children. He graduated from Bowdle High School,
received a bachelor of arts degree from University of South Dakota and a
bachelor of science degree from University of South Dakota School of
Medicine.

A significant year in his life was 1941. He completed his MD degree at Rush
Medical College in Chicago, IL and married Dorothea Lillian Ernest Nov. 27,
in Hammond, IN, her birthplace and hometown. Dorothea is a graduate of
Presbyterian Hospital School of Nursing in Chicago.

Following an internship at Ancker Hospital in St. Paul, MN George served as
a flight surgeon in the U.S. Air Force four years and attained the rank of
Major.

Dr. Mac, as he is known by his patients, began medical practice in Eureka
in the spring 1946 and currently practices there with his daughter Susan
Amy McIntosh Ostrowski, MD.

He has also served on the staff of Bowdle Hospital and performed surgery
there several years.

Three children were born to Dr. Mac and Dorothea. Judith Ann was born Oct.
22, 1946. She is married to John Richard Baudler, MD and resides in Arden
Hills, MN. Their children are Sarah Rachel and Jessica Ann.

Susan Amy was born Jan. 14, 1949. She married Peter John Ostrowski Jr. They
live in Eureka where she practices medicine and he is a lawyer. Their
children are John Peter, David Paul and Diana Sara.

Pamela Ann, born Jan. 7, 1957, is a medical secretary and lives in
Saratoga, CA.

ARTHUR C. and WALLY [WALTERS] MERKEL

Arthur C. Merkel was born Oct. 25, 1901 to Fred P. and Jacobina (Blumhardt)
Merkel. His parents were of German-Russian extraction. His father came to
Bowdle in 1884 and was a blacksmith. Jacobina came with her parents in 1895.

Mr. Merkel's blacksmith shop was just north of the Bowdle Pioneer on third
Avenue until it burned. Then he moved it to a location on Second Street
where Bowdle Cenex is now doing business. Arthur attended Bowdle Schools
and after graduation he and his cousin Edwin Blumhardt attended Mankato
(MN) Business College.

On his return home Art was employed at J. Kurle Implement Co. and Security
State Bank with Alex Searle and Carl Kundert as officers until it closed in
1932. He then set up an insurance and real estate agency. In May 1929 Art
and Leurene (Wally) Walters of Groton were married and established their
home on Third Avenue where they lived until they retired.

Wally was the daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Robert Walters. She was born in 1902
in Wisconsin and came with her parents to the Groton area in 1910. Her
father was a farmer. Wally was a graduate of Groton and Presentation School
of Nursing at St. Luke's Hospital in Aberdeen. After obtaining her RN
Degree she did private duty nursing and spent some time in Crescent City,
CA working in a hospital. She was employed at Bowdle Hospital when she met
her future husband.

After their marriage Wally continued to assist with surgery and in other
emergencies at the hospital, took an active interest in the hospital
contributing to its welfare and progress in many ways. She was a member of
Bowdle Hospital Auxiliary, Order of Eastern Star and several social clubs in
the city.

In 1932 their only child Merle was born. He attended Bowdle School and
University of North Dakota and joined the Naval Air Force rising to the
rank of Ensign. He married Marilyn Hagel of Ellendale, ND in 1956. They
lived at Pensacola, FL where he was stationed until an airplane collision
took his life in 1959. Their daughter Barbara was born in 1960. Marilyn
remarried to Robert Widhalm and they live in Jacksonville, FL.

Mr. and Mrs. Art Merkel furnished a room at the hospital in memory of their
son Merle. Art Merkel succeeded Karl Kundert as manager of Federal Land
Bank Association of Bowdle in 1937. At that time the office was located in
the old Atlas Lumber Co. building northwest of Kurle Implement. The
building later became Bowdle Livestock Sales Barn. Art bought the building
on main that housed Larson Jewelry and the Federal Land Bank was housed
there until it became affiliated with Federal Land Bank and Credit
Production Association in Aberdeen.

Art was a very community spirited person. Through his efforts the streets
of town were dust-proof surfaced, improvements were made at the little City
Park, he was interested in the construction of the new hospital completed
in 1962, served as president of Commercial Club, a member of Sportsmen's
Club and Golf Club, served as city auditor and was on committees for
Bowdle's Golden and Diamond Jubilees. Through his efforts the city acquired
the first building used for municipal purposes (the old city liquor store,
now the Senior Citizens building), was secretary of the cemetery
association and through his efforts a perpetual care system was set up and
improved the appearance of this final resting place.

After Art's retirement in 1966 he and Wally spent their last years in
Bowdle and wintered in North Palm Beach, FL and visited their
daughter-in-law and granddaughter in Jacksonville, FL. Art died in 1972.
Wally returned to Groton and died in June 1976. Their granddaughter, Mrs.
Barbara Clark, lives in San Antonio, TX.

ERNEST and LOLA [THOMAS] MERKEL

Ernest (Ernie) was the son of Ludwig (Lou) and Eva Merkel. He was born June
21, 1905 at Bowdle. He graduated from Bowdle High School. After spending
two years in Linton, ND and a year at Dupree, he returned to Bowdle. Ernie
married Lola Thomas Nov. 28, 1928. She was born Dec. 19, 1909 at Everly, IA
to James and Ida Thomas.

In 1929 this young couple purchased Bowdle Meat Market which they operated
until 1944. Just like his father, Ernie learned the trade of butchering and
cutting meats. Ernie was an active member in many organizations including
the fire department, city council and school board.

Ernie and Lola had four children. Jerae married Bemadine Naasz and lives in
Fargo, ND. He has a career in the Navy. Bonnie (Mrs. Roland Buechler) lives
in Des Moines, IA and is in the insurance business. Joyce (Mrs. Lester
Giedt) lives at Bowdle and is finance officer for the city of Bowdle.
Marilyn (Mrs. Dean Schnaible) lives at Adrian, MN and is a teacher's aide.

Ernest Merkel died Dec. 21, 1963 and Lola died Aug. 19, 1980.

LUDWIG and EVA [HOFFMAN] MERKEL

Ludwig (Lou) Merkel was born June 25, 1872 in Okna, Russia to Mr. and Mrs.
Philip Merkel. In 1893 he came with his parents to the United States and
settled in Bowdle.

In November 1897 he married Eva Hoffman who came to this country with her
parents in 1886. They lived on a farm 14 miles northwest of Bowdle.

Lou Merkel was in the meat market business in Bowdle 1903-1923. After
selling his business he operated the farm he owned on the east city limits
until 1941 when he retired from active duties. He died at the age of 84.

Lou Merkel was active in civic affairs, serving as mayor, alderman and
county commissioner for two terms. Lou and Eva spent their entire married
life in Bowdle.

Their children are Minnie (Mrs. A.J. Englehard); Carrie (Mrs. D.F. Meile);
William, Ernest; Belle (Mrs. Albert Kilber); Adela (Mrs. George Blando Jr.)
and Agnes (Mrs. Thomas Lipscomb.)

RUDOLPH and LORETTA [DIEDE] MERKEL

Rudolph (Rudy) Merkel has lived on the same farm seven miles south of
Bowdle for 45 years. He was born in 1916 to William and Magdalena Merkel at
Eureka. His father was born Jan. 25, 1890 at Greenway and died Nov. 17,
1958. Magdalena Merkel was born at Greenway Feb. 29, 1894 and lives in
Eureka.

        Back: Lawrence and Clyde Front: Lois, Loretta, Rudolph, Alice Merkel

Rudy Merkel married Loretta Diede Nov. 16, 1939 at Venturia, ND. She was
born July 17, 1918 to Andrew and Emilia Diede. Her father was born Feb. 11,
1884 in Johannestahl, South Russia and died Nov. 1, 1957. Her mother was
born Oct. 4, 1890 in Eureka and died March 10, 1984.

Rudy's parents farmed northeast of Eureka, where he received his education
in the district school and then attended the Auto and Tractor School in
Fargo, ND. He operated his own garage for some time and then worked in the
Ford Garage at Hosmer before taking his family to the farm south of Bowdle
in the spring of 1940. He purchased the farm through Federal Land Bank
Association of Bowdle at the time Art Merkel was the association manager.

Rudy recalls many of the ups and downs of farming, the drought years and
good crop years, but outstanding was the hardship of the heavy snowfalls of
January and February 1952 when they were isolated for six weeks with no
groceries, mail, fuel or telephone. They were not able to deliver their
farm products for sale so they churned the cream into butter in the family
washing machine.

A member of Evangelical United Brethren Church until it was consolidated
with United Methodist Church, Rudy says, "The Lord has blessed us with four
children, good health and a good life."

Rudy Merkel served on the Odessa Township Board many terms. He and Loretta
are now in retirement on the same farm.

Lawrence Merkel was born June 2, 1940. He married Patricia French and they
live in Belton, TX. Their children are Phillip, Jeffery and Henry. Lawrence
is employed in house trailer set-up, repair and sales and city farming.

Alice F. Merkel was born July 29, 1943 and married Jacob S. Helm. They live
in St. Charles, IL where Jacob is a conveyor sales engineer. Their children
are Aileen and Stuart.

Lois L. Merkel joined the family Dec. 14, 1944. She is the wife of John
Mumford. He is an engineer for Ford Motor Co. in Farmington Hills, MI and
they have a son Andrew.

Clyde D. Merkel was born Dec. 2, 1960 and married Julie Schaefer. Lt.
Merkel was stationed at Columbus, GA where Julie attended the University
until March 1985 when the U.S. Army transferred Clyde to Germany for a tour
of duty.

ADAM and ROSE [AIPPERSPACH] MERTZ

Adam Mertz and Rose Aipperspach were married Dec. 9, 1922 and moved to a
farm near Mahto. In 1925 they moved to a farm west of Bowdle and in the
1950's they moved to a farm in the Hoven area. Adam moved to Minneapolis,
MN in 1956. He continued to make his home there until he died April 11,
1964. Rose moved to Java where she made her home for some time until moving
to Mobridge. In 1975 she became a resident of Hosmer Nursing Home until her
death in the early 1980's.

        Adam and Rose Mertz

Eight children blessed their home. Ervin died in infancy. Ellina married
Walter Barth. They reside in Huron where Walter works for Federal Crop
Insurance Corporation. They have four children and nine grandchildren.

Ella Mertz married Vernard Schneider and they live in Mobridge where Ella
works for Stoick's Super Valu and Vernard works for the City Water Plant.
They have a son and four grandchildren.

        Back: Don, Allen, Quentin Front: Ellina, Ella, Roland, Eleanor Mertz

Eleanor Mertz married Johnny Gab. They reside in Mobridge where Johnny owns
and operates Mobridge Gas Co. They have a daughter and a grandson.

Roland Mertz married Mary Lassle. They also live in Mobridge where he works
for the state department and Mary is employed at Mobridge Hospital. They
have a son, a daughter and one grandson.

Quentin Mertz married Lynn Bohenkaup. They also live in Mobridge where he
is employed by Montana-Dakota Utilities Co. and Lynn works for Bormann and
Buckmeier attorneys.

Donald Mertz married Margaret Raba. They live at Mobridge where he works
for Amoco Standard Station and Margaret is employed by the Unemployment
Claim Center. They have three children. Allen Mertz married Jane Kosters.
They live in Mobridge where he works for Jensen Rock and Sand and Jane
works at Stoick's Super Valu. They have three children.

DAN B. and JEANETTE [TAYLOR] MERTZ

Dan B. Mertz was born June 3, 1914 in Bowdle and died May 1, 1979. He
attended Bowdle High School, graduated from Plainview Academy in Redfield
in 1933 and attended Union College in Lincoln, NE. It was there he met
Jeanette Taylor of Lubbock, TX. They were married Sept. 13, 1935 in Walla
Walla, WA and returned to the farm east of Bowdle where they lived until
1945 when they moved to Lodi, CA. They operated a Grade "A" dairy for 15
years. Dan was also into building and construction work in Lodi.

        Jeanette and Dan Mertz

Dan and Jeanette continued grain farming near Bowdle, making the trip twice
each year (spring and fall) and also did custom harvesting in the southern
states with two big John Deere combines for 11 years. Jeanette did all the
trucking of grain to the elevators. Their comment was, "two busy, but happy
people."

Their son Dr. Kenneth J. Mertz was born Aug. 12, 1936. He is a dentist in
Calimesa, CA. He and his wife Shirley have two sons: Michael and Daniel.

Their daughter Mary Etta (Mertz) Sheridan was born Sept. 18, 1937. She is a
dental nurse in Lodi, CA and has two daughters: Jeanne Lyn and Sherri Lyn.

EMIL M. and LENORA [PIETZ] MERTZ

Emil M. Mertz, local farmer and conservationist, was born Dec. 15, 1919 to
Jacob and Elizabeth Mertz in Walworth County northwest of Bowdle. He
received his education in the rural school. Jacob Mertz was born Nov. 28,
1892 in South Russia and died Jan. 5, 1978. Elizabeth Mertz was born Sept.
27, 1892 in Eureka and died Feb. 22, 1986.

        Lenora and Emil M. Mertz

Emil married Lenora A. Pietz, who was born Sept. 6, 1926. She is the
daughter of Ruben and Emila Pietz. Ruben was born Dec. 30, 1900 in Hosmer
and Emila was born in Roscoe March 27, 1900.

Emil worked on the family farm until 1948 when he purchased the Ernest Haupt
farm 1-1/2 miles west of Bowdle. Emil and Lenora were married June 11,
1950. She received her education in the district school and worked as a
hired girl. She recalls that in those days wages were $2 a week and
increased to $2.50 if you proved competent. As she says, "How times have
changed." Emil and Lenora are active members of St. Paul American Lutheran
Church.

ERNEST and DOROTHY [GIEDT] MERTZ

Ernest was the son of Mr. and Mrs. Jacob D. Mertz, the oldest of seven
children. He was born Oct. 15, 1915 on a tiny farm northwest of Bowdle. He
remembers running up and down the hill where the tiny farm was located. His
mother had to tie him and his brother Otto to the table legs so the baby
Emil would be safe while she went milking. Like most of the children in the
community, Ernest went to school with a horse and buggy.

Although Ernest loved school and had aspired to be a pastor (as were three
of his uncles) this was not to be. Otto wanted to go to high school and Dad
Mertz needed help at home, so Ernest bowed to the inevitable and ended up
being a farmer.

Dorothy Mertz, likewise, grew up on a farm south of Bowdle. She was
born July 29, 1923 to Mr. and Mrs. Henry Giedt. While she was going to high
school she was a classmate of Ernest's sister Frieda. There were a few
chance invitations to the Mertz farm. Dorothy worked at Jones Drug Store
after school and weekends. One April night Ernest got up enough courage to
ask Dorothy if he could take her home. This eventually led to a wedding
Aug. 29, 1943 at St. John's Ev. Lutheran Church with Pastor Albrecht
officiating.

The sermon was in German for the grandparents Mr. and Mrs. Adam Mertz of
Java and Mr. and Mrs. John Ulrich's benefit. However the ceremony was in
English. The reception was at the Mertz farm northwest of Bowdle. Many of
the neighbors arrived later in the evening for a good old-fashioned
shivaree. The Honeymoon was out to the cow barn and the threshing fields the
next day. Dorothy kept an eye on the farrowing sows and helped unload
barley.

        Back: Michael, Paul, Garry, Dean, Ernest J. Front: Dorothy, Ernest,
        Ruth Mertz

Ernest and Dorothy's children amounted to a basketball team and a
cheerleader. Ernest J. was born in 1944, Ruth in 1947, Paul in 1951, Dean in
1952, Michael in 1954 and Garry in 1958. To relate some things this group
pulled would fill the pages of a book.

Ruth had to help Dorothy in the house and soon became a better cook and
bread baker than her mother. With her talents she was able to go to the
State Fair and win a purple ribbon with her bread baking. This also won her
a trip to the National Club Congress.

All the children, along with their parents, were very active in 4-H and the
Farmers Union youth group. Ernest was a leader for several years before he
and Dorothy were married. Dorothy was a leader for 22 years and a Farmers
Union youth leader for 21 years.

After graduating from high school Ernest J. went to SDSU. He was always
gun-shy and said it would take a good horse and a long rope to catch him.
One lovely lady by the name of Pauline Thomas caught his eye and his heart.
They were married and have three lovely children: Tina, Keith and Rachel.
They live on the family farm.

The boys were all sports minded. It was very few weeks that one did not
come home with a knee or ankle injury either from football or basketball.
Ernest kept busy keeping his sons occupied and teaching them. Dorothy was
busy with Farmers Union youth, 4-H and loved plants and also had a huge
garden, chickens and turkeys. The love for plants led to an extensive hobby
with a number of greenhouses -- some of which the wind and tornadoes wrecked.

Ruth married a college sweetheart Don Claeys. Don went into the service in
1969. Ruth followed him to Germany along with their 18-month-old son
Joseph. In 1971 Ernest and Dorothy, along with Albert and Bertha Leidholt,
drove to Milwaukee. Cousin Bob Giedt took them to Chicago where they
boarded a plane for an unforgettable trip to Europe, chiefly where Don,
Ruth and Joseph were. They spent a month visiting Ruth and family and a
number of places in Belgium and England. Ruth and Don also have a daughter
Amy and now live in Jefferson.

After Ernest and Dorothy got back from Europe in July Dorothy drove to
Brookings to take a course in floral design to help her with the flower
shop she had started in the family room of the farm home.

Meanwhile the rest of the family was maturing. Paul continued his education
at NSC and worked at Bonanza. He now lives in Watertown, is married to
Rosemary Dewald and has three children: Adam, Christopher and Scott. Dean
Mertz majored in public health nursing and administration at SDSU. He lives
at Prescott, AZ with his wife Debbie and two children: Ryan and Eric.
Michael Mertz attended NSC and lives with his wife and children Nicole and
Nathan at Milwaukee, WI. Garry Mertz attended NSC and lives in Ellendale,
ND with his wife Monica Steiger.

In 1976 Ernest and Dorothy built a home in Bowdle, which was also the site
of the flower shop. They moved in Dec. 24, 1976 and Christmas Day dinner
was served in the new home. Two days later Dean married Debbie Bennett at
Redeemer Lutheran Church. Dorothy baked the wedding cake and arranged all
the flowers for the wedding.

Ernest kept busy driving to the family farm where Ernie and his family live.
Dorothy was busy with flowers and cakes. In August 1979 Dorothy realized
she was unable to handle the flower shop and sold it. By a chance of luck
she was able to get back with people again by getting into the insurance
business.

Ernest keeps busy in the summer going to the farm. He loves working with
the fields. Ernie is a cattleman so this works out fine for both. Ernest
will go with Dorothy occasionally on her insurance calls to see she isn't
driving too fast. They both love to take some time off when they go to
visit their children and 12 grandchildren.

ERNEST J. and PAULINE [THOMAS] MERTZ

Ernest J. Mertz born Sept. 21, 1944, son of Ernest and Dorothy Mertz,
attended Buechler Country grade school and graduated from Bowdle High
School in 1962. He attended one year of college and then worked on the
family farm.

        Tina, Ernest J., Pauline, Rachel, Keith Mertz

Pauline Thomas, born May 7, 1948, daughter of Adam and Jennie Thomas,
attended Bowdle School and graduated in 1966. She attended one year of
college and worked in Onida before their marriage April 12, 1969. Since
then they have lived on the Mertz family farm and have three children. Tina
is 13, Keith 10 and Rachel 4.

FRED and KATHRYN [BITZER] MERTZ

Fred and Kathryn (Bitzer) Mertz arrived in the United States in 1893. They

Mildred married Leo Schack of Tolstoy in November 1936. They moved on the

children are Shawn, Rhett, Flynt and Cindy. Janice Schack married Wyman
Haberer in 1958. They live in Long Lake, MN and have two children Dawn and
Jerry. Karis Schack married Doris Beck. Karis is in construction business
and lives in Lincoln, NE. Their children are Janeen and Garnell. Leo and
Mildred moved to Bowdle to retire in 1978.

Jacob and Martha's son Victor married Ruby Pedersen of Moscow, ID. They
moved to Lodi, CA where they have a construction company. Their children
are Gary and Marlys.

HARLAN and JOYCE [KRAUSE] MERTZ

Harlan John Mertz was born the youngest of seven children to Jacob D. and

southwest of Bowdle.

Harlan married Joyce, daughter of Rev. & Mrs. A.A. Krause, in 1957. They

Mark Mertz and his wife Lori live and work in Denver, CO. Mark is an auto

Lisa and husband Raymond DeWall live in Grand Forks, ND. She is an

Jonathan Mertz is interested in political science and economics and has had
some interesting experiences working for the mayor of Sioux Falls, Senator
James Abdnor in Washington, D.C. and being assistant campaign manager and
coordinator for the Dale Bell campaign. He is now a legislative assistant
for Senator Abdnor in Washington, D.C.

Marilyn Mertz is interested in business with options in management and

        Back: Jonathan, Harlan, Raymond, Mark Front: Marilyn, Joyce, Lisa,
        Lori

One highlight of their family life was in 1983 when they had the excitement

JACOB D. and ELIZABETH [BIEBER] MERTZ

Jacob David Mertz was born in Neuglueckstahl, South Russia Nov. 27, 1892 to
Adam and Caroline Mertz. He was 2 years old when he came with his parents
from South Russia and settled on a small parcel of land 5 miles east of
Java. This was a homestead. The winters were very hard so they kept warm by
twisting slough hay to burn. Father Adam Mertz walked to Ipswich to get
flour for bread that mother Caroline baked. This trip took him two days
complete as it was approximately 35 miles one way.

The family's first animals were a horse and ox. They broke some land and
seeded it by hand and threshed the grain with a flail. In due time three
more children were born: Margaret, John and Lena.

Jacob grew to manhood on this tiny homestead. As young Jacob grew his
thoughts were to establish a home of his own. No doubt he did some scouting
by horse and buggy. His trips eventually led him to the Johann Bieber home
where he had his eye on a young lady by the name of Elizabeth. He had heard
many things about this young gal -- that she was a thrifty person and also
was a good cook and young Jacob loved to eat.

Jacob and Elizabeth's courting culminated in a wedding at Java Dec. 27,
1914 officiated by Rev. Kirchdoerfer. Their first home was established
1-1/2 miles south of the original homestead. They had a tiny four-room
frame house and a barn. The garden fence was rows of rocks which surrounded
the garden area and they are still standing today, as are the rhubarb and
iris Elizabeth planted in 1914. Jacob eked a living on this tiny farm. Here
also the first three boys were born: Ernest, Otto and Emil.

Jacob and Elizabeth could see that the hilly terrain of their tiny farm was
just not the place they wanted to raise their family. In 1922 they moved to
the family farm one mile east of the original. Their new home now was a sod
house which was cool in the summer and comparatively warm in the winter. As
soon as they could they moved the original house from the first farm and
lived in that. In 1922 their first girl Frieda was born.

        Elizabeth and Jacob Mertz

By now Jacob and Elizabeth could see that their tiny house was getting too
small. In 1928 they built a new and much larger home. In order to fill the
added bedrooms three more children were born: Hulda, Caroline and Harlan.

Jacob and Elizabeth worked very hard enduring many hardships and droughts.
They were very fortunate that the family was comparatively healthy and
being a farm family everyone learned the meaning of work.

In 1939 Ernest, his brothers and sisters surprised their parents with a
25th wedding anniversary party at the family farm.

The year 1941 brought the start of the war years and for a time it looked
as the oldest son Ernest would have to go into the service. Jacob knew that
the Army needed food to survive so he was able to keep Ernest at home with
a deferment. Emil's health prevented him from the draft. Otto was teaching
and going to school so in 1942 he was drafted. He spent his service time in
the states and did not have to go overseas.

In 1943 Ernest decided it was time to break away and establish his own
home. Jacob and Elizabeth had purchased the Joe Kelsch home in 1942 so
after Ernest's wedding they moved to town with most of the family. Emil
remained on the farm with Ernest and his new bride.

Jacob and Elizabeth kept busy the first years in Bowdle. Elizabeth had a
few chickens and a garden. She also learned to braid rugs and made many
quilts. In 1954 Jacob and Elizabeth celebrated their 40th wedding
anniversary at St. Paul's American Lutheran Church in Bowdle. Not all the
children were able to be home.

On a blustery Dec. 27, 1964 the couple celebrated their 50th anniversary at
Redeemer Lutheran Church in Bowdle. By now all of their brood had left home
and established homes of their own. Jacob and Elizabeth's health was
deteriorating. Jacob spent about a year at Good Samaritan Home in Selby and
then was a resident of Bowdle Nursing Home. He died Jan. 5, 1978. Elizabeth
died Feb. 23, 1985. Jacob's parents Adam died in 1951 and Caroline in 1947.

The Mertz children follow. Ernest is married to Dorothy, has six children
and live in Bowdle. Otto married Juanita, has two children and lives in
California. Emil married Lenora and lives in Bowdle. Frieda was married to
Cyril Paepke, had two children and died April 19, 1985. Hulda lives in
California and has four children. Caroline married Dwayne Lee. They had two
children (one deceased) and live near Bowdle. Harlan married Joyce, has
four children and lives near Bowdle.

JOHN and MARY [KRUEGER] MERTZ

John Mertz was born in Bowdle Sept. 1, 1887, the son of Fredrick and
Katherine Klein Mertz. His parents were married in Russia Jan. 23, 1883 and
shortly thereafter immigrated to the United States, settling on a farm six
miles south of Bowdle. Their son John lived with his parents until his
father bought another farm 5-1/2 miles southeast of Bowdle.

        John and Mary Mertz

John batched it on this farm until he was 25, when he met and married Mary
Krueger of McClusky, ND. Mary was born Jan. 31, 1893 on the ship en route
to the States from Odessa, Russia. They lived on the farm southeast of
Bowdle until 1937 when they moved to Lodi, CA.

Mr. Mertz had been an extensive wheat farmer while living in South Dakota.
In California he became a vineyard dresser. They spent many happy years
with their family singing favorite hymns in German and English. Mary died
July 2, 1978 and John died June 2, 1981.

Their children include Dan B. of Lodi, CA. He was born June 3, 1914 and
died May 1, 1979. His wife was the former Jeanette Taylor of Lubbock, TX.
They had two children: Dr. Kenneth J. Mertz and Mary Etta Mertz Sheridan.
The Sheridans have two daughters.

Elmer Mertz was born Sept. 11, 1915 and lives in Lodi, CA. Edgar Dale Mertz
was born Nov. 25, 1916 and lives in Lodi, CA.

John and Mary's hearts were touched when death took the lives of close
relatives leaving a two-year-old little girl without parents. They took
Selma Mertz into their home. She was married to Ted Entzi March 17, 1940 at
Lodi, CA.

Seventeen years later the family was surprised with the birth of a
beautiful little girl Flora Jean March 11, 1934. She married Leonard
Fischer of Lodi, CA June 2, 1956 and died Nov. 11, 1961.

The Mertz family feels, "In life man plans, but God directs. Many sad
experiences occur that we cannot understand now, but some day in the Great
Hereafter, all will be made known."

OTTO J. and JUANITA MERTZ

Otto J. Mertz was born May 30, 1917 on a farm northwest of Bowdle to Jacob
D. and Elizabeth Mertz. His father died in January 1977 and his mother died
Sept. 27, 1984.

Otto and his wife Juanita were married June 23, 1960 at Spiro, OK. They
have a daughter Monica Ruth who was born Sept. 14, 1967. She is a high
school senior and three-year varsity tennis player.

        Juanita, Monica, Otto J. Mertz

Dr. Otto Mertz graduated from Java High School in 1936, attended Northern
State College in Aberdeen and received his bachelor of science degree with
an agricultural science major and a minor in education from South Dakota
State University at Brookings in 1942. He received his doctorate in
education in 1953 from University of California Los Angeles and has
continued his education at UCLA through summer schools.

His first teaching experience began in rural schools of his home district
and he has completed 30 years of teaching, 28 of which were in California
institutions. He taught pupils in the sixth grade, junior and high schools
and college in California including such subjects as driver's education,
on-farm service for veterans in Phoenix, AZ, biology, physiology, general
and physical science and communications on a full-time basis.

As he said, "Putting it another way, teaching took me from the prairie to
the asphalt and concrete jungle."

OSCAR and ANNE [KUEBLER] METZGER

Oscar Metzger was born Oct. 15, 1916 in Campbell County, son of Gustave and
Anna Metzger. His father was born in 1891 in Russia and died Jan. 1, 1974.
His mother was born in 1897 in Campbell County.

Oscar married Anne Kuebler, daughter of John and Selma Kuebler. She was
born Aug. 30, 1917. The birthplace of both parents was McPherson County.
John was born in 1892 and died April 30, 1968 and Selma was born in 1897 and
died Aug. 31, 1950.

Oscar and Anne were married in Eureka June 25, 1939. Anne recalls,
"Remembering our wedding date we remember that old-fashioned barn dance and
that midnight supper we had for our guests. After a short honeymoon we
returned to our respective families. I helped my dad with the harvesting
and Oscar helped his dad. After harvest we moved to a rented farm from Rose
Straub."

        Anne and Oscar Metzger

The Straub farm was sold causing Anne and Oscar to move to Bowdle to
purchase the Aldinger farm. Here was a dream come true--600 acres for $5.75
an acre. Being the depression years times were hard for the young couple.
Oscar used to hunt rabbits with Emil Kuebler for money. Anne remembers
driving around picking cow chips to burn for household fuel. The weather at
times was not cooperative causing hailstorms that would damage 50-60% of
the crops, yielding only about 10 bushels per acre. But still the young
couple was not discouraged.

Oscar remembers often working late into the night in the fields while Anne
often spent days pulling weeds and burning them. Together they saved enough
money to buy an International Harvester binder from Kurle's in Bowdle. It
was a time of rationing so Kurle's only got three of them, making Oscar
quite fortunate to receive one. Much of the harvesting done was shared with
other farmers on each others land. In the fall 1942 Oscar did not complete
his harvesting until the day before Thanksgiving. In 1943 he purchased a
1936 tractor for $150 and a threshing machine for $1,000.

In 1945 the Metzgers brought electricity to their home making great
improvements on the farm. The source of electricity was a 32-volt wind
charger with 18 batteries in the house basement. This meant lights in the
house and barn and even a washing machine for Anne.

Although farming conditions were improving the Metzgers decided to change
careers. So in 1947 they moved to Bowdle and purchased the Phillips 66
Station from Jake Kessler. Oscar owned the business for 33 years. Retired
now, he still helps Duane Knecht, the present owner.

While on the farm Oscar and Anne's only family member was a dog named
Sandie. But in the 104 degree weather Aug. 16, 1950 a baby girl Sheila Kay
was born. She had a sister Marcie DeeAnn born March 19, 1955. Sheila
married Dr. David Anderson, has four children and lives in Mendota Heights,
MN. Marcie married Arlyn Schaible. They have two children and live in West
Fargo, ND.

Having an interest in community services Oscar served on the city council,
school board, fire department and church council. Anne was president of the
Hospital Auxiliary at the time when the new hospital was built. She served
17 years as assistant leader of the Busy Bowdle Stars 4-H Club, Sunday
School teacher, secretary of the church council, member of ALCW and
contributed much volunteer time to heart and cancer funds.

Anne recalls, "One of my greatest highlights of my life was the day in 1976
when I received my high school diploma from Pierre after completing a short
adult evening course named G.E.D. from Bowdle High School.

LARRY and ALEXZINE [KIESZ] MILES

Alexzine was born Jan. 26, 1951 to Arnold and Martha Kiesz of Bowdle. She
graduated from Bowdle in 1969 and received a nursing degree in 1971 from

        Alexzine and Larry Miles and Marc, Eric, Todd

when he opened a business with Sydney Baus known as B & M Body and Repair

Alexzine has been working as a nurse since college graduation and has been
