Henry married Doris Himmrich July 25, 1948. They have three sons and live
in Mobridge.

Elsie married Dewane (T-Bone) Rosch Nov. 14, 1948. They have four daughters
and lived in Selby.

DeWAYNE and KAREN [SCHLEPP] WEISZHAAR

DeWayne Weiszhaar, who served Bowdle as mayor three years, is the son of
Alex and Anna (Buechler) Weiszhaar. He was born in Bowdle May 20, 1938.
DeWayne graduated from Bowdle High School in 1956. He attended Gayle
Institute of Technology in Minneapolis and worked for Burlington Northern
Railroad a year. He married Karen Jean Schlepp June 16, 1957.

Karen was born at Bowdle Hospital June 14, 1938 to Adam and Eugenia (Dubs)
Schlepp. She received her education in rural and public schools, graduating
from Bowdle in 1956. She was employed by Liberty Mutual Insurance Co. in
Minneapolis and also worked at the A & B Shop in Bowdle in 1957.

The couple returned to Bowdle in 1958 and farmed until 1972 when DeWayne
took the position of salesman for Haberer's Implement. In 1978 he purchased
the business and its branch in Mobridge.

DeWayne has served on the St. Paul Lutheran Church Council, is a member of
the Bowdle Fire Department and Bowdle Golf Club. He was on the City Council
1974-1984 and is a past member of the Bowdle Jaycees.

        Mike, Curt, Scott, DeWayne and Mike Schlomer Karen and Becky

The couple has four children. Scott Wayne was born Sept. 10, 1960. He
attended Northern State College in 1979 and SDSU in 1980. He presently is
parts manager for Haberer's Implement Inc.

Becky Lynn was born Sept. 28, 1961. She earned a bachelor of music degree
at Northern State College and was music instructor at Selby School. She
married Michael Schlomer June 8, 1985.

Michael Jon, born Jan. 16, 1966, is a student at Northern State College in
Aberdeen and Curtis Wade, born Nov. 14, 1969, is a student at Bowdle High
School.

Karen keeps busy as organist for her church, is a past Jaycette member and
a member of Bowdle Golf Club, Extension Club, ALCW of her church and
Hospital Auxiliary.

JACOB and NELLIE A. WEISZHAAR By Nellie Weiszhaar

"In the fall of 1931 I came to Bowdle to teach at the John B. Buechler
School. When I inquired directions to the school Martin Gross asked me
Which John Buechler, John A., John B. or John J? I had to look at the name
on the contract and found it was John B. Martin Gross also told me that I
had better learn to understand German so I would know what people were
saying about me. I did learn and Mrs. John B. (Mary) Buechler and I had
many conversations with her speaking German and me speaking English.

"In 1944 my husband Jacob Weiszhaar and son Robert and I moved to a farm
one mile north of Bowdle which we purchased from Mr. Nickisch. At that time
I was teaching in the Roscoe High School. Then I taught in the Bowdle High
School from 1946 to 1949 and was elected Edmunds County Superintendent of
Schools in 1960 and until the fall of 1963 drove daily to Ipswich, when we
moved to make our home there.

"I served as Edmunds County Superintendent of Schools until 1971 when that
office was terminated due to the reorganization of school districts. From
1971 to 1975 I was employed as elementary principal and librarian at
Hitchcock.

        Jacob and Nellie Weiszhaar

"Since retiring I continue to live in Ipswich where I have served as
chairman of the Bicentennial Celebration in 1976 and the chairman of the
Ipswich Centennial in 1983."

ANTON and IDA [WIEPKING] WENTZ

Among Californians who still have fond memories of Bowdle as their hometown
are Anton (Tony) and Ida (Wiepking) Wentz of Stockton. Tony was born Dec.
10, 1903 at Bowdle. His parents were Sebastian and Rosina Wentz who came
from Russia. Sebastian was foreman on the railroad. In 1917 they moved to
the Raphael Dewald farm east of Bowdle and later to the John Koch farm
where a fire destroyed the home and all their personal possessions and they
moved back to the Dewald farm thankful no lives were lost.

        Ida, Anton and granddaughter Tenneill

In 1921 Tony's dad died, leaving a widow and 10 children. The older
children went out to find jobs to help their mother and saved $250 which
they sent her. She moved her family into Bowdle and some years later she
married Mr. Werner. After his death she joined her four sons and two
daughters in Las Vegas, NV and lived to age 95, spending the last years
crocheting and playing pinochle. She died in 1977.

Anton received his education at Bowdle and worked for farmers in the area.
In 1942 he enlisted in the U.S. Army, receiving his training as a 37 MM
Anti-tank Gunner at Camp Roberts, CA. In 1943 he received an honorable
discharge. Anton and Ida were married Feb. 1, 1944. She was the daughter of
Albert and Mary Wiepking, Sr.

Ida was born Sept. 29, 1913 at Bowdle. She writes, "I began my education in
a one-room school, graduated in 1933 from Bowdle and decided to become a
teacher, as I love to work with children. I attended Northern State College
in Aberdeen and taught several years in and around Bowdle.

"For my first teaching job I received $60 a month and I always had to be my
own janitor. When I think of the country school years, with maybe pupils in
all eight grades, I can feel again the harsh cold winter weather, the
nights spent at the school house due to blizzards, kerosene lamps we used
for light, having to melt snow so I could wash my face and hands, the
outdoor chick sales with the Sears and Roebuck catalog instead of toilet
paper, the Nash car that would not start in cold weather even after a team
of horses pulled it and I would have to walk three miles or more, the
pot-bellied stove that would not draw so the fuel would burn and produce
heat and how the children and I would clap our hands and stamp our feet to
warm them. The children were so anxious to learn and I cannot remember any
discipline problems. God bless them. Those were the days, but I loved it
all."

After their marriage Anton and Ida decided to go to California. In Stockton
there was a demand for workers at the Naval Supply Annex and Ida applied
for the clerk-typist position and was sent to Oakland for training. She
worked in communications until 1947 and then she took time out to have a
family.

Their children: Frank G. is now assistant vice-president of the real estate
department of American Savings and Loan Association in Stockton and doubles
as information and cost systems manager. Donald D. works as a plumber for
Vince Cowan Plumbing Inc. and Judy Ann (Wentz) Cordova is employed at
Diamond Walnut Plant. She presented her parents with their only
grandchildren, Tennill and Raymond.

Ida Wentz decided to go back to teaching after her children were older and
obtained a bachelor of arts degree from University of the Pacific. She
taught in the elementary grades until she retired in 1975.

Anton worked for Pollack Ship Yards and International Harvester Co. in
California and finally as maintenance engineer for Stockton School District
until his retirement in 1969. He was a member of the board of directors of
Hoover School Little League, serving as coach. He was always greatly
interested in sports and recreation for children. The Wentz family is
enjoying their warmer climate life and their retirement.

GEORGE and EDNA [BAER] WERON

George Weron was born Dec. 27, 1915 to Emanuel and Barbara (Walth) Weron.
He attended rural school and served in the U.S. Army. George married Edna
Baer, daughter of Bernhardt J. and Pauline (Walz) Baer. She lived on a farm
in Walworth County until age 2, when her family moved to Bowdle.

George and Edna lived on a farm near Java, working for Herbert Bieber.
After a short time they moved back to Bowdle where George worked as a
mechanic for Kessler and later Metzger. He also worked 18 years as a
mechanic for Alvin Reuer and before his death he was employed with Schaible
Chevrolet Co.

Edna did housework for others and worked at the library and hospital.
George died Nov. 5, 1970. Edna continues to live at Prairie View Housing
Inc.

CHRISTIAN and HELEN [KNITTEL] WERRE

Christian was born Aug. 5, 1912 near Hosmer to Philip and Christina
(Hottman) Werre. He graduated from the eighth grade in a rural school and as
a young man farmed with his father.

Christian married Helen E. Knittel at the American Lutheran Church in
Bowdle Jan. 27, 1939. She was the daughter of William and Elizabeth (Walz)
Knittel. Helen was born June 28, 1918 at Avon and received a high school
education.

        Back: Mary Lou & Gladys. Front: Helen & Christian

After their marriage Chris and Helen farmed on the Werre homestead place
northeast of Hosmer where their two daughters, Mary Lou and Gladys Mae,
were born.

Farm life was short lived when Chris Werre became seriously ill. They had a
farm auction and moved to Roscoe in 1965 and two years later they moved to
Bowdle where Helen still resides. Christian died Jan. 15, 1985.

Mary Lou Werre married Dan Hintz and they live at Mobridge.

Gladys Mae married Edward Dressler. They live at Bowdle where Gladys is
employed at Bowdle Nursing Home and Edward does small machine repair work
and is a yard maintenance man.

ALBERT F. and MARY [KUEHN] WIEPKING SR.

Albert F. Wiepking was born in Chicago in 1864. In 1900 he decided to look
elsewhere to make his livelihood and came to the Bowdle vicinity where he
homesteaded in Cloyd Valley Township southeast of Bowdle.

His wife Mary Kuehn came to this country from Germany when a young girl and
resided for a time in Baltimore, MD. She then came to South Dakota and
lived until her husband died in 1942.

Albert was engaged in farming with his family which consisted of Anna,
Albert, Ida, Lillian, Henry and Esther. Mr. Wiepking was always interested
in community improvements. He helped organize Cloyd Valley Township and the
Cloyd Valley Telephone Company. He was assessor of the county many years
and a strong believer in education.

        Lillian, Esther, Albert, Ida, Anna. Henry in front.

Albert died at age 74 in 1942 and his wife Mary died in March 1952 at age
77.

ALBERT B. and MARY [BORKIRCHERT] WIEPKING JR.

Albert B. Wiepking was born to Albert F. and Mary Kuehn Wiepking in 1911 in
Cloyd Valley Township, where he was baptized in St. Jacobus Ev. Lutheran
Church and attended the district school. He was confirmed by Pastor P.G.
Albrecht at St. John's Ev. Lutheran Church in Bowdle. Albert has been a
farmer all his working years.

        Mary, Arlyn, Albert Wiepking Jr.

Albert Wiepking married Mary Borkirchert April 1946 at Hosmer. They lived
on a farm southeast of Bowdle in Cloyd Valley Township. In the early years
on the farm there was no electricity so they used kerosene lamps, a
kerosene cooking stove and a wood and coal space heater. All water for
domestic use had to be carried up the hill to the house and there were only
outside Chick Sale facilities in those days. Milking was done by hand and
the cream and eggs income bought groceries and other necessities.

Only a prairie road led 1-1/2 miles to the house, so in a snowy winter the
car was left at the gravel road and the cream and eggs were taken by sled
and horses to the car and then to town. This could only be done once or
twice a month.

Mary and Albert have one son Arlyn who lives in Omaha, NE. He attended
Cloyd Valley District School four years and completed his education in
Bowdle after the family moved to town in 1962. Arlyn graduated from
National College of Business in Rapid City with a degree in computer
science.

Mary Wiepking's parents Jacob F. and Magdalena (Burrer) Borkirchert farmed
north of Roscoe. Mary was confirmed in the Reformed Church at Hosmer. After
graduating from Roscoe High School she was employed in the AAA office in
Ipswich and Bowdle State Bank. She worked 18 years at the R.J. Herman
Insurance Agency in Bowdle until the business was sold.

Mary and Albert are members of St. John's Ev. Lutheran Church in Bowdle and
Mary belongs to the Ladies Aid.

HENRY and ALYCE [GROTH] WIEPKING

Henry Wiepking was born Aug. 12, 1918 in the Bowdle area. His father Albert
was born in 1868 in Chicago, IL and died in 1943. His mother Mary was born
in 1868 in Germany and died in 1951.

Henry earned a bachelor of arts and master of arts and was a teacher in the
Santa Clara, CA schools. He married Alyce Groth, daughter of Albert and
Florence Groth, in 1943. She was born in San Francisco.

Henry's comment is very interesting regarding family life. "My father
homesteaded 160 acres southeast of Bowdle in the early 1900's. Homesteading
in a wild prairie state was indeed a very challenging experience for my
parents. Neither had much experience. My father grew up in Chicago and had
never been on a farm. My mother was an immigrant from Germany who knew very
little about the prairie or farming. Yet, they accepted the challenge. One
has to wonder how they prevailed in a land that was so foreign to them.
Certainly credit must be given to all the early Bowdle settlers who stayed
the course and finally mastered the obstacles.

"There were seven children in their family: Arthur, Anna, Albert, Ida,
Lillian, Henry and Esther. Arthur died at birth and all of the children
were products of home delivery.

"One certainly has to credit the older brothers and sisters who took the
place of hired help. Without their help the struggle to survive would indeed
have been more complex. Education was sacrificed by the older family
members.

"The things I remember as enjoyable are the wide open spaces, clean air, no
pollution except in the 1930's, the four seasons and of course the
wholesome food that can be produced in and around the Bowdle area."

Henry and Alyce Wiepking had four children: Chad, a technician; Robert, an
engineer; Joyce, a credit manager and Mark, a chemist. All live in Santa
Clara, CA.

LOUISA WIEPKING

Louisa Wiepking was the mother of Albert Wiepking Sr. She was born in
Germany in 1840 and died at age 94 in 1934. She lived in Bowdle many years
and later lived with her son Albert until her death.

Grandma, as she was probably best known, was one of Edmunds County's oldest
citizens.

LEONARD J. and GERALDINE [LEIDHOLT] WINCHESTER

Geraldine, daughter of Albert and Bertha Leidholt, was born Sept. 17, 1937
in Bowdle and grew up on the family farm west of Bowdle. She married
Leonard J. Winchester, who was born Sept. 1, 1938 in Aberdeen. The nuptials
took place in Rapid City Sept. 28, 1962. His parents were James and Della
Winchester, both born in Brown County.

Geraldine was born and raised on the farm 4-1/2 miles west of Bowdle which
was originally owned by her grandparents Mr. and Mrs. John J. Buechler. Her
parents then owned it and now her brother Harvey Leidholt owns it. While on
the farm the children went to Yellowstone Trail School 1/2 mile north of
their home.

Geraldine writes, "In the winter there was so much snow the roads were not
opened so Andrew Bauer would hitch the horses to the sleigh and pick up the
Jake Lassle children, Adolph Fleck children and me. He'd come through our
yard and one time the sleigh tipped over and we all rolled out. Mr. Bauer
would cover us with blankets and to keep us warmer the box had a bedding of
hay. One of our grade school teachers was Delores Haupt Rohrbach and when
recess time was over we would be having so much fun playing in the trees,
we didn't want to come when she rang the bell. Then she would punish us by
making us stay in the next school day at recess time. That hurt.

"Then came high school. I had to drive an old Model "A"-- embarrassing to a
young kid (now I wish I had the car) - so I would park the Model "A" at Leo
Sterns and walk to school with their daughter Ronita. Sometimes the Sebert
kids would stop at the farm and give me a ride.

"Chores came before and after school, which included helping to milk 16
cows by hand, feed the chickens, separate the milk, feed the calves and 528
finally breakfast time. My hands were chapped the year round.

"In the spring came seeding and I would do some of the plowing. Sometimes
the plow would hit a rock and off came the plow -- sometimes I would be at
the end of the furrow before I looked around, turned around and got the
plow positioned. Guess I sang or talked too much.

"The blizzards were the best time of year -- no school! Harvey, JoAnn and I
made tunnels and holes in the big snowbanks, which would run from the house
to the barn. The big treat was our sleds.

"I moved to Rapid City in 1959 and lived with my aunt Mrs. Art (Edna)
Aldinger. She was like a second mother to me. There I met Leonard
Winchester and we were married. We now live in Aberdeen where Len works for
the Coca Cola Co."

Mr. and Mrs. Winchester have two daughters. Brenda Kay was born Jan. 29,
1964 and works at the Gibson store. Debbra Ann was born May 29, 1965. She
attended Northern State College and married John Davis of Columbia May 25,
1984.

WILLIAM and KATHERINE [MAIER] WOLF

William Wolf was born March 8, 1900 at Java. He has been a resident of
Bowdle since Oct. 8, 1944 and with his son-in-law Leonard Joachim owned and
operated the City Dray Line 7-1/2 years. They sold the business in 1952 and
William took the job of City Police, which he held 13 years.

He then became a salesman for Standard Feed and Minerals and later helped
with farm work in the Java and Ipswich areas. In the spring 1974 ill health
forced him to retire. His wife Katherine (Maier) Wolf died April 19, 1976.
Their son Lloyd died Dec. 9, 1944.

William has made his home with his daughter Frances and husband Leonard
Joachim in Bowdle since Nov. 10, 1978.

ERVIN and LORETTA [MILLER] WOLFF

Ervin Elmer Wolff was born Dec. 1, 1927 in Cleveland, ND. His parents are
John Wolff, who was born Oct. 15, 1901 in rural Gackle, ND and Rose Wolff,
born April 5, 1905 in rural Streeter, ND. Elmer received an eighth grade
education.

He married Loretta LaVerna Miller June 21, 1951 in Bowdle. She was the
daughter of Jacob and Clara Miller. Jacob was born Dec. 3, 1888 in
Hoffnungstal, South Russia and died June 9, 1967. Clara was born Aug. 29,
1900 in Tarutino, Bessarabia and died May 19, 1934.

Ervin and Loretta were married at St. John's Evangelical Lutheran Church in
Bowdle. At the time he was serving in the U.S. Army. After his discharge
they moved to his father's farm near Cleveland, ND. Loretta was born Sept.
20, 1938 in Isabel. She received a high school education and attended one
year of college.

        Back: Linda, Errol, Ervin Front: Ervin Jr., Loretta, Elon

The couple has four children. Ervin Elmer was born April 1, 1952 in
Harwood, ND and is a fireman. Errol Eugene was born Nov. 13, 1953 and farms
near Cleveland, ND. Linda LuWayne was born Dec. 30, 1961 and is a secretary
to the Secretary of State of North Dakota. Elon Ethan is a junior in high
school.

CHRISTIAN WOLFF FAMILY

Christian Wolff was born Aug. 11, 1850 and his wife Magdalena Frey was born
Jan. 27, 1854. They were married in the 1870's and came to South Dakota in
1888 with their four children who were born in Marionsburg, Russia.
Christian was born Oct. 21, 1873, Johnathan Oct. 29, 1874, Matthew Feb. 24,
1876 (who married Lydia Weisser in June 1906 and lived in Spokane, WA) and
Elizabeth Aug. 5, 1878, who married William Bonen and died Feb. 23, 1974 at
Valley City, ND.

Phillip joined the family circle April 21, 1889 at Eureka. He chose as his
life's companion Mary Magdalena Bertsch Oct. 19, 1910.

Friederika was born Jan. 29, 1891 and married Gottlieb Banik. She died at
Aberdeen in 1974.

Edward was born Nov. 17, 1892 at Bowdle. He married Louise Seidel Feb. 8,
1913 and made their home at Bison.

The youngest child Jacob was born May 24, 1893 at Hoven. He married
Kathleen Stotz Oct. 12, 1919 and died at Watertown April 14, 1971.

Christian Wolff farmed in the Swan Creek area, north of Bowdle and in the
Tolstoy area. He told his grandchildren of being robbed by gypsies who
managed to take the money out of his pocket without his being aware of it.

PHILLIP WOLFF FAMILY

Phillip Wolff was born Aug. 21, 1889 at Eureka, the fifth child of
Christian and Magdalena (Frey) Wolff. He married Mary Magdalena Bertsch,
also born at Eureka March 5, 1890. The nuptials took place Oct. 18, 1910.
Their first child Ella Magdalena arrived Aug. 6, 1912 at Bowdle. Her
marriage to John Buckenberger took place in 1936 and they made their home
in Java where he died in 1965.

In 1914 Phillip took his family to McIntosh where the following children
were born. Edgar Ernest (10-30-14) married Esther Schnabel June 19, 1939
and lives at Paul, ID. Eugene Phillip (10-9-16) married Irma Endriza April
15, 1950 and lives at Rupert, ID. Esther Caroline (9-5-18) married George
Zimmerman Feb. 17, 1946, lives at Rupert. Lenora Ruth (9-24-20) married
Edwin Whitworth Dec. 31, 1937, lives at Rupert. A son Ruben died in
infancy. Martha Margaret (2-7-26) married James Grace Nov. 3, 1943, lives
at Rupert and after his death she married Elmer Attlesay. Elmer Jacob Wolff
(8-26-29) married Lucille Ambrose Aug. 28, 1954 and they also reside at
Rupert, ID.

From 1914 to 1929 Phillip and his family lived near McIntosh. He worked for
the Milwaukee Railroad in the roundhouse while his wife Mary and children
homesteaded land 13 miles from town.

The need of his parents for care in their old age brought the Phillip Wolff
family back to the Tolstoy area in 1929 where Phillip farmed and his wife
sold milk to the townspeople. In 1933 they moved to Bowdle where Phillip
farmed the Edwards land until October 1936 when he took his family to
Rupert, ID where they operated a truck garden and fruit orchard for the
remainder of their lives. Phillip died Aug. 10, 1949 and Mary died Oct. 16,
1961.

Called by the Grim Reaper . . .

Compiled by Connie Goetz

H.C. MAAS
Came to Bowdle in 1890 to work for Dr. Edwards in his drug store as a
pharmacist. When the building burned in 1900 he rebuilt on the same site.
Married Minnie Hoelworth. Had three children. In 1925 sold the business to
M.J. Jones. Went to California. Died Dec. 6, 1935.

H.A. MASON [Hiram Adelbert Mason]
Born at Pulaski, NY Feb. 6, 1851. Lived on a farm near Chicago, IL. Age 16
went to Baraboo, WI and learned the trade of tinsmith. Went into hardware
and implement business with his brother Dan F. Mason in Minnesota. Married
Sarah J. Darkneel. Had one son Burt. In early 1880's moved to Pierre; later
moved to Scranton. In 1887 moved to Bowdle engaging in the hardware and dry
goods business. Sarah died Jan. 29, 1891. Remarried Louisa M. Warren.
Member of Masons. Held many offices in Bowdle community and county. Died
May 13, 1921. Lies in Bowdle Cemetery.

WILLIAM L. BOYD
Born Sept. 23, 1851 in Belfast, Ireland. Came to U.S.A. at age 21. Was a
stone mason. Married Margaret Meehan. In 1889 moved to Bowdle. Had two
daughters who died at an early age. Became a farmer. Then in 1898 moved to
Bowdle and engaged in stone masonry. Later set up a grain buying business
in an elevator located where Bowdle Creamery now stands in 1985. Built Boyd
Hall which later became H & H Theatre. Was charter member of Bowdle Masonic
Lodge. Died June 12, 1935.

JOHN KOCH
Born Dec. 26, 1861 in Beek, Holland. In 1883 at age 22 came to Dakota
Territory. Married Sadie Hall Christmas Day 1890. In 1896 elected Sheriff of
Walworth County, in 1906 Deputy U.S. Marshall. Later engaged in flour mill
business until 1931. Was State Senator of this District 1920-1922. Died
April 13, 1938.

C.T. SMITHERS [Cale]
Was one of the pioneers of this country coming with his parents, brothers
and sisters directly from England in 1884. Came by train as far as Ipswich.
Purchased a yoke of oxen and came to Bowdle. Married Laura Hoffman.
Operated Bowdle Pioneer for many years, selling it later to Fred Zimmers.
Moved to Aberdeen to go into moving picture business. Later moved to
California and became a picture salesman at Hollywood. Died in California.

ARTHUR BICKERT
Born July 27, 1879 at Nebraska. At age 3, came with his parents to Bowdle.
Married Nora Auby. Children were Kathleen and Gordon. Was a businessman in
Bowdle many years. President of the bank. Was killed accidentally Oct. 27,
1926.

WILLIAM C. DICKHAUT
Born Sept. 16, 1899. Went to school in North Dakota. Started his career
with a bank at Bowdle. Later a credit manager for International Harvester
Co. at Bowdle. During 1930's was bank examiner in this area. Died in
California April 10, 1958.

JOHN LOEBS
Took active part in Bowdle's affairs. More than 35 years an employee at
Gross Bros. Store. Served on City Council 27 years from 1920-1947. Worked
under nine mayors of Bowdle.

GERALD HILBERS
Born at Stanton, NE April 8, 1920. Served in U.S. Army. Received many honor
medals including Purple Heart. Wounded, returned to U.S. and came to
Bowdle. Worked as a mechanic and was Chief of Police. Employed at Reuer
Garage until his death Jan. 27, 1974.

TILLIE SCHNAIBLE
Born Nov. 13, 1907 at rural Bowdle to Mr. and Mrs. John Schnaible. Attended
Bowdle Public Schools. Remembered for her smile serving Nels Waltman,
Bowdle Hospital and Nursing Home for about 30 years. Died at age 75 Oct.
29, 1983.

ROBERT HAM
Born April 30, 1876 in Minnesota. Moved to Bowdle in early 1880's with his
parents. Later homesteaded near Bowdle. Married Mary F. Schaick. Had 15
children. Farmed near Bowdle. Retired in 1950 to Aberdeen. Moved to Lemmon
in 1958. Died Oct. 8, 1976 at the age of 100 years, 5 months and 8 days.

ALEX SEARLE
An attorney. President of Security State Bank, owned several farms in this
county. Married Mary Edwards, daughter of Dr. Wm. Edwards. She died Feb.
11, 1985 at Oklahoma City, OK and was buried in Bowdle Cemetery. Alex died
Nov. 22, 1955.

HARLEY C. CHAFFEE
Born July 22, 1876 at West Point, WI. Married Emily Van Zyle. For 29 years
was the photographer in Bowdle. Contributed much time to Boy Scouts.

OMUND LARSEN
Born Sept. 4, 1860 in Stravanna, Norway. Came to Bowdle with his wife in
1886, homesteading on same section of land where Pete Murray home is now
located. Opened a jewelry store in location later occupied by Security
State Bank. The fire of 1900 destroyed the store. Continued to operate the
jewelry business in Maas Drug Store. In 1906 erected a new building west of
Mason Store, now the dental office.

CHARLES E. LENNAN
Was engaged in the real estate business in Bowdle in the early 1880's.
Native of Maine. Died Feb. 8, 1925. He was cremated.

JACOB K. MOSER
Born Dec. 1, 1884 at Kleindorf, South Russia. Came to the U.S. at age 9.
Homesteaded southwest of Bowdle. Later moved to Washington and North
Dakota, but came back to Bowdle. Married Christina Baer. Purchased Bowdle
Hardware Store and operated it until retirement. Was Mayor of Bowdle. Died
Nov. 22, 1968.

WILBUR F. DAVIS
Born Oct. 25, 1835. At age 22 came west to seek his fortune. In spring of
1857 arrived at the village of Fillmore, riding horseback from Iowa through
deep snow. Was in Civil War. Married Cordelia Pettis. Worked as a
brickmaker. In 1889 moved to Bowdle. Died at age 92.

L.E. AMERPOHL
Came to Bowdle from Brodhead, WI with G.C. Aurand June 12, 1886. Was one of
the first merchants in Bowdle. Put up first sign posts in Bowdle to help
homesteaders find their way to Bowdle to trade. Died July 12, 1943 at
Janesville, WI.

SAMUEL A. BOYD
Born in Ireland April 29, 1859. Married Mary Chester. Came to Bowdle in
1885. Settled on a farm southwest of Bowdle. In 1887 built their farmhouse
of lumber. Played the violin for neighborhood dances. Lived on the farm 22
years. In 1886, with his friend Mr. Baker, laid the foundation for the
Congregational Church. Died July 8, 1925.

ARNOLD ARTZ
Born in Holland Nov. 24, 1872. Married Gertrude Karst. Together worked with
the photography business at Bowdle. The studio burned, so in 1913 they
moved to Aberdeen and continued to operate the photography business.

B.A. OESTREICH [Bernard]
Born April 6, 1868 near Watertown, WI. Received his education in Wisconsin.
In 1907 came to Bowdle and made his home for 18 years. Made the creamery
and produce business in Bowdle a great success. Became associated with
several banks in the central part of the state. In 1925 moved to Lemmon to
establish a cream and produce business and operated a general store and
meat market. At one time was known as the largest shipper of eggs in the
Middle West. Acquired a number of farms. Built a housing project in eastern
part of Lemmon. Was original stockholder and director of Bank of Lemmon.
Died Nov. 30, 1947 from a stroke in Milwaukee, WI.

WILLIS E. RING
Born Feb. 7, 1869 in Merton, MN. Married Nora McClellan. Moved to Bowdle in
1902. Worked in Bowdle Flour Mill and later was in charge of the Electric
Light Plant. In 1915 was Marshall of Bowdle and held that title until May
1, 1944. Died Feb. 25, 1950 at age 81.

JAKE RING
Helped build and operate Bowdle Flour Mill. Was in partnership in the mill
for a time with his brother Willis. Later lived at Minot, ND operating a
shoe repair and harness shop. Died at age 92 in December 1956.

GEORGE SAUTNER
Lived in Bowdle 45 years. Born Feb. 10, 1866 in Carmen, South Russia, son
of Anton and Katherine Sautner. Was German descent, but received education
at Zaradoff, Russia where he attended high school and a seminary. Served
six months in Russian Cavalry. Married Frances Marthaller. Worked on farms
until 1895 in Bowdle and then became a carpenter. In 1925 became janitor at
Bowdle School for 10 years. Died Jan. 4, 1940.

DR. A.G. NICKISCH
Born in Germany, came to U.S. in March 1882. Married Anna. Came to Marion
where Dr. Nickisch practiced as a country doctor. In 1898 purchased land
and farmstead from Dr. Wm. Edwards 3/4 of a mile northwest of Bowdle.
Participated in the division of the Territory, creating the statehood of
South Dakota Nov. 2, 1889. Influential in changing location of state
capital from Huron to Pierre. Promoter of Yellowstone Trail.

THOMAS O'MALLEY
An old, well-known pioneer died Feb. 1, 1932 at age 84. Was a quiet man.
Offered little advice and attended strictly to his own business. Helped many
friends and neighbors when needed. All organizations received his support
and forgot no one. Born in Ireland in 1848. Came to Bowdle with his wife in
1886. Filed on a claim west of Bowdle for many years (present Clarence
Schumacher farm.) Owned a saloon in Bowdle for 28 years, known as Tom's
Place.

GEORGE STOUT
Born March 10, 1865 at Ashland County, Ohio. Came to Dakota at age 21.
Married Ella E. Miller Had nine children. Later married Katie Posz in 1915.
Was on School Board and was Justice of the Peace. Died Nov. 8, 1940.

F.P. MERKEL [Frederick Phillip]
Born in Bergdorf, South Russia Feb. 9, 1867. Emigrated to America in 1884.
Came to Bowdle in 1889. Married Rosina Buechler January 1893. She died Nov.
10, 1894, leaving him a son Phillip. In 1896 Frederick married Josephina
Blumhardt. He died April 7, 1915 at Cherokee, Iowa at age 48.

E.J. EDWARDS [Even]
Born March 9, 1847 at Wabasha, WI. In 1883 came to South Dakota with his
brother Dr. Wm. Edwards. Settled at Theodore. In 1896, while driving from
Bangor to Bowdle, Mrs. Edwards fell off the buggy and was killed by the
runaway team. In 1898 Mr. Edwards was appointed postmaster at Bowdle and
held that post 14 years. In 1901 married Mrs. Bingham. Died April 14, 1915.

JACOB GUNDERT
Born near Odessa, Russia Jan. 18, 1853. Married Miss Maag. Moved to Hosmer
to start a lumber yard and established the 1st State Bank. Moved to Bowdle
and established 1st State Bank and then to Tolstoy to organize a bank.
Father of 10 children. Died at Tolstoy Oct. 26, 1918 at age 65. Buried at
Bowdle.

JOHN MEAKINS
Born June 17, 1856 in Buffalo, NY. Orphaned by death of his mother, he and
his sister were placed in an orphanage. At age 12 was bound out in
servitude to a farmer for room and board. Cruel treatment forced him to run
away at age 16. A kindly train conductor took him 50 miles away. Worked his
way west driving mules on the Erie Canal, serving as a lighter of street
lamps in Chicago. Finally worked with threshing crews in Kansas and
Nebraska. Hauled mail for a hotel keeper in Nebraska. In 1883 came to
Aberdeen and worked as "handpower" for the printing press for a newspaper.
Later with a partner Pierce and he acquired a team of oxen and set out for
the west. Took 6 weeks to find their "promised land" on Swan Lake Lived
there until rumor was heard the Milwaukee Railroad was coming to Bowdle.
Sold his land and bought land two miles west of Bowdle, which was home for
many years until unable to walk to town. Again sold the land and purchased
land adjoining the town. Credited for growing the first corn in this area.
Presented the city land for the athletic field and site of Meakins Park.
Last 10 years his nephew Carl W. Burt cared for him. He died Dec. 6, 1951 at
age 95.

FREDERICK HAM
Born March 28, 1862 at Roxbury, MA. Graduated from Harvard. Opened a law
office at Bowdle. Married Olive S. Finch. Was probate judge 8 years. Died
Feb. 6, 1918.

REV. WM. McCREADY
Born in Canada. Founder of Congregational Church in Bowdle. Married Lydia
Rowe who died after Civil War. In 1868 he married Maro Doane. At age 76 he
died in California.

CAPT. WM. O'NEILL
Born in Queens County, Ireland July 14, 1825. Obtained a Squatter's Right
on a farm 8 miles from Bowdle which was still possessed at the time of his
death in July 1919. Married Mary Craig. Had nine children. Twice elected to
State Legislature and once as County Judge.

MORRIS BAKER
Came to Bowdle with his wife in 1884 to homestead. In 1910 the family moved
to Bowdle. Their daughter Grace and Ruth Boyd were the first graduates from
the 4-year course at Bowdle High School. Mr. and Mrs. Baker died in 1942.

W.J. BICKERT
Born April 15, 1884 at Bowdle. One of Bowdle's first babies. Attended State
College at Brookings. Married Belle McCafferty. Died May 24, 1936 at age 52.

ROBERT deMALIGNON
Born Oct. 9, 1891 in Walworth County. Grew to manhood in Selby. Married
Emily Rossiter in 1916. In 1926 established an undertaking business at
Bowdle for 30 years. Member of many clubs, Masonic Lodge. Instrumental in
establishing the Bowdle Golf Club. Had one son Brooke and one daughter
Eileen. Died May 16, 1956. Buried in Riverside Cemetery at Aberdeen.

HENRY B. BAER
Born Sept. 28, 1876 in Crimea, Russia, son of Mr. and Mrs. Bernhardt Baer.
Came to Bowdle in 1901 to go into general merchandise and hardware
business. While a lad his oldest brother Christ left Russia to avoid
military service, coming to the U.S. The rest of the Baer families came in
1889. Henry attended Lutheran College in New Ulm, MN. Married Sophia. In
1901 bought Andy Gerup's Store in Bowdle. When that burned in 1906 Henry
and his brother Herman built the two-story cement block building known as
Bowdle Hardware and operated the business for many years.

HERMAN C. BAER
Born in Crimea, Russia in 1874. Came to the U.S. with his parents at age
10. First home in area known as Baer District southwest of Bowdle. Was in
the grain and implement business with Jake Gross. Married Anna Wagner. Had
four children: Elsie, Rev. A. H. Baer, Theodore and Wilmer. For years
operated the hardware business with his brother Henry B. In 1915 Herman and
Henry Bauder purchased the grain elevator at Gretna. In 1945 sold the
business to Joseph Stappler. Later moved to Seattle. In 1959 moved to
Michigan to live with their son. Died May 14, 1964.

EBIN STROUP
Born Dec. 26, 1861 in Wisconsin. Came to Bowdle in 1884. Married Lena Jole.
Had eight children. Worked as a mail messenger at the local post office
when he died July 15, 1929. "Eb" was a true pioneer. Watched the building
of the Milwaukee Railroad into Bowdle and later in 1900 saw the road extend
west from Bowdle to Puget Sound.

DR. WM. EDWARDS
"Greater love no man hath than that he gives his life for a friend." From
1883 to November 1919 he cared for the sick. Two generations were helped
into this world by him. As a business man he contributed much to the
development of the town. As a neighbor, was kind and agreeable. Died Feb.
8, 1920 of cancer. Born on a farm near Madison, WI Feb. 16, 1850. Attended
Madison University. Received a medical degree from Northwestern and Keokuk
Medical Colleges. Began his medical practice in 1877 at Taopi, MN where he
married Ida L. Wells. From Minnesota came to Dakota. Established a practice
at Madison. Fame as a good surgeon. In 1882 the family settled at Theodore
until 1885 when they moved to Bowdle. Made many sick calls, sometimes as
far as 80 miles away. In 1892 was elected State Senator from this district.
Member of State Board of Health. President of the Councilors of the State
Medical Society. First Mayor of Bowdle. Established first drug store in
Bowdle. Member of Masons. Funeral was at Opera House, no church large
enough to accommodate all his friends. Rev. Brakemeyer officiated. Had a son
Frank and a daughter Mary.

GEORGE BAUMGARTEN
Born in Wisconsin July 15, 1858. Came to Walworth County in 1884. Filed a
homestead a few miles southwest of Bowdle. Married Emily Hoffman. Was a
County Auditor 1888-1924.
